chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “She seems exhausted to me,” remarked Obed, breaking his silence since coming back from the barn. “You ought to put her to bed, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Thirza had pondered which bed Nell ought to occupy. For the hoped-for and anticipated male child, she had made up a sofa located in the kitchen room. Yet, despite its tidy and spotless state, placing a female child there felt somehow inappropriate. On the other hand, offering the guest bedroom to a mere homeless orphan was completely impossible, leaving the room in the east gable as the sole option. Thirza set fire to a candle wick and instructed Nell to come after her, a command Nell obeyed without energy, picking up her head covering and luggage off the hall table along the way. That hallway possessed a daunting cleanliness; the small gable bedroom where she soon ended up appeared even more immaculate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Thirza placed the light upon a triangular table with three legs and folded back the bedding.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “I take it you own a nightgown?” she asked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Nell gave a nod.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Indeed, I possess two. They were crafted for me by the matron at the asylum. They are terribly scant. Because an asylum never has sufficient supplies to distribute, items are invariably scant—or at least that is the case in an impoverished asylum such as ours. Scant night-dresses are something I despise. Nevertheless, it is possible to dream equally well inside them as inside beautiful sweeping ones that feature neck frills, which serves as a single comfort.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Now, strip off your clothes as fast as possible and get into bed. In a little while, I’ll return to fetch the candle. Leaving you to extinguish it on your own is too risky. It’s probable you’d burn down the house.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: After Thirza departed, Nell gazed about herself mournfully. So agonizingly plain and bright were the whitewashed walls that she believed they had to hurt from their own plainness. Likewise, the floor was uncarpeted, save for a central circular braided mat unlike any Nell had previously encountered. The bed, an elevated, antique model featuring four dark, shortly turned posts, occupied one corner. The previously mentioned triangular table was situated in the opposite corner, decorated by a chubby, red velvet pincushion sufficiently firm to bend the tip of even the boldest pin. A small six-by-eight mirror was suspended above it. Located halfway between the table and the bed was the window, covered by a frozen white muslin frill, while the wash-stand sat across from it. The entire room possessed an indescribable stiffness that chilled Nell to the deep center of her bones. Weeping, she rapidly removed her clothes, donned the tight nightgown, and leaped into bed, where she dug face down into the pillow and dragged the covers above her head. When Thirza returned upstairs to fetch the light, several meager pieces of clothing strewn very carelessly across the floor and a particular chaotic look to the bed served as the sole signs that anyone besides herself was there.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: She intentionally gathered the garments belonging to Nell, laid them orderly upon a stiff yellow chair, and afterwards, carrying the candle, walked across to the bed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Good night,” she spoke, somewhat stiffly, yet with a degree of warmth.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: With a suddenness that was startling, Nell’s pale face and large eyes emerged above the bedding.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “In what way is it possible for you to term the night good, given your awareness that it has to be the most terrible one I have ever experienced?” she asked in a tone of reproach.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Afterward, she descended below sight once more.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Thirza walked leisurely down toward the kitchen, where she began cleaning the dishes from supper. Obed was engaged in smoking, which served as a clear indication that his mind was troubled. He rarely used tobacco, since Thirza firmly opposed it on the grounds that it was a disgusting practice; however, on particular occasions and in certain circumstances, he felt compelled to do so, and Thirza would deliberately ignore the behavior during those moments, recognizing that an ordinary man requires some outlet to release his feelings.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Well, this is a fine mess,” she declared angrily. “That is the result of dispatching a message rather than traveling there in person. The family of Richard Tranter has altered that news in some manner. It is definite that a person among us must travel by carriage to visit Mrs. Tranter the following day. This child must be returned to the orphanage.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Yes, I guess that is right,” Obed admitted with hesitation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “You believe that is the case! Is it not a certainty to you?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Indeed, Thirza is quite a lovely young girl. Since she is so eager to remain with us, returning her seems rather unfortunate.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Obed Abernethy, surely you are not suggesting that we should retain her!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Thirza could not have been more astonished if Obed had declared a preference for standing on his head.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “I don't imagine we do—at least, not entirely,” Obed faltered, trapped uneasily while attempting to clarify his exact intention. “It seems to me—it would scarcely be reasonable for us to retain her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “I would think not. Of what use could she possibly be to us?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “We could perhaps render her some assistance,” Obed remarked abruptly and out of the blue.

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Obed Abernethy, my belief is that you have been enchanted by that child! It is as clear as day to me that your desire is to retain her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Well now, she is a truly fascinating young lady,” Obed continued. “If only you had listened to her speaking on the way from the station.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Oh, her tongue moves quickly enough. That was immediately obvious to me. Furthermore, it counts against her. Children with so much to say are not to my liking. An orphan girl is not what I want, and even if she were, I would not choose her type. About her, there is something I fail to comprehend. No, she must be sent back without delay to the place she originated from.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “A French boy could be hired by me for assistance,” Obed said, “and you would have her for company.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Company is not something I am lacking,” Thirza replied abruptly. “Furthermore, keeping her is not my intention.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: “Indeed, Thirza, things are precisely as you describe,” Obed remarked while standing up and stowing his pipe. “I am retiring for the night.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised
text: Obed retired to bed. Thirza likewise retired to bed, a look of utmost determination on her face, after storing her dishes. Meanwhile, on an upper floor within the east gable, a little girl who was solitary, starving for affection, and devoid of friends wept until sleep took her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: WHEN Nell opened her eyes and sat up in bed, it was broad daylight, and she gazed bewilderedly toward the window, where a torrent of bright sunlight streamed in, while beyond it a pale, feathery object fluttered against patches of blue sky.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Briefly, she was unable to recall her surroundings. An enjoyable sensation occurred initially, like something exceedingly nice; subsequently, a dreadful memory returned. She was at Grey Shutters, where her presence was undesired simply because she failed to be a boy!

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: However, morning had arrived, and indeed, a cherry-tree covered in blossoms stood right past her window. Leaping from her bed, she hurried over the floor. She shoved the sash upward—it moved with a stiff, creaking resistance, appearing as though it had not been raised in ages, which was true; moreover, it jammed so firmly that no support was required to keep it elevated.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Nell fell to her knees and stared out at the June morning, her eyes shining with joy. Oh, was it not beautiful? Was it not a wonderful location? What if she was not actually going to remain here! She would pretend she was. There was room for imagination in this place.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: An enormous cherry-tree stood outdoors, positioned so near that its branches struck the building, and it was so densely covered in blooms that almost no leaves could be observed. Adjacent to the house on either side lay a large orchard, comprising apple-trees on one side and cherry-trees on the other, which were likewise covered in a shower of blossoms; moreover, dandelions were scattered throughout their grass. Within the garden underneath stood lilac-trees heavy with purple blooms, and the morning breeze carried their intoxicatingly sweet scent up toward the window.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: A verdant meadow thick with clover inclined downward beneath the garden toward the basin that contained the flowing brook and dozens of pale birches, which rose lightly from a carpet of bushes hinting at wonderful prospects of ferns, moss, and broad forest flora. Past that lay a ridge, verdant and soft with spruce and fir trees; an opening cut through it, revealing the gray gable end of the small dwelling she had noticed from the opposite bank of the Lake of Glassy Waters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: To the left stood the large barns, and past them, further down across low-sloping green fields, the blue sea could be seen sparkling.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: The beauty-loving eyes of Nell lingered upon the entire scene, absorbing each detail with greed. So many unlovely places had been beheld by her in her life, poor child; nevertheless, this was as lovely as any place she had ever dreamed of.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: She remained on her knees, unaware of anything except the beauty surrounding her, before a hand upon her shoulder frightened her. Unnoticed by the little dreamer, Thirza had entered.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “You ought to be dressed by now,” she stated in a abrupt manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Thirza truly lacked the knowledge of how to converse with the little girl, and this awkward lack of understanding caused her to be sharp and abrupt when that was not her intention.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Rising to her feet, Nell took a deep breath.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Oh, isn’t it wonderful?” she said, making a broad gesture with her hand toward the pleasant world beyond.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “The tree is large,” Thirza stated, “and its blossoms are grand, but its yield is never worth anything—it is tiny and full of worms.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Oh, I am not referring solely to the tree; naturally it is beautiful—yes, it is dazzlingly beautiful—it flowers as though it really intended to—however I was referring to all of it, the garden along with the orchard, the stream, and the forest, the entire immense beloved world. Do you not feel a deep affection for the world on a morning such as this? Furthermore, I am able to hear the stream laughing all the way to this spot. Did you ever observe how joyful streams are? They laugh constantly. I have even heard them beneath the ice during the winter. I am exceedingly pleased that a stream is located close to Grey Shutters. You might suppose it matters nothing to me since you do not plan to keep me, yet it does matter. It will always bring me pleasure to recall that a stream exists at Grey Shutters, even should I fail to behold it ever again. Were there no stream, I would be plagued by the uneasy sensation that one should exist. I am not plunged into deep despair this morning. Morning never allows me to be. Is it not a marvelous reality that mornings exist? Nevertheless, I feel extremely mournful. I was merely picturing that I was actually the person you desired after all and that my stay here would endure for ever and ever. That provided immense solace while it endured. Yet the most painful aspect of picturing things is the arrival of the moment when stopping becomes necessary, and that causes pain.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “It would be best for you to put on your clothes and descend the stairs, ignoring your fancies,” Thirza remarked the moment she found an opportunity to speak. “The morning meal is ready. Clean your face and brush your hair. Keep the window raised and fold your bedding over the bed’s end. Hurry as much as possible.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: It was clear that Nell was capable of being prompt when necessary, as she appeared on the lower floor within ten minutes, wearing neatly arranged garments, with her hair combed and plaited, her face cleansed, and her mind filled with a satisfying sense that she had satisfied every one of Thirza’s demands. Actually, though, turning down her bedding was something she had neglected to do.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “This morning, I have quite an appetite,” she declared while sliding onto the seat that Thirza held out for her. “Last night, the world felt like a howling wilderness, but it doesn’t seem that way anymore. It makes me happy that the sun is shining this morning. Even so, rainy mornings are also very much to my liking. Every kind of morning holds interest, wouldn’t you agree? What the day will bring remains unknown, leaving vast room for imagination. Still, I am pleased about the lack of rain today, since maintaining cheerfulness and enduring suffering comes more easily under a sunny sky. I sense that I have quite a lot to endure. Reading about griefs and picturing yourself facing them with courage is fine and good, yet experiencing them in reality is not nearly as pleasant, is it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “In the name of mercy, keep quiet,” Thirza said. “For a young girl, your speech is altogether excessive.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: At that point Nell became quiet so dutifully and completely that her ongoing lack of speech rendered Thirza somewhat uneasy, as though she were in the company of a thing that was not quite normal. Obed likewise remained silent,—though this was customary,—with the result that the dinner proved to be extremely quiet.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: As the meal went on, Nell grew increasingly preoccupied, consuming her food automatically while her large eyes remained constantly glued to the firmament beyond the glass, seeing nothing. Thirza grew increasingly anxious because of this; a distressing sensation came over her that although the strange youngster's physical form was present at the board, her soul had traveled off to a distant, lofty cloud realm, carried high by imaginative wings. Who could desire a youngster like that in the house?

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Still, among all unthinkable desires, Obed desired to retain her! Thirza sensed his longing for it was no less strong this morning than it had been on the previous evening, and that his desire would persist. Such was Obed's manner—to adopt a caprice and adhere to it with an astonishingly quiet stubbornness—a stubbornness whose very quietness rendered it tenfold more powerful and successful than if he had given it voice.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Once she had finished eating, Nell emerged from her deep thought and volunteered to do the washing up.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Are you able to clean plates properly?” inquired Thirza with suspicion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Fairly well. However, I am superior at caring for young ones. I possess a great deal of practice in doing so. It is a terrible shame that you do not have any in this place for me to care for.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “I do not think that I desire any additional youngsters to care for beyond those currently in my charge. In all honesty, you present a sufficient challenge. I am at a loss as to what should be done regarding you. Obed is an utterly absurd person.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “I consider him wonderful,” Nell remarked with disapproval. “He displays such great empathy. The extent of my speaking didn't bother him—it appeared to please him. The very moment I laid eyes on him, I sensed that our souls were aligned.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “If being kindred spirits implies being peculiar, the two of you certainly fit the description,” Thirza declared, sniffing. “Indeed, the dishwashing is permitted. Utilize an abundance of heated water, and ensure they are thoroughly wiped dry. My schedule is full today because I must journey to Pale Sands later today to meet Mrs. Tranter. Your presence will be required beside me so we can determine your future arrangements. Upon completing the kitchen work, proceed to the upper level to tidy your bedding.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Thirza observed the process with a vigilant gaze and recognized that Nell cleaned the plates with sufficient skill. Subsequently, the girl was not as adept at making her bed, since the skill of dealing with a feather mattress had never been taught to her. Nevertheless, the task was eventually accomplished and flattened out; whereupon Thirza, wishing to be free of her presence, informed her that she could venture outside and entertain herself until it was time for dinner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Nell rushed toward the door, her face radiant and her eyes shining. Right at the threshold she halted abruptly, turned completely around, returned and took a seat beside the table, her radiance and shine extinguished as thoroughly as though a person had placed a snuffer over her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “What is wrong this time?” Thirza asked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “I don’t dare go out,” Nell stated, sounding like a martyr giving up every joy on earth. “Unless I am permitted to remain in this place, loving Grey Shutters is pointless. Furthermore, should I venture outside and become familiar with every one of those trees and blossoms, as well as the orchard and the stream, I will inevitably fall in love with it all. The situation is difficult enough already, so I refuse to increase the difficulty. I have a strong desire to venture outside—all things appear to be shouting to me, ‘Nell, Nell, come out to us. Nell, Nell, we want a playmate’—yet abstaining is the wiser choice. Loving anything is useless if one must be ripped away from it, wouldn't you say? Besides, preventing oneself from loving things is terribly difficult, isn't it? For that reason, I felt such joy upon believing I would reside in this home. I assumed I would possess numerous objects to love without any obstacles stopping me. However, that fleeting fantasy has ended. Now that I have accepted my destiny, I believe I will avoid going outside lest I become unresigned once more. Could you tell me the name of the geranium sitting on the window-sill?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “The apple-scented geranium is what that is.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Oh, that isn't the kind of name I am referring to. I am asking about a name you invented for it on your own. Hasn't a name been provided by you? Is it permissible for me to bestow a name upon it, in that case? Might I refer to it as—let me think—Bonny could work—could I speak of it as Bonny for the duration of my stay? Oh, please allow me to!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Gracious, it doesn't matter to me. Still, why in the world would anyone bother giving a name to a geranium?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Oh, even when they are just geraniums, I prefer items to possess names. They appear more like individuals that way. How can you be sure a geranium’s feelings aren't wounded merely by being referred to as a geranium and nothing more? It wouldn't suit you to be addressed as merely a woman constantly. Yes, Bonny will be its name. This morning, I gave a name to that cherry-tree beyond my bedroom window. Frost Maiden was what I called it owing to its extreme whiteness. To be sure, its blossoms will not last forever, but it is possible to pretend they do, isn't it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Never in my whole life have I seen or heard anything that equals her,” Thirza muttered, retreating down into the cellar to fetch potatoes. “Obed is right that she is sort of interesting. Already I can feel myself wondering what in the world her next words will be. It won't be long before she casts a spell over me as well. Obed is already under it. That glance he threw my way on his way out repeated every single thing he stated or suggested yesterday evening. I wish he possessed the traits of normal men and would discuss matters fully. Then a person could reply and use logic to persuade him. However, how can anyone handle a man who merely stares?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: When Thirza came back from her journey to the cellar, Nell, who had her chin resting in her hands and her gaze fixed on the sky, had fallen back into a dream. Thirza then departed from her side until the early dinner was served on the table.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Obed, am I able to take the mare and buggy later today?” asked Thirza.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Nodding his head, Obed cast a longing glance toward Nell, which Thirza cut across before speaking sternly:

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “I am heading over to Pale Sands to get this matter sorted out. Nell will accompany me, and it is likely that Mrs. Tranter will arrange her immediate return to Nova Scotia. After I prepare your tea and leave it out for you, I will return in time for the cow milking.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Obed remained silent, which made Thirza feel as though her words and breath had been spent in vain. A man who refuses to respond is the ultimate source of annoyance—with the sole exception of a woman who behaves the same way.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: In good time, Obed tackled the sorrel to the buggy, whereupon Thirza and Nell departed. Obed unlatched the yard gate for their exit, and while they navigated it at a walk, he remarked, apparently to no one specifically:

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: “Young Tobias Buote from the Creek came by earlier today, and I informed him that I thought I would take him on for the summer season.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
text: Thirza remained silent, yet she struck the unfortunate sorrel with the whip so fiercely that the chubby mare, unaccustomed to such handling, dashed furiously down the lane at a terrifying speed. As the buggy jolted forward, Thirza glanced behind her a single time and observed that irritating Obed bent over the gate, gazing mournfully in their direction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “DO you know,” Nell remarked in confidence, “I have decided that I will enjoy this drive. Experience has taught me that if a person firmly resolves to enjoy things, they almost always can. Naturally, one has to resolve it firmly. While this drive is happening, I intend not to dwell on returning to the asylum. My thoughts will be focused solely on the drive. Oh, see, a single early wild rose has bloomed over there! Is it not beautiful? Wouldn't you agree that it must be happy being a rose? Wouldn't it be wonderful if roses were able to speak? I am certain of their ability to share such wonderful things with us. And isn't pink the absolute most charming hue anywhere? I adore it, yet it doesn't suit me. Pink cannot be worn by individuals with red hair, even inside their imagination. Have you ever heard of someone who had red hair during childhood, but whose hair turned into a different shade upon reaching adulthood?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “No, I cannot say that I ever have,” Thirza remarked without pity, “and I doubt that such a thing will occur for you either.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: A sigh escaped Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Well, another expectation has been shattered. ‘My life is a perfect graveyard of buried hopes.’ Having come across that line in a book one time, I repeat it to console myself each time I face disappointment about something.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “I fail to perceive the comfort in it myself,” Thirza remarked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Well, it is due to how lovely and romantic it sounds, precisely as though I were a book's heroine, don't you see. Romantic things appeal to me deeply, and what could be more romantic than a graveyard packed with interred hopes, don't you think? Having one actually pleases me quite a bit. Will our journey take us over the Lake of Glassy Waters today?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “If your Lake of Glassy Waters refers to Pembroke’s pond, that is not our route. Our path lies along the shore road.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “The shore road sounds lovely,” Nell remarked in a dreamy voice. “Does its beauty match its name? The moment you mentioned ‘shore road’, a mental image of it appeared to me, just like that! Pale Sands is also a charming name; however, I do not prefer it to Brierley. Brierley is a beautiful name that resembles music when heard. What is the distance to Pale Sands?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “The distance is five miles; since you are clearly determined to converse, you may just as well speak to some end by informing me of what you know concerning your own history.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Oh, the things I know regarding myself are not actually worth mentioning,” Nell stated with enthusiasm. “Should you merely allow me to describe my self-imagined ideas, you will find it far more fascinating.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “No, I have no desire for any of your imaginings. You must merely adhere to plain facts. Start right at the start. Where did your birth take place and what is your age?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “I turned eleven this past March,” Nell stated, giving in to plain reality with a faint sigh. “And Nova Scotia’s Harborough is where I was born. Edmund Harcourt was my father’s name, and he worked as a teacher at the Harborough High School. Bertha Harcourt was my mother’s name. Don’t you think Edmund and Bertha are beautiful names? I feel so happy that my parents possessed pleasant names. Having a father who was named—oh, for instance Jedediah—would be an actual shame, wouldn’t it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “It likely is not important what an individual is called provided that he conducts himself properly,” Thirza stated, believing she was required to teach a helpful and virtuous lesson.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Well, I don’t know.” Nell seemed to be pondering. “A book I once read stated that a rose would smell just as sweet if it had a different name, but believing that has always been impossible for me. A rose would not be as lovely if it were named a thistle or a skunk cabbage, in my opinion. Even if my father had been named Jedediah, I imagine he could still have been a fine man; however, I am certain it would have proved a burden. Well, my mother was also a High School teacher, but naturally, she relinquished her teaching career upon marrying father. Managing a husband was a sufficient duty. They were a couple of infants and as poor as church mice, according to Mrs. Thomas. They moved into a tiny little yellow house located in Harborough. Although I have never set eyes on that house, it has been in my imagination thousands of times. It surely had honeysuckle climbing over the parlor window, lilacs growing in the front yard, and lilies of the valley right by the gate, I believe. Yes, and every window had muslin curtains. Muslin curtains bestow such a grand feel upon a house. My birth occurred in that very house. Mrs. Thomas remarked that I was the ugliest infant she had ever laid eyes on, being extremely thin, small, and composed of nothing but eyes, yet mother considered me utterly gorgeous. A mother ought to be a superior judge compared to a poor woman who arrived to perform scrubbing, wouldn't you agree? At any rate, I am pleased she felt contented with me; it would bring me great sorrow to think I disappointed her—since her life ended shortly after that, you understand. Fever took her life when my age was merely three months. I truly wish her life had lasted long enough for me to possess a memory of addressing her as mother. Saying ‘mother’ would be so lovely, don't you think? Then, four days later, fever caused father's death as well. Consequently, I became an orphan, and people were utterly baffled, as Mrs. Thomas recounted, regarding how to handle me. As you can tell, no one desired me even at that time. It appears to be my destiny. Places far off were the origins of both father and mother, and it was common knowledge that they possessed no living relatives. In the end, Mrs. Thomas announced she would accept me, despite her poverty and her intoxicated husband. I was brought up by hand by her. Is there any quality in being brought up by hand that should render individuals raised in that manner superior to others, do you happen to know? For every time I behaved badly, Mrs. Thomas would inquire, in a reproachful manner, how I could turn out to be such a wicked girl when she had brought me up by hand.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Mr. and Mrs. Thomas relocated from Harborough to Marysville, and I remained in their household until my eighth year. My duties included helping to care for the Thomas children—four of whom were my juniors—and they certainly required a great deal of attention, I assure you. Following Mr. Thomas’s fatal accident when he fell beneath a train, his mother proposed to harbor Mrs. Thomas and the young ones, though she refused to accept me. Mrs. Thomas expressed that she was utterly bewildered as to how to dispose of me. At that juncture, Mrs. Rudge traveled down from further up the river and offered to adopt me, owing to my skill with young ones, whereupon I journeyed upriver to reside with her in a modest clearing surrounded by stumps. The location was exceedingly desolate. Had I lacked an imagination, I am positive I could not have endured staying there. Mr. Rudge operated a small sawmill at that site, while Mrs. Rudge was the mother of eight children. On three separate occasions, she gave birth to twins. Although I am fond of infants in reasonable numbers, bearing twins thrice consecutively exceeds proper bounds. I stated this to Mrs. Rudge with conviction when the final set arrived. Lugging them around used to exhaust me so terribly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “For more than two years, I resided up river alongside Mrs. Rudge, but after Mr. Rudge passed away, Mrs. Rudge dissolved her household. Following the distribution of her children among her family members, she departed for the States. Since no one was willing to receive me, I was forced to enter the asylum located at Marden. Even the asylum did not desire my presence, claiming they were already experiencing overcrowding. Nevertheless, they were obligated to admit me, and I remained in that place for four months until the arrival of Mrs. Tranter.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: Nell concluded her remarks with a further sigh, which now expressed relief. Clearly, discussing her encounters within a world where she had been unwelcome was not to her liking.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Was school ever somewhere you went?” asked Thirza, steering the sorrel mare onto the coastal road.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Hardly anything. During my final year residing with Mrs. Thomas, I attended for a short time. After moving up river, the school was located at such a distance that winter walking was impossible, and summer brought vacation, leaving me able to attend solely throughout the spring and autumn months. Naturally, I attended during my stay at the asylum, though. Reading comes quite easily to me, and I have memorized a great number of poems—‘The Battle of Hohenlinden’ along with ‘Edinburgh after Flodden,’ as well as ‘Bingen on the Rhine,’ plus numerous selections from ‘Lady of the Lake’ and the majority of James Thompson’s ‘The Seasons.’ Are you not simply fond of poetry that causes a tingling sensation along your spine? A poem featured in the Fifth Reader—‘The Downfall of Poland’—is absolutely packed with excitement. Naturally, my placement was not in the Fifth Reader—I had only reached the Fourth—yet the older girls would allow me to borrow their copies for reading.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: Glancing sideways at Nell, Thirza inquired, “Were those women—Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Rudge—good to you?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “O-o-o-h,” Nell stammered. A deep red wash instantly covered her delicate small face, and her forehead displayed her discomfiture. “Oh, their intentions were—I am certain their intentions were to be as friendly and gentle as they could be. And if folks intend to treat you well, you are not overly bothered if they are not entirely—at all times. They had many troubles to upset them, as you are aware. Having a spouse who drinks is extremely difficult, as you can understand; and having three consecutive sets of twins must be terribly difficult, wouldn’t you agree? Even so, I am certain their intention was to treat me well.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: Thirza ceased her questioning. Nell surrendered to mute delight regarding the coastal route, and Thirza drove the sorrel in an absent-minded fashion as she thought intently. Compassion was abruptly awakening in her soul toward the young girl. What a deprived, loveless existence she had endured—an existence marked by hard labor, indigence, and disregard; because Thirza possessed sufficient acumen to discern what lay beneath the surface of Nell’s past and grasp the reality. It was no surprise that she had felt such joy when considering a true home. It was unfortunate that her return was necessary. What would happen if she, Thirza, were to humor Obed’s inexplicable desire and allow her to remain? He was determined about the matter; and the young girl appeared to be a pleasant, impressionable small person.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “She speaks far too much,” Thirza reflected, “though that habit could perhaps be corrected. Furthermore, her speech contains nothing vulgar or colloquial. Her manners are refined. Her family was probably respectable.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: The coastal route was “woodsy and wild and lonesome.” Dense scrub firs, whose vigor remained completely unbowed by decades of fighting the gulf gales, lined the right side. On the left stood the sheer red sandstone bluffs, which approached the path so closely at points that a horse with less calm than the sorrel could have unsettled the passengers she pulled. At the foot of the bluffs rested piles of wave-eroded stones or small sand inlets set with pebbles like sea gems; past them stretched the ocean, glinting and azure, while overhead flew the gulls, their wings gleaming like silver in the sun’s rays.

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Is the sea not marvelous?” asked Nell, breaking a lengthy, staring quietness. “A single time, back when Marysville was my home, Mr. Thomas rented a delivery wagon and escorted every one of us to pass the day by the coast ten miles distant. Every second of that day brought me delight, despite my having to care for the kids the entire time. For years afterward, I re-experienced it in joyful dreams. However, this coastline surpasses the Marysville coastline. Are those gulls not magnificent? Would being a gull appeal to you? I believe it would to me—meaning, provided I was unable to be a human girl. Do you not agree that waking at dawn, swooping down toward the waves, and traveling far across that beautiful blue all day would be wonderful; and subsequently returning to one’s nest at night? Oh, I am able to picture myself doing that very thing. What large dwelling is that directly before us, if you don’t mind?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “Over there is the Pale Sands Hotel. It is operated by Mr. Kirke, though the season is not under way yet. A great number of Americans arrive at that place for the summer. This coast is considered by them to be ideal.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER V. Nell’s History
text: “I feared it could be the home of Mrs. Tranter,” Nell stated sorrowfully. “Reaching that destination is something I wish to avoid. In a way, it will feel as though all things have come to a close.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: ARRIVE there they certainly managed to, nevertheless, when the time came. Mrs. Tranter resided within a large yellow dwelling located at Pale Sands Cove, and she approached the entrance with astonishment and hospitality combined upon her kindly countenance.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Dear, dear,” she cried out, “you happen to be the final people I anticipated seeing today, yet I am truly happy you are here. Will you stable your horse? And how have you been, Nell?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “With no smile, Nell replied, “Thank you, I am doing as fine as could be anticipated.” It appeared that a dark shadow had fallen over her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I guess we will remain a short time so the mare can rest,” Thirza said, “however, I gave Obed my word that I would return home at an early hour. Truthfully, Mrs. Tranter, an odd error has occurred somewhere, and my purpose in coming here is to locate it. We communicated, Obed and I, requesting that you deliver a boy from the asylum to us. We instructed your brother Robert to inform you that our desire was a boy aged ten or eleven.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Thirza Abernethy, it can’t be!” exclaimed a troubled Mrs. Tranter. “Listen, Robert dispatched a message through his girl Nancy, and didn't she mention that a girl was needed by you—wasn't that it, Flora Odette?” she asked, turning to her daughter who had stepped onto the porch.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Miss Abernethy, she most certainly did,” Flora Odette verified with great sincerity.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I am so very sorry,” Mrs. Tranter remarked. “This is most unfortunate; however, it was definitely not my doing, Miss Abernethy, as you must realize. Having done everything in my power, I believed that I was acting according to your directions. A more dreadfully light-headed girl than Nancy would be hard to find. On numerous occasions, her lack of thought has forced me to give her a thorough tongue-lashing.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “We have only ourselves to blame,” Thirza remarked with acceptance. “Rather than entrusting a critical communication to be relayed verbally like that, we ought to have visited you in person. Regardless, since the error occurred, our sole option at present is to correct it. Is it possible for us to return the youngster to the orphanage? They will accept her return, I assume, will they not?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I guess that’s true,” Mrs. Tranter remarked reflectively, “however, returning her shouldn't be required in my opinion. Yesterday, when Mrs. Peter Scobie came by, she mentioned how she regretted not asking me to bring back a young girl to assist her. As you are aware, Mrs. Peter has many children, making assistance difficult for her to find. Nell is going to be ideal for her needs. It seems to me entirely fortunate.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Thirza’s appearance suggested she doubted Providence played a significant role in the affair. A surprisingly favorable opportunity to rid herself of this undesirable orphan had presented itself, yet she failed to experience any gratitude regarding it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Mrs. Peter Scobie was known to her merely by sight as a tiny woman with a shrewish face and not a single bit of extra flesh on her frame. Nevertheless, rumors about her had reached her ears. Mrs. Peter was reputed to be “A terrible worker and driver,” while former servant girls related terrifying stories regarding her disposition, her meanness, and her brood of insolent, argumentative youngsters. The idea of surrendering Nell to her gentle care caused Thirza to experience a pang of guilt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Well, I’ll enter so that we may discuss the issue,” she stated.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “And if Mrs. Peter isn’t walking up the lane this very moment!” Mrs. Tranter cried out, hurriedly ushering her guests through the hall and into the parlor, where a severe coldness hit them as though the air had been filtered through dark green, tightly pulled blinds for such a long time that it was devoid of any warmth it had once held. “That is truly fortunate, because we can resolve the issue immediately. Sit in the armchair, Miss Abernethy. Nell, sit on the ottoman right here and stop wriggling. Let me gather your hats. Flora Odette, head outside and set the kettle on the stove. Good afternoon, Mrs. Scobie. We were only just remarking on how lucky it was that you came by. Allow me to present you two ladies to each other. Mrs. Scobie, Miss Abernethy. Kindly pardon me for a brief second. I neglected to instruct Flora Odette to remove the buns from the oven.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Mrs. Tranter hurried off, having raised the blinds first. Nell, who sat silently upon the ottoman with her hands squeezed together in her lap, gazed at Mrs. Scobie as if spellbound. Would she be handed over to the care of this woman with the keen face and keen eyes? She sensed a lump rising in her throat, and a sharp sting affected her eyes. She was starting to fear that she would be unable to hold her tears in check when Mrs. Tranter came back, red-faced and smiling, fully equipped to weigh every single problem—be it physical, mental, or spiritual—and resolve it on the spot.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “It appears a error occurred regarding this young girl, Mrs. Scobie,” she stated. “I believed that Mr. and Miss Abernethy were looking to adopt a young girl. That was definitely what I was informed. However, it appears a boy was what they desired. Therefore, if your intentions remain unchanged from yesterday, I believe she will suit you perfectly.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Mrs. Scobie quickly scanned Nell’s entire length, moving her eyes from top to bottom.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “What is your name, and how many years old are you?” she asked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Nell Harcourt,” stammered the cowering child, lacking the courage to specify how it should be spelled, “and my age is eleven years.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Humph! You appear to lack substance. However, you possess toughness. It may well be that those with toughness prove superior in the end. Now, should I accept you, it will be necessary for you to be a proper young lady—well-behaved, clever, and polite. You will be required to work for your room and board, without any doubt. Indeed, it seems reasonable for me to relieve you of her, Miss Abernethy. That infant is extremely difficult, and caring for him has left me entirely exhausted. Should it suit you, she can come back to my house with me this very minute.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Upon seeing the young girl's drained countenance and its expression of silent despair—the agony of an undefended small being that is trapped again in the snare it had fled—Thirza’s demeanor relaxed as she gazed at Nell. A troubling certainty came over Thirza that failing to answer the plea in that expression would cause it to torment her until her death. Additionally, she was not fond of Mrs. Scobie. Relinquishing a delicate, “highstrung” youth to a person like her! Indeed, taking on the accountability of performing such an action was impossible for her!

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Indeed, I am uncertain,” she uttered deliberately. “It was not my statement that Obed and I were utterly resolved against retaining her. On the contrary, I might mention that Obed leans toward retaining her. My sole reason for coming was to learn the manner in which the error happened. My opinion is that I ought to carry her back home now and discuss the matter further with Obed. Deciding on anything without conferring with him feels wrong to me. Should we come to the conclusion that we will not retain her, our plan is to deliver or convey her to your house tomorrow evening. Should we fail to do so, you can understand therefrom that her permanent home will be with us. Would such an arrangement be satisfactory to you, Mrs. Scobie?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I guess that must do,” Mrs. Scobie uttered ungraciously.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: As Thirza spoke, a sunrise began to break across Nell’s face. Initially, the expression of hopeless misery washed away; subsequently, a subtle glow of hope appeared; her eyes became intense and luminous like stars at dawn. The girl appeared utterly transformed; then, shortly after, as Mrs. Tranter and Mrs. Scobie exited to search for a recipe that Mrs. Scobie had arrived to request, she leaped to her feet and darted across the room toward Thirza.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Oh, Miss Abernethy, did you truly state that maybe you would allow me to remain at Grey Shutters?” she asked, using a quiet, raspy breath, as though talking in a normal voice could ruin the wonderful chance. “Did you truly state it? Or was it just my imagination that you did?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Nell, you really ought to get a handle on your imagination if discerning reality from fantasy is beyond you,” Thirza remarked irritably. “Indeed, those exact words were what I said, and nothing further. Nothing has been finalized, and it may be that we decide to allow Mrs. Scobie to have you in the end. Her need for you is surely far greater than mine.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I’d prefer returning to the asylum over living with her,” Nell exclaimed passionately. “She appears just like a—like a gimlet.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Thirza hid a grin, believing that Nell needed to be scolded for making that remark.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “It is shameful for a small girl such as you to speak in that manner regarding a lady and a visitor,” she remarked sternly. “Return to your place, sit in silence, keep quiet, and conduct yourself as a well-behaved girl ought to.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I will attempt to perform and become whatever you desire of me, provided you just retain me,” Nell remarked, going back submissively to her ottoman.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: As they returned to Grey Shutters that evening, Obed was waiting in the lane. Having spotted him pacing there from a distance, Thirza had divined his intent. The sense of comfort evident on his features upon realizing she had successfully brought Nell home was something she was ready for. Nevertheless, she refrained from discussing the matter with him until the two of them were in the yard behind the barn, engaged in milking the cows. It was at that moment that she concisely recounted Nell’s past to him and conveyed what had transpired during her meeting with Mrs. Tranter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “That Scobie woman wouldn't be given a dog I had any affection for,” Obed stated with an uncharacteristic burst of energy.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Her way doesn’t really suit my taste,” Thirza confessed, “yet the alternative is us retaining her, Obed. And, because you appear to desire her, I guess I am agreeable—or forced to be. I have pondered the concept so long that I am somewhat accustomed to it. A duty of sorts is what it feels like. Raising a child, a girl in particular, is something I have never done, and I suppose I will fail miserably at it. Even so, my best effort will be given. As for my part, Obed, she is permitted to remain.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: A radiance of pleasure lit up the timid countenance of Obed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “Ah, I figured you would end up viewing it that way, Thirza,” said he. “Such an intriguing little creature she is.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “It’d be more useful if you could describe her as a helpful little thing,” Thirza replied, “but I’ll ensure it becomes my task to train her to be just that. And remember, Obed, you must not interfere with my ways. Maybe an old maid isn’t very knowledgeable about raising a youngster, but I suppose she understands more than an old bachelor. Therefore, you simply let me handle her. When I prove unsuccessful, that will be soon enough for you to meddle.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “There, there, Thirza, you may do as you wish,” Obed offered comfortingly. “Just treat her with as much goodness and kindness as you are able to while avoiding spoiling her. I have a feeling she belongs to the type that allows you to accomplish anything with them, provided you first win their affection.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: Thirza gave a sniff to convey her disdain for the views Obed held regarding anything connected to women, after which she headed toward the dairy carrying the pails.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind
text: “I won’t inform her this evening that she is permitted to remain,” she thought to herself, while pouring the milk through the strainer into the creamers. “Her excitement would be so great that she would not catch a single wink of sleep. Thirza Abernethy, you are truly committed now. Could you ever have imagined a time when you would be taking in an orphan girl? That is astonishing in itself; yet it is even more astonishing that Obed is the one responsible for it, considering how he always appeared to possess such a deep-seated fear of little girls. Regardless, the trial has been agreed upon, and heaven alone can tell what the outcome will be.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: At the time Thirza escorted Nell upstairs to bed that evening, she remarked rigidly:

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Now, Nell, I saw yesterday evening that you dropped your garments everywhere across the ground as you undressed. That shows a lack of neatness, and I am unable to permit it whatsoever. The moment you remove each piece of attire, crease it orderly and set it upon the seat. I have zero patience for young ladies who lack tidiness.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “My mind was in such a state of distress yesterday evening that my clothing never crossed my thoughts,” said Nell. “I will tuck them away neatly this evening. At the asylum, we were perpetually forced to do so. Frequently, however, I would fail to remember, because I was so eager to slip into bed silently and indulge my imagination.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “If you are going to remain here, remembering will need to be a bit easier for you,” Thirza warned. “Now, that appears more like it. Offer your prayers this instant and climb into bed.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “I don’t ever pray,” Nell stated.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Thirza appeared shock-stricken with horror.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Indeed, Nell, what is your meaning? Have you really not been instructed to offer your prayers? Young girls ought to pray, as God constantly desires it of them. Are you unaware of God’s identity, Nell?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “‘Being infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in His existence, wisdom, strength, holiness, justice, benevolence, and veracity, God is a spirit,’” Nell answered without delay or hesitation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Thirza appeared to be somewhat eased.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Thank goodness, you actually know a thing or two! You aren't entirely a pagan. How did you come to learn that?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Oh, during Sunday-school at the asylum. Learning the entire catechism was required of us. I enjoyed it fairly well. A few of the words possess a magnificent quality. ‘Infinite, eternal and unchangeable.’ Is that not grand? It possesses a rolling sound—resembling a large organ being played. I imagine you could not precisely label it poetry, yet it possesses a very similar sound, does it not?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “We are discussing saying your prayers, Nell, rather than poetry. Are you unaware of what an awful, evil deed it is if you fail to say your prayers each evening? I fear that you are quite an awful little girl.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “If your hair were red, being wicked would come more naturally to you than being good,” Nell remarked with blame in her voice. “The difficulties of life remain unknown to those without red hair. Mrs. Thomas informed me that my hair was made red by God intentionally, and my feelings for Him vanished after that. Besides, my exhaustion every evening would forever prevent me from troubling myself with prayers. Expecting folks who must care for twins to recite their prayers is unreasonable. Truly, is that not what you believe?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Thirza came to the conclusion that the initiation of Nell’s religious education required immediate action. Clearly, no time could be wasted.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “As long as you live in my house, Nell, it is required that you say your prayers.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Why, naturally, provided that you wish it,” Nell agreed happily. “I would perform whatever needed doing to please you. However, you must instruct me on the words to speak for this single time. Once I am lying in bed, I am going to invent a truly lovely prayer that I can recite every time. Now that I reflect upon the matter, I think that it will prove to be rather entertaining.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “It is necessary for you to kneel,” Thirza remarked awkwardly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Nell dropped to her knees beside Thirza and peered upward with a serious expression.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “For what reason are individuals required to drop to their knees to offer prayers? Were I truly desirous of praying, I will inform you of my exact course of action. I would venture forth entirely by myself into an immense open field or penetrate the thickest, darkest forest, whereupon I would gaze upward toward the heavens—higher and higher—targeting that exquisite azure expanse that appears as though its color possesses no final boundary. Subsequently, I would simply experience a prayer within myself. Now then, I am prepared. Which words ought I to utter?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Thirza experienced an even greater sense of embarrassment. Her intention had been to instruct Nell in the juvenile classic, “Now I lay me down to sleep.” However, as I have recounted to you, she possessed the beginnings of a sense of humor—a quality that merely serves as another label for recognizing what is appropriate; and the realization abruptly struck her that the modest little prayer, held sacred by white-clad children lisping beside motherly knees, was wholly inappropriate for this freckled witch of a girl who possessed neither knowledge of nor concern for the love of God, given that human affection had never served to translate it to her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Nell, your age is sufficient for you to offer your own prayers,” she eventually remarked. “Simply express gratitude to God for what He has bestowed upon you, and modestly request from Him the items you desire.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Well, I’ll do my best,” Nell assured her, pressing her face against the lap of Thirza. “Gracious heavenly Father—ministers use those words in church, which makes me think they’re appropriate for private prayer, doesn’t it?” she inserted, raising her head briefly. “Gracious heavenly Father, I thank Thee for the Petal Road of Delight and the Lake of Glassy Waters and Bonny and the Frost Maiden. I’m truly very thankful for those things. That covers every blessing I am able to recall at this moment to give thanks for. Regarding my desires, there are so many that listing every one would require a lot of time, which is why I’ll name just the two highest priorities. Please allow me to remain at Grey Shutters; and please allow me to turn out attractive as an adult. I remain,

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “With respect, Nell Harcourt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “There, was my performance okay?” she inquired with enthusiasm, standing. “Had I been given slightly more time to consider it, I could have rendered it far more elaborate.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Only the recollection that Nell’s astonishing prayer stemmed from a lack of spiritual knowledge rather than disrespect saved poor Thirza from falling apart entirely. After tucking the youngster into bed and inwardly resolving to instruct her in a prayer on the following day, she was departing from the chamber holding the lamp when Nell summoned her to return.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “It has only just occurred to me. In lieu of ‘yours respectfully,’ I ought to have uttered ‘Amen,’ ought I not?—as ministers are accustomed to do. Though it had slipped my mind, I believed a prayer required a proper conclusion, which led me to include the former phrase. Is it your opinion that this will alter the outcome?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “I—I do not think it is likely to,” Thirza stated. “Now go off to sleep as a good child should. Good night.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Tonight, I am able to bid good night with an untroubled conscience,” Nell said, snuggling comfortably into her pillows.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: Withdrawing to the kitchen, Thirza placed the candle solidly upon the table and stared angrily at Obed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers
text: “Obed Abernethy, that young girl ought to have been taken in by someone and given an education long ago. She is almost a complete pagan. Would you credit the fact that she had not uttered a single prayer her entire life until this evening? Tomorrow, I intend to request the loan of the Peep of the Day series from the manse, that is my plan. Furthermore, she will be sent to Sunday-school the moment I am able to sew appropriate garments for her. It is obvious to me that I will be kept very busy. Ah well, nobody passes through this life without enduring their portion of difficulty. My existence has been fairly comfortable up to this point, but my turn has finally arrived, and I imagine I must simply endure it as well as I can.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: For reasons she knew best herself, Thirza refrained from informing Nell about remaining at Grey Shutters until the subsequent afternoon. She occupied the child with different chores throughout the morning, observing her with a sharp gaze as she completed them. By midday, she had decided that Nell was intelligent and compliant, ready to labor and prompt to comprehend; her major fault appeared to be an inclination to drift into reveries halfway through a chore and lose track of it completely until she was abruptly brought back to reality by a scolding or a disaster.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: As soon as Nell was done with the dinner dishes, she abruptly faced Thirza, possessing the demeanor and look of somebody fiercely set on discovering the worst. Her slight, small frame shook all over; her cheeks reddened and her pupils widened to the point of turning nearly black; she squeezed her hands together firmly and stated with a beseeching tone:

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: “Oh, I beg you, Miss Abernethy, will you not inform me whether you intend to dismiss me or keep me? Throughout the entire morning I have striven to remain patient, yet I truly believe I am unable to endure this uncertainty a moment longer. The sensation is terrible. I implore you to tell me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: “You failed to rinse the dishcloth with fresh boiling water like I instructed,” Thirza stated firmly. “Go handle that right now prior to asking additional questions, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: Nell departed to take care of the dishcloth, after which she came back to Thirza and fixed begging eyes upon the face of the latter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: “Well,” stated Thirza, who could not discover any pretext to delay her clarification any further, “I guess I may as well inform you. Obed and I have resolved to retain you—provided, that is, you attempt to be a dutiful little girl and prove that you are appreciative. Why, child, what on earth is wrong?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun
text: “Tears are falling from my eyes,” Nell remarked, sounding confused. “The reason escapes me. My joy couldn't be greater. Actually, glad fails to properly describe it. Feeling glad matched my experience with the cherry blossoms on Petal Road—whereas this! Ah, it goes far beyond mere gladness. Such happiness fills me. Trying to act as good as possible will be my goal. That promises to be a difficult struggle, considering how frequently Mrs. Thomas remarked on my extreme wickedness. Even so, my utmost efforts will be given. Still, are you able to explain my tears to me?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Nell,” she uttered with a degree of softness.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: There was no reply.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Nell,” with increased sternness, “get off that bed right now and pay attention to my words to you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: Nell wriggled down from the bed and took a stiff seat on an adjacent chair, her puffy face marked by tears while her gaze remained obstinately attached to the ground.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “You are acting in a fine manner, Nell! Do you not feel shame?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “She lacked the right to call me redheaded and ugly,” Nell replied, avoiding the point and acting defensively.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “You were not entitled to become so enraged and speak in that manner to her, Nell. My shame regarding you was complete—utterly complete. My desire was for you to act courteously toward Mrs. Sowerby, yet you brought shame upon me rather than doing so. It is quite beyond me why Mrs. Sowerby mentioning that you possess red hair and plain looks should cause you to fly into a rage like that. You state the very same thing frequently yourself.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Oh, but saying something yourself is so completely different from hearing someone else say it,” Nell cried out. “A thing might be known to you as fact, yet you cannot stop hoping that others do not entirely believe it to be so. It must seem to you that my temper is terrible, but it was beyond my control. When those words came from her, something simply swelled up inside me and suffocated me. I was forced to lash out at her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Indeed, you displayed yourself in a splendid manner, I am bound to remark. A delightful tale concerning you will be spread far and wide by Mrs. Sowerby—and without doubt, she will share it. For you to become so enraged was a terrible occurrence, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Try to picture what your reactions would be if a person stated directly to you that you were scrawny and hideous,” begged Nell through her tears.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: A former memory unexpectedly occurred to Thirza. Having been a tiny child, she had overheard one aunt remark about her to another aunt, “What a pity she is such a dark, homely little thing.” Thirza reached fully fifty years of age before that recollection ceased to cause her pain.

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Nell, I am not claiming I believe Mrs. Sowerby acted entirely properly when she spoke to you in that manner,” she conceded with less harshness in her voice. “Agatha speaks her mind too freely. However, that does not justify you acting as you did. Being an unfamiliar face, an aged lady, and a guest in my home are three separate, compelling grounds for you to have shown her deference. Your conduct was disrespectful and impudent, and”—a fortunate idea for a penalty struck Thirza—“you are required to approach her, express deep regret for losing your cool, and beg for her pardon.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “That is something I will never do,” declared Nell with dark resolve. “You are free to penalize me however you wish, Thirza. You may lock me away inside a pitch-black, soggy vault filled with serpents and amphibians while giving me nothing to eat but bread and water, and no protest will come from me. However, I am incapable of begging Mrs. Sowerby for her pardon.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “It is not our practice to lock individuals inside cold wet vaults,” Thirza remarked crisply, “mainly because they are quite rare in Brierley. However, you are required to make amends to Mrs. Sowerby, and you will remain confined to this room until you are able to inform me of your readiness to comply.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Then this means I must remain here for all time,” Nell stated sorrowfully, “since apologizing to Mrs. Sowerby for what I uttered to her is impossible for me. In what way could I? Remorse is not what I feel. My regret lies in having upset you; nevertheless, delivering those exact words to her brought me joy. The feeling of relief was immense. Expressing regret when it does not exist is impossible for me, is it not? Conceiving that I am regretful is beyond my ability.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: “Maybe your morning state of mind will improve the functioning of your imagination,” Thirza remarked, getting up to leave. “The night lies ahead for you to ponder your behavior and attain a superior mental attitude. Your promise was to endeavor to be an exceptionally well-behaved girl should we retain you at Grey Shutters, yet I am bound to remark that tonight’s events have hardly reflected that.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified
text: Abandoning this parting blow to fester within Nell’s tempestuous heart, Thirza went down into the kitchen, deeply disturbed in spirit and annoyed in her innermost self. Her irritation was directed as much at herself as at Nell, since, each time she remembered the speechlessly astonished face of Mrs. Agatha, her lips quivered with entertainment and she experienced a highly blameworthy impulse to chuckle.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: THIRZA did not speak to Obed regarding the matter that night; however, because Nell remained disobedient on the following morning, it became necessary to explain why she was missing from the morning meal. Thirza recounted the entire tale to Obed, making a deliberate effort to make him realize just how grave Nell’s conduct had been.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Agatha Sowerby is an intrusive old busybody, so she deserved to be scolded,” Obed offered as a comforting reply.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Obed Abernethy, my surprise at you is great. Though aware of Nell’s terrible conduct, you still defend her! Next, I expect you will claim that no punishment whatsoever should be given to her!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Well now—no—not quite,” Obed answered anxiously. “I suppose she should receive a bit of punishment. However, Thirza, refrain from being overly strict with her. Keep in mind that she has never possessed anybody to instruct her properly. You—you intend to provide her with food, do you not?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Have you ever known me to make people starve so they would behave?” Thirza asked with indignation. “Her meals will be given to her regularly, and I am going to take them to her room personally. However, Obed, she will remain upstairs until she is ready to offer an apology to Mrs. Sowerby, and I will not change my mind.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: The meals of breakfast, dinner, and supper proved to be extremely quiet, as Nell continued to be unyielding. Following every repast, Thirza bore a laden tray up to the east gable, returning with it afterward without any remarkable reduction in its contents. Obed watched this final trip downward with a worried expression, wondering if Nell had consumed a single morsel.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: As Thirza departed that night to fetch the cattle from the rear field, Obed, who had lingered near the barns while observing, sneaked into the dwelling like a thief and tiptoed to the upper floor. Usually, Obed moved back and forth between the kitchen and the small bedchamber adjoining the corridor where he stayed; occasionally, he made an uneasy foray into the parlor or sitting room whenever the minister arrived for tea. Yet he had not set foot on the upper level of his personal residence since the spring he assisted Thirza in wallpapering the spare bedroom, which occurred four years prior.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Stealthily walking on his tiptoes down the hallway, he lingered for a few minutes past the entrance to the east gable prior to gathering the bravery needed to knock his fingers against it and subsequently swing the door wide enough to sneak a look inside.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Nell occupied the yellow chair beside the window, staring sadly into the garden. Her appearance was exceedingly small and miserable, which struck a pang of guilt in Obed’s heart. Shutting the door quietly, he crept over on his toes to reach her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Nell,” he murmured, in the manner of someone fearing they might be heard, “how are you faring, Nell?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: A faint smile touched Nell’s face.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Fairly well. A lot is imagined by me, which assists in passing the time. Naturally, it is somewhat lonely. Even so, I might as well become accustomed to it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Nell flashed another smile, courageously confronting the extensive duration of lonely confinement that lay ahead of her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Remembering the need to deliver his message quickly before Thirza might come back too soon, Obed spoke in a low voice, “Well now, Nell, wouldn’t it be best if you just got it finished and behind you?” He added softly, “You realize it is bound to happen eventually, because Thirza possesses a terrible resolve—a terrible resolve, Nell. My advice is to perform it immediately and get it done.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Are you saying I should express regret to Mrs. Sowerby?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Yes—apologize—that’s the exact word,” Obed said with enthusiasm. “Merely make amends in a manner of speaking. That’s the point I was trying to reach.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “I guess I might do it as a favor to you,” Nell remarked contemplatively. “Stating that I feel regret would be accurate enough, since I do feel regret at present. Last night I was not the least bit regretful. I was utterly enraged, and that rage persisted the entire night. That I am certain of, as I awakened on three occasions and felt simply irate each time. However, by this morning that had passed. My anger had vanished—and its departure left a terrible kind of emptiness, as well. I experienced such deep shame regarding my behavior. Even so, I simply was unable to consider going to express that to Mrs. Sowerby. Doing so would be deeply embarrassing. My decision was made that I would remain confined in this place indefinitely instead of doing such a thing. Even so—I would perform any action for your sake—if it is truly your desire—”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Indeed I do, naturally. Without your presence, it gets dreadful lonely down below. Be a dear child and simply go make amends.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “All right,” Nell stated with a tone of resignation. “The moment Thirza returns, I will let her know that I have changed my mind.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Indeed—you are correct, Nell. However, keep Thirza from knowing I mentioned a word regarding it. She could believe I was meddling, and I gave my word to refrain from doing so.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Unamed untamed steeds will not extract the mystery from me,” Nell pledged with gravity. “In what manner would untamed steeds pull a mystery out of someone, in any case?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: However, Obed had departed, frightened by what he had accomplished. To prevent Thirza from guessing his actions, he hurried away to the farthest end of the horse pasture. As for Thirza, when she came back to the house, she was pleasantly startled when a mournful voice called, “Thirza” from above the banisters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Well?” she asked, stepping into the hall.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “I apologize for losing my self-control and making impolite remarks, and I am prepared to visit Mrs. Sowerby to convey that to her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “All right.” Showing no trace of her relief, Thirza spoke briskly. She had been pondering what on earth she ought to do should Nell refuse to yield. “When the milking is done, I’ll bring you down.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Consequently, following the milking, there were Thirza and Nell strolling along the lane, with the first standing straight and victorious, and the second slumping and gloomy. Midway down the path, however, Nell’s gloom disappeared as though by magic. Raising her head, she walked briskly onward, keeping her eyes set upon the evening sky while carrying an aura of quiet excitement. Thirza viewed this transformation with displeasure. Here was not the humble apologizer whom it was appropriate for her to bring before the aggrieved Mrs. Sowerby.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Nell, what is on your mind?” she inquired abruptly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “I am figuring out what needs to be said to Mrs. Sowerby,” Nell replied in a dreamy manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
