text: Although this ought to have been pleasing, it failed to fully satisfy. Thirza remained unable to shake the feeling that her punitive plan was somehow going awry. It was entirely improper for Nell to possess an expression so ecstatic and glowing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Absorbed and glowing, Nell kept going up to the exact spot where Mrs. Sowerby sat knitting beside her kitchen window. At that point, the glow disappeared. Sorrowful remorse showed on all of her features. Prior to any spoken word, Nell abruptly dropped to her knees in front of the amazed Mrs. Agatha and stretched her hands out imploringly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Oh, Mrs. Sowerby, my regret is so immense,” she uttered while her voice trembled slightly. “Even exhaustively reciting every word in a dictionary would fail to convey the full extent of my remorse. Your imagination will simply have to fill in the rest. My conduct toward you was atrocious—and I have brought shame upon those beloved companions, Obed and Thirza, who permitted my residence at Grey Shutters despite my not being a boy. My wickedness and lack of gratitude are appalling, making me worthy of eternal punishment and banishment by decent society. Becoming enraged simply because you imparted the truth to me was a deeply evil act. Indeed, it was the truth; absolute veracity marked your every word. Red describes my hair, and my appearance is freckled, scrawny, and hideous. Likewise, truth backed my own statements to you, yet they ought to have remained unspoken. Oh, Mrs. Sowerby, I beg, I beg of you to bestow your forgiveness upon me. Denying it would inflict permanent grief upon a helpless young orphan girl, a fate you surely would not wish even upon one with a horrific temper, would you? Oh, my heart tells me you could not. Mrs. Sowerby, please declare that I am forgiven.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Nell pressed her hands together, bent her head downward, and stood awaiting the verdict.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Her truthfulness was beyond doubt, emanating from every nuance of her vocal expression. This authentic quality was perceived by both Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby. However, the first of them realized with consternation that Nell was truly taking delight in her period of disgrace—that she was delighting in the complete nature of her degradation. What had become of the beneficial chastisement for which she, Thirza, had congratulated herself? Nell had transformed it into a form of definite enjoyment.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: The kindly, if rather meddlesome, heart of good Mrs. Sowerby lacked the sharpness of perception to notice this. All she observed was the completely exhaustive nature of Nell’s apology, which caused every bit of her anger to disappear.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Come, come, stand up, little one,” she stated warmly. “Naturally, you have my forgiveness. It seems I was likely somewhat overly strict with you, regardless. However, I am simply quite a candid individual. You simply must not pay me any heed, that is all. No one can dispute that your hair is exceedingly red; nevertheless, I used to know a female—we actually attended school together—who possessed hair precisely as red as yours in her youth, yet it deepened into a truly lovely auburn as she matured. It would not amaze me in the slightest if the same thing happened to yours—not in the slightest.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Oh, Mrs. Sowerby!” Nell inhaled deeply while standing up. “You have offered me hope. I will forever consider you a benefactor. Oh, I would be able to bear anything provided I just believed my hair was going to turn a handsome auburn once I was grown up. Would it not be far simpler to be good if a person possessed a handsome auburn hair, don’t you think? And now would it be all right if I went out into your garden to sit upon the bench beneath the apple-trees while Thirza and you discuss things? There exists far greater room for imagination in that spot.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Mercy, indeed, run on, little one. Furthermore, you may gather a bunch of those white June lilies located in the corner if you wish.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: When the door shut after Nell, a lamp was promptly lit by Mrs. Sowerby as she rose.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “She is truly a peculiar little child. Thirza, move to this chair, which offers more comfort than the one you are currently using; that one is merely reserved for the hired boy's use. Indeed, her behavior is undeniably strange, yet she possesses an appealing quality regardless. My astonishment at you and Obed deciding to raise her has diminished from what it once was—and my pity for both of you has lessened too. It is possible she will turn out fine. Naturally, her manner of speaking is unusual—a bit overly—well, rather too forceful, as you are aware; nevertheless, she will probably outgrow that trait now that her life is spent among civilized people. Furthermore, I suspect she possesses a rather swift temper; yet one reassuring thought is that a youngster with a fiery temper, who simply flares up and then settles down, is not at all prone to being cunning or dishonest. May I be spared from a deceitful child, above all else. When all is considered, Thirza, I am somewhat fond of her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: As Thirza departed for her house, Nell emerged from the sweet-smelling dusk of the orchard, holding a bundle of white narcissi in her hands.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Did I not make a rather good apology?” she inquired with pride while they walked along the lane. “It occurred to me that as long as I was required to perform the task, I ought to accomplish it completely.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “You certainly did a complete job of it,” commented Thirza. Finding that she was disposed to giggle at the memory filled Thirza with consternation. A troubling sense that she should reprimand Nell for offering such an effective apology also came over her; yet, such an action would be absurd! Saying sternly, she struck a middle ground with her moral sense:

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “It is my hope that you will not need to offer numerous further excuses of this nature. My wish is that you will endeavor to govern your passion from this point on, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “If folks didn't tease me regarding my appearance, that would be less difficult,” Nell said, sighing. “Other matters do not make me angry; yet being mocked about my hair exhausts me so much that it simply causes me to explode with rage. Is it your opinion that my hair will truly turn into a lovely auburn once I am older?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Nell, your appearance shouldn't occupy your thoughts to such a degree. It worries me that you are an exceedingly vain young girl.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “In what way am I capable of vanity if my own plainness is clear to me?” Nell objected. “Beautiful items are my passion; and staring into the mirror only to behold an unlovely image fills me with distaste. A deep sadness comes over me—the exact sensation I experience whenever I view something repulsive. My compassion goes out to it for its lack of beauty.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Handsome is as handsome does,” Thirza quoted. “That has been told to me previously, yet I am dubious regarding its truth,” skeptical Nell observed, smelling her narcissi. “Oh, these blossoms are so sweet! Mrs. Sowerby was very kind to present them to me. At present, I harbour no resentment toward Mrs. Sowerby. Expressing regret and receiving pardon bestows a delightful, soothing sensation, doesn’t it? Are not the stars brilliant this evening? Were it possible to dwell within a star, which would be your choice? I would prefer that beautiful, bright, large one far off in that direction, situated atop that dark hill.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Nell, do hold your tongue,” said Thirza, who was completely exhausted from attempting to keep up with the twists and turns of Nell’s mind.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: Nell uttered nothing else prior to their turning into the lane that belonged to them. Down it to encounter them came a slight gypsy wind, filled with the spicy fragrance of dew-moistened young ferns. High up amidst the darkness, from the kitchen situated at Grey Shutters, a bright light shone through the trees. Nell abruptly drew near Thirza and slid her own hand inside the hardened palm of the older woman.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Going back to a place I know is truly home feels wonderful,” she remarked. “Grey Shutters has my love already, even though I have never cared for anywhere else before. Not a single place ever felt like home to me. Oh, Thirza, my happiness is so great. I could offer up a prayer this very minute without struggling in the slightest.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: As those slender fingers met hers, a gentle, comforting feeling overflowed within Thirza, perhaps representing a pulse of the motherhood she had never known. The sheer unfamiliarity and delight of the sensation rattled her. To regain her usual tranquility, she hurried to deliver a moral lesson.

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Provided that you act as a good girl, Nell, happiness will always be yours. Furthermore, uttering your prayers ought never to be a difficult thing for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Uttering one’s prayers does not quite equate to praying,” Nell remarked thoughtfully. “However, I am about to pretend that I am the wind that blows up above in the tops of those trees. Once I grow weary of the trees, I will pretend that I am swaying softly down here among the ferns—and next I will soar across to Mrs. Sowerby’s garden and make the flowers dance—and after that I will rush in a single huge swoop across the clover field—and then I will sweep across the Lake of Glassy Waters and stir it completely into small, glittering waves. Oh, a wind offers such immense possibilities for imagination! Therefore, I will refrain from speaking any longer at present, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology
text: “Thanks be to goodness for that,” Thirza breathed in devout relief.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “SO, what is your opinion of them?” Thirza asked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: Nell, who was in the gable room, gazed earnestly at three brand-new dresses laid across the bed. The first was made of snuffy colored gingham that Thirza had felt driven to purchase from a peddler during the previous summer owing to its durable appearance; the second was a black-and-white checkered sateen that she had acquired from a bargain counter that winter; and the third was a rigid print featuring an unpleasant tint of blue, bought by her that very week in a Delford store.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: She was the one who had fashioned them herself, and each of them was constructed in the exact same manner—unadorned skirts gathered densely into unadorned bodices, featuring sleeves that were just as unadorned as the bodices and skirts and as snug as it was possible for sleeves to be.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “I will pretend to enjoy them,” Nell stated with gravity.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “I am not asking you to picture it,” Thirza stated, her feelings hurt. “Oh, I perceive that you dislike the attire! What is wrong with it? Are the garments not tidy, spotless, and brand-new?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Yes.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “For what reason do you dislike them, then?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Pretty—they’re—they’re not,” Nell admitted with hesitation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Pretty!” Thirza expressed with a sniff. “Getting pretty dresses for you was not something I troubled my head about. I do not believe in indulging vanity, Nell, and I will let you know that straight away. Good, sensible, and serviceable are what those dresses are, devoid of any frills or furbelows, and for this summer, they are all that you will receive. School, once you start attending, can be done in the brown gingham and the blue print. For church and Sunday-school, you have the sateen. Keeping them clean, neat, and untorn is what I will expect from you. After the skimpy wincey things that you have been wearing, I should think you would feel grateful to receive almost anything.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Oh, I feel thankful,” Nell declared. “However, my gratitude would be vastly greater had you—had you constructed merely a single one possessing gathered shoulders. Gathered shoulders are the height of style currently. Wearable fabric boasting gathered shoulders would deliver me a supreme rush, Thirza, simply by putting it on.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Well, you must forgo your excitement. I lacked fabric to throw away on puffed sleeves. In any case, I consider them foolish-looking items. My preference is for the simple, practical ones.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Yet I would prefer to seem foolish alongside everyone else instead of simple and practical on my own,” Nell continued in a sorrowful manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “I know I can rely on you for that! Now, place those dresses neatly on hangers inside your closet, after which you must sit and study the Sunday-school material. A quarterly was obtained from Mr. Bell on your behalf, and your attendance at Sunday-school is expected tomorrow,” declared Thirza, departing for the lower floor in a fit of pique.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: Nell folded her fingers together and gazed at the garments.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “I really hoped for a white dress featuring puffed sleeves,” she murmured gloomily. “I asked God for one, though I didn't actually anticipate it because of that. It didn't seem likely to me that God would take the time to care about the clothing of a small orphan girl. I realized I would simply need to rely on Thirza to get it. Oh well, luckily I have the ability to pretend that a dress among them consists of snow-white muslin adorned with exquisite lace ruffles and triple-puffed sleeves.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: When the following morning arrived, Thirza was kept from attending Sunday-school alongside Nell because of signs that a sick headache was coming on.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Nell, it will be necessary for you to head downstairs and fetch Mrs. Sowerby,” she stated. “You will be placed in the correct class by her. Now, ensure that you conduct yourself appropriately. Remain behind for the preaching later, and request that Mrs. Sowerby point out our pew to you. This cent is for the collection. Avoid staring at others, and do not squirm. Upon returning home, I expect the text to be recited to me by you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: Nell began looking completely respectable, clad in the rigid black-and-white sateen, a garment that was modest concerning its length and surely free from any accusation of being skimpy, yet managed to highlight each corner and angle of her slender frame. Her headwear was a small, flat, shiny, brand-new sailor hat, whose utmost simplicity had similarly greatly let down Nell, who had allowed herself hidden dreams of flowers and ribbon. These blossoms were provided, nonetheless, prior to Nell arriving at the main thoroughfare, because encountering a golden storm of wind-ruffled buttercups and a magnificence of wild roses halfway along the lane, Nell immediately and generously decorated her hat using a dense garland of the flowers. No matter what additional folks may have considered regarding the outcome, it pleased Nell, and she walked briskly down the highway, bearing her red head with its adornment of yellow and pink quite haughtily.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: Upon arriving at Mrs. Sowerby’s home, she discovered that the lady had already left. Undeterred, Nell continued her journey to the church by herself. Within the porch, she encountered a gathering of small girls, who were all dressed up in varying degrees of bright whites, blues, and pinks, every one of them gazing with inquisitive eyes at this newcomer among them, wearing her bizarre head decoration. The young girls of Brierley were already familiar with strange rumors regarding Nell. Mrs. Sowerby claimed that her temper was terrible; Tobias Buote, the hired farmhand at Grey Shutters, reported that she conversed constantly with herself or addressed the trees and flowers as if she were insane. They observed her and exchanged whispers with one another behind their Sunday school papers. No one offered any welcoming gestures, either at that moment or afterward when the preliminary proceedings concluded and Nell found herself placed in Miss Rogerson’s class.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: A lady in middle age, Miss Rogerson had spent twenty years teaching a Sunday-school class. The way she taught involved reading the printed questions straight from the quarterly while glaring over its border at whichever little girl she believed should provide the response. Her gaze landed frequently on Nell, who replied without hesitation because Thirza had drilled her so well; nevertheless, it was doubtful whether she truly grasped much regarding the questions or her own replies.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: She was of the opinion that Miss Rogerson was not to her liking, and her feelings were most unhappy; puffed sleeves were worn by all the other little girls in the class. Life, as Nell perceived it, held no true value if one lacked puffed sleeves.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Well, how did you like Sunday-school?” Thirza inquired upon Nell’s return home. Because her wreath had wilted, Nell had thrown it away in the lane, which temporarily prevented Thirza from discovering it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “I displeased it entirely. It was dreadful.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Nell Harcourt!” Thirza said in a rebuking manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: Releasing a drawn-out sigh, Nell took a seat on the rocking chair, planted a kiss upon a leaf belonging to Bonny, and gave a wave of her hand toward a blooming fuchsia.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “It is possible they felt lonely during my absence,” she clarified. “Furthermore, regarding Sunday-school, my conduct was good, exactly as you instructed me. Although Mrs. Sowerby had left, I proceeded on my own. Along with numerous other small girls, I entered the church, and as the preliminary portion took place, my seat was in the pew corner near the window. The prayer delivered by Mr. Bell was exceedingly lengthy. Had I not been positioned beside that window, I would have become terribly fatigued prior to his conclusion. However, because it offered a direct view of the Lake of Glassy Waters, I simply stared at it and envisioned various marvelous scenarios.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “You ought not to have done anything like that. You ought to have obeyed Mr. Bell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “However, his words were not directed at me,” Nell objected. “God was the one he addressed, and even then, he appeared to lack much enthusiasm. My impression was that he felt God was located at too great a distance. Suspended above the water was an extensive line of white birches, and the sunlight filtered through their branches, penetrating deeply, deeply into the lake. Oh, Thirza, a gorgeous dream could not have been more lovely! A feeling of excitement went through me, and I simply stated, ‘Thank you for it, God,’ a couple of times.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Only in silence, I trust,” Thirza remarked with concern.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Oh, no, merely under my breath. Well, Mr. Bell finally managed to finish, and I was instructed to enter the classroom alongside Miss Rogerson’s class. Nine other girls were present in it. Puffed sleeves were worn by all of them. I attempted to envision that mine were puffed as well, yet I was unable to do so. Why was I unable to? Envisioning that they were puffed when I was by myself in the east gable was as easy as could be, but doing it there amidst the others who possessed actual, genuine puffs was dreadfully difficult.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Your mind ought not to have dwelt upon your sleeves during Sunday school. Your focus should have been directed toward the lesson instead. I trust you were familiar with it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “Oh, yes; and I responded to a great number of inquiries. Miss Rogerson posed quite a few. It felt unfair to me that she did all the questioning. I desired to ask her numerous things, but I refrained since I felt she was not a kindred spirit. Afterwards, every one of the other little girls recited a paraphrase. She inquired whether I was familiar with any. My reply was that I was not, though I offered to recite, ‘The Dog at His Master’s Grave’ if she wished. It is contained in the Third Royal Reader. Although it is not genuinely religious verse, its sad and melancholy tone makes it practically the same thing. She stated that it was unsuitable and instructed me to memorize the nineteenth paraphrase for the following Sunday. I perused it later while in church, and it is wonderful. Two lines, especially, cause me to feel a real thrill.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “‘Fast as the butchered hosts dropped In Midian’s wicked time.’

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: “I am ignorant of the meaning of ‘squadrons’ and ‘Midian,’ too, but its sound is so tragical. Waiting until next Sunday to recite it is almost impossible for me. During the entire week, I will practice it. Following Sunday-school, I requested Miss Rogerson—since Mrs. Sowerby was located too far off—to point out your pew to me. I remained as motionless as possible, and the text chosen was Revelations, chapter three, verses two and three. That text was exceptionally long. Were I a minister, my choices would be the brief, snappy ones. That sermon went on terribly long, as well. It seems to me the minister was obliged to make it correspond to the text. I failed to find him even slightly interesting. His problem appears to be a lack of sufficient imagination. I gave him very little of my attention. My mind was simply allowed to wander, and I imagined the most astonishing things.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
text: A sense of powerlessness came over Thirza, knowing a stern reprimand was called for, yet her hands were tied because a portion of Nell’s remarks, particularly those concerning the sermons of the minister and the prayers of Mr. Bell, reflected the very ideas she had harbored in her own innermost soul for a long time without ever voicing them. It appeared to her almost as if those hidden, unspoken, judgmental opinions had abruptly materialized into a tangible and reproachful figure through this candid scrap of forgotten humankind.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: It was only on the following Friday that Thirza was told the tale about the hat covered in flowers. Upon her return from the house of Mrs. Sowerby, she demanded an explanation from Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Nell, Mrs. Agatha says you attended church this past Sunday wearing a hat absurdly adorned with roses and buttercups. Whatever possessed you to pull a stunt like that? You must have looked quite sightly!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh. I am aware that pink and yellow do not look good on me,” Nell started.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Nonsense to speak of becoming! What proved ridiculous was placing any flowers whatsoever upon your hat, regardless of their hue. You are an exceedingly infuriating child!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “I fail to understand how wearing flowers on a hat is any more absurd than on a dress,” Nell objected. “A great number of young girls present had flowers fastened to their dresses. Where is the distinction?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Thirza refused to be led away from the secure realm of the concrete toward the uncertain routes of the abstract.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Do not respond to me in that manner, Nell. Doing that was an extremely foolish action on your part. Do not ever allow me to catch you playing such a prank again. Mrs. Agatha mentions that she felt as though she would sink through the floor the moment she witnessed you arrive all dressed up in that fashion. She was unable to approach you closely enough to instruct you to remove them until the opportunity had passed. She states that the gossip among people was quite terrible. Naturally, they would assume I lacked the good judgment to prevent you from going out adorned in such a way.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh, I’m so sorry,” said Nell, as tears began filling her eyes. “I never imagined it would bother you. I felt they would look charming on my hat because the buttercups and roses were so sweet and pretty. Artificial flowers were worn on the hats of many of the little girls. I fear I will turn out to be a terrible trial for you. Perhaps returning me to the asylum would be best for you. It would be awful; enduring it seems impossible for me; I would probably develop consumption; you can see how thin I am already, after all. Still, it would be preferable to being a trial for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Nonsense,” stated Thirza, annoyed with herself because she had caused the child to weep. “I am certain that I have no desire to return you to the asylum. My sole wish is for you to conduct yourself as other little girls do and refrain from making yourself look foolish. Stop weeping now. There is some news I have for you. Isolde Pembroke arrived home this afternoon. I am heading up there to find out whether I can borrow a skirt pattern from Mrs. Pembroke, and you may accompany me and become acquainted with Isolde if you wish.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Nell stood up, her hands folded together and tears yet shining upon her cheeks, while the dish towel she was in the middle of hemming slid unnoticed down to the floor.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh, Thirza, I am filled with fear—at present that the moment has arrived, I am genuinely afraid. Suppose she fails to be fond of me! That would stand as the most tragic letdown I have ever experienced.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “There now, try not to become flustered. Furthermore, I really hope you will refrain from employing such lengthy vocabulary. Coming from such a small girl, it comes across as quite strange. It is my belief that Isolde will find you pleasant enough. However, the person you must truly account for is her mother. Should she take a dislike to you, Isolde’s affection for you will be of no consequence. In the event that she has been informed of your angry display toward Mrs. Sowerby and your attendance at church wearing buttercups around your headwear, I cannot imagine what opinion she will hold regarding you. It is essential that you remain courteous and act properly, and avoid delivering any of your shocking remarks. Goodness gracious, the child is truly shaking!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Nell shuddered, her pale face stretched tight.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh, Thirza, had you been about to encounter a young girl you desired to have as your closest companion and whose mother perhaps would not approve of you, excitement would overcome you as well,” she uttered while hurrying to retrieve her hat.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Taking the shortcut over the brook and through the fir-tree grove, they made their way to Pear Hill. Thirza knocked on the kitchen door, which was answered by Mrs. Pembroke. Possessing a remarkably determined mouth, she was a tall woman with dark eyes and dark hair. She was known to be extremely firm when it came to her children.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “In what manner do you fare, Thirza?” she inquired warmly. “Enter. Further, I presume this represents the small female child you have taken as your own?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Indeed, Nell Harcourt is who this is,” Thirza declared.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Spelled with an E,” gasped Nell, who, despite being excited and tremulous, was resolute that no misunderstanding should exist regarding that crucial detail.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Failing to hear or perhaps not understanding, Mrs. Pembroke simply clasped hands and remarked gently:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “How are you?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Thank you ma’am, my physical health is fine, even if my mood is quite disheveled,” Nell stated seriously. After that, she turned toward Thirza and whispered loud enough to be heard, “Thirza, that wasn't particularly shocking, was it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: A book was being read by Isolde as she sat on the sofa, but she let it fall upon the arrival of the visitors. A extremely attractive young girl, she possessed the dark eyes and hair of her mother, along with cheeks of rose, while her cheerful look came to her as a legacy from her father.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “This is Isolde, my little girl,” Mrs. Pembroke said. “Isolde, perhaps you can show Nell your flowers out in the garden. Doing that will be far better for you than making your eyes suffer over that book. She spends way too much time reading—” she remarked to Thirza while the young girls stepped outside—“and I am unable to stop her, because her father encourages and helps her. A book is something she is constantly reading. Having the possibility of a playmate makes me happy—maybe she will spend more time outside because of it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Nell and Isolde were standing out in the garden, which was filled with the soft light of the setting sun shining through the dark, ancient fir trees located to its west, and they looked at one another bashfully across a patch of splendid tiger lilies.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: A bowery wilderness of flowers, the Pembroke garden would have gladdened Nell’s heart during any period less charged with fate. Enclosing it were massive old willows and lofty firs, under which blossomed shade-loving flora. Crisp, right-angled walkways neatly edged with clamshells crossed it such as damp red ribbons, and old-fashioned blooms grew profusely in the intervening beds. Rosy bleeding-hearts were present alongside grand, magnificent crimson peonies; white, sweet-scented narcissi stood with prickly, sweet Scotch roses; columbines of pink, blue, and white grew near lilac-shaded Bouncing Bets; there were clusters of southernwood, ribbon grass, and mint; purple Adam-and-Eve appeared with daffodils and aggregations of sweet clover pale with its dainty, aromatic, feathery plumes; scarlet lightning thrust its flaming spears above demure white musk-flowers; it was a garden in which sunshine rested and bees droned, and breezes, coaxed to linger, purred and rustled.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh, Isolde,” Nell uttered finally, holding her hands together and uttering the words barely above a breath, “oh, do you believe you could fondle me slightly—sufficiently to become my dearest companion?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Isolde burst into laughter, as she invariably did prior to uttering a word.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Well, I suppose that’s true,” she stated openly. “I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful. No other girls reside close enough for us to play together, and none of my sisters are old enough.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Will you promise to be my friend for all time?” Nell asked with eagerness.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Isolde looked shocked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “The act of swearing is remarkably evil, after all,” she stated with a tone of rebuke.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh no, my sort of swearing isn't that. You know there exist two types.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “I only ever knew of a single type,” Isolde remarked with hesitation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Another one truly exists. Oh, it is not evil in any way. It merely involves making a solemn vow and promise.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Indeed, I am fine with performing that,” consented Isolde, feeling a sense of relief. “In what way do you accomplish it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “We must clasp hands—like this,” Nell said with gravity. “It should take place above flowing water. We will simply pretend this trail is flowing water. First, I will say the vow. I solemnly swear to remain loyal to my bosom friend, Isolde Pembroke, for as long as the sun and moon endure. Now repeat it yourself and insert my name.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Laughter echoing from both bow and stern, Isolde reiterated the “oath.” She subsequently remarked:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: As far as the log bridge, Isolde accompanied Thirza and Nell on their walk home. Embracing each other, the pair of young girls strolled along. Upon reaching the brook, they separated, having made numerous pledges to meet again the following afternoon.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Well, did you find Isolde a kindred spirit?” Thirza inquired while they ascended through the garden at Grey Shutters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Indeed,” Nell breathed out, entirely unaware that Thirza was being sarcastic. “Oh Thirza, right now no girl on St. Brendan’s Island feels more joy than I do. You can be certain that I will offer my prayers with genuine gladness this evening. Isolde and I plan to construct a playhouse tomorrow within the birch grove belonging to Mr. William Bell. May I take the fragments of smashed china located in the woodshed? February brings Isolde’s birthday, whereas my own falls in March. Wouldn't you agree that such a timing is an exceptionally odd coincidence? Isolde intends to loan me a volume for reading. It is absolutely wonderful and intensely thrilling, according to her. She will point out a spot deep among the trees where rice lilies can be found. Wouldn't you say that Isolde possesses exceedingly soulful eyes? It would be wonderful if my own eyes were soulful. Isolde plans to instruct me in singing a piece entitled ‘Nelly in the Hazel Dell.’ She means to present me with an illustration to display inside my bedroom; according to her, it is a truly magnificent image—a exquisite woman wearing a gown of pale blue silk. It was presented to her by a representative selling sewing machines. It breaks my heart that I possess nothing to present to Isolde. My height exceeds Isolde’s by an inch, yet her body is considerably plumper; she claims a desire to be slender due to it being far more elegant, though I suspect she merely made that statement to comfort my emotions. At some point, we plan to visit the beach to collect seashells. We settled on naming the stream near the log bridge the Nymph’s Well. Would you not call that a supremely sophisticated name? I previously read a tale featuring a spring bearing that title. It is my belief that a dryad resembles an adult fairy.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Well, my sole wish is that Isolde isn't talked to death by you,” Thirza remarked. “However, Nell, bear this in mind throughout your preparations. Your time won't be spent playing entirely, or even for the greater part of it. Your tasks will await you, and completing them must come before anything else.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: Nell’s joy was complete, and Obed made it spill over. Having recently returned from a journey to the Delford store, he awkwardly drew a little package out of his pocket and presented it to Nell, casting an apologetic glance toward Thirza.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “I brought you these because I overheard you mention that you enjoyed chocolate sweeties,” he said.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Humph,” Thirza sniffed. “It is going to destroy her stomach and teeth. Now, now, child, do not appear so gloomy. Since Obed went out and purchased them, you may consume those. It would have been preferable if he had carried peppermints to you. Those are more wholesome. Do not make yourself ill by consuming every one of them right away now.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “Oh, no, indeed, I won’t,” Thirza was eagerly told by Nell. “I’ll just consume a single one this evening, Thirza. And half of them can be given to Isolde by me, can’t they? To me, the remaining half will taste doubly sweet if a portion is bestowed upon her. Thinking that I possess something to present to her brings me great joy.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
text: “To give the girl her due,” Thirza remarked after Nell retired to her gable, “selfishness isn’t in her nature. That pleases me, because a penny-pinching child is something I find particularly repulsive. Goodness, she arrived merely three weeks ago, yet it feels as though her presence here has been lifelong. The household seems unthinkable without her now. Now, refrain from giving me that triumphant expression, Obed. Such behavior is intolerable enough when a woman does it, but from a man, it cannot be borne at all. I am entirely ready to admit my satisfaction at agreeing to harbor the girl and my growing affection toward her, but do not taunt me with it, Obed Abernethy.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “IT’S time Nell was in to do her sewing,” declared Thirza, looking first toward the clock and then toward the yellow August afternoon, where the heat caused everything to drowse. “She remained playing with Isolde over thirty minutes longer than I permitted her to; and at present she’s seated out there on the woodpile speaking to Obed, nineteen to the dozen, despite knowing full well that she should be doing her chores. And naturally he’s attending to her like an utter ninny. I never witnessed a man so infatuated. The further she speaks and the stranger her words become, the more pleased he appears to be. Nell Harcourt, you come right in here this minute, do you hear me!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: Nell came rushing inside from the yard because of a succession of sharp taps against the west window, her gaze gleaming, her cheeks lightly tinged with a rose hue, and her unplaited hair flowing out after her like a radiant river.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Oh, Thirza,” she cried out, gasping for air, “a Sunday-school picnic is happening next week—taking place in Mr. Gorham Pullen’s field, very close to the lake of Glassy Waters. Also, Mrs. Superintendent Bell along with Mrs. Agatha Sowerby intend to prepare ice cream—imagine that, Thirza—ice cream! And, oh, Thirza, am I allowed to attend?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Nell, be so good as to check the time on the clock. At what hour did I instruct you to return?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “It is two o'clock—however, isn't the news regarding the picnic marvelous, Thirza? Am I allowed to go, please? Oh, a picnic is something I have never attended—picnics are things I have envisioned in my dreams, yet I have never—”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Indeed, I instructed you to arrive at two o'clock. Yet the time is now a quarter to three. I want an explanation for your disobedience, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Why, Thirza, I intended to, as fully as possible. But Larkrise is fascinating beyond what you can imagine. And besides, I needed to inform Obed regarding the picnic. Such a sympathetic listener, Obed is. May I please go?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “You must train yourself to withstand the attraction of Idle-whatever-its-name-is. If I order you to return at a specific hour, my intention is that exact hour, rather than thirty minutes after it. Furthermore, there is no need for you to pause and converse with understanding hearers along your path. Regarding the picnic, naturally your attendance is permitted. You attend Sunday school, so it is improbable that I would deny you permission to attend when every other young girl is attending.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “However—however,” stammered Nell, “Isolde claims that each person is required to bring a food basket. Thirza, you are aware that I am unable to cook, and—and—I am not as bothered about attending a picnic lacking puffed sleeves, yet being forced to attend without a basket would make me feel deeply ashamed. It has been haunting my thoughts from the moment Isolde mentioned it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Well, there is no need for it to weigh on your mind any further. I will prepare a basket of baked goods for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Oh, you sweet precious Thirza. Oh, you show me such kindness. Oh, I feel so deeply indebted to you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: Finishing her “ohs,” Nell threw herself into Thirza’s arms and enthusiastically kissed her sallow cheek. Thirza’s face had never before in her entire life been willingly touched by childish lips. Once more she felt the thrill of that unexpected, astonishingly sweet sensation. Nell’s sudden embrace secretly delighted her immensely, which was likely why she remarked curtly:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Now, now, forget about your affection nonsense. I would rather watch you obey my instructions precisely. Regarding culinary work, I intend to start instructing you in it one of these upcoming days. However, you are so scatterbrained, Nell, that I have postponed starting until I see whether you might settle down somewhat and become reliable. One must remain fully focused during food preparation instead of halting midway to allow one's mind to wander everywhere. Presently, fetch your needlework and finish your block prior to teatime.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Patchwork isn't to my liking,” Nell uttered sorrowfully, searching for her sewing basket and placing herself in front of a small pile of white and red diamond shapes while sighing. “Certain types of needlework would probably be pleasant, I believe; however, patchwork provides no room for imagination. One small seam merely follows another, and you appear to make no progress whatsoever. Still, I naturally prefer being Nell of Grey Shutters stitching patchwork over being Nell belonging to any different location with nothing else to do except play. Even so, I wish the hours passed as rapidly while stitching patches as they pass when I am playing together with Isolde. Oh, Thirza, we experience such wonderful times. I must supply the majority of the imagination, yet I am fully capable of managing that. Every other aspect of Isolde is utterly flawless. You are aware of that small plot of ground across the stream that extends upward between our property and that of Mr. Pembroke. Mr. William Bell owns it, and right inside the corner stands a small circle of white birch trees—a most romantic place, Thirza. Isolde and I maintain our playhouse at that location. Larkrise is the name we give it. Does that not sound like a poetical name? I can promise you that devising it took me a considerable amount of time. I lay awake for almost an entire night prior to creating it. Then, right as sleep was coming over me, it arrived like an inspiration. Isolde was delighted upon hearing it. Our house is arranged in an elegant fashion. Thirza, you must visit and look at it—will you not? Moss covers large stones that serve as our seats, and planks stretched between trees act as shelves. All our dishes are arranged upon them. Naturally, every piece is broken, yet imagining that they are intact is the simplest matter imaginable. One portion of a plate featuring a branch of yellow and red ivy is particularly magnificent. We store it inside the parlor, where we also keep the fairy glass. As lovely as a dream, that fairy glass is. Isolde discovered it outdoors in the forest behind their chicken coop. It is completely filled with rainbows—merely tiny young rainbows that are not yet fully grown—and Isolde's mother informed her that it had been broken away from a hanging lamp which they used to own. Nevertheless, imagining that the fairies misplaced it during a ball one night is lovely, so we name it the fairy glass. A table is going to be built for us by Obed. Oh, Reedmere is what we have called that small circular pond over inside Mr. Pembroke's field. That name came to me from the volume Isolde provided to me. Thirza, that volume was thrilling. Five lovers belonged to the heroine. A single one would satisfy me, would it not satisfy you? Very beautiful, she underwent immense suffering. Fainting was the easiest thing for her to do. Being capable of fainting is something I would adore, would you not like that, Thirza? Romantic is what it is. Yet, despite being so thin, I am actually extremely healthy. However, I think that I am becoming plumper. Do you not agree that I am? Every morning upon rising, I check my elbows to observe whether dimples are starting to form. A new dress featuring elbow sleeves is being fashioned for Isolde. She intends to wear it when attending the picnic. Oh, I truly trust the weather will be pleasant this coming Wednesday. Should something occur that hinders me from attending the picnic, I do not think I could bear the disappointment. Survival would likely happen, I suppose, but I am convinced a lifetime of grief would result. Attending one hundred picnics during future years would not count; missing this specific one could not be compensated for by them. Boats are to be present on the Lake of Glassy Waters—along with ice cream, as I previously mentioned to you. Ice cream has never been tasted by me. What it tasted like was something Isolde attempted to describe, but my guess is that ice cream belongs to those matters that lie outside imagination.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Nell, your speech has continued without interruption for ten minutes according to the clock,” Thirza stated. “Now, merely to satisfy my curiosity, discover whether you are able to remain silent for an equal duration of time.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: Nell remained silent as requested. However, during the remainder of the week, picnics filled her conversation, her thoughts, and her dreams. When rain fell on Saturday, she grew so terribly agitated fearing the downpour might persist up to and through Wednesday that Thirza forced her to stitch one more patchwork square to calm her nerves.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: While returning home from church on Sunday, Nell confessed to Thirza that an actual chill of excitement swept over her entire body as the pulpit minister gave notice of the picnic.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “A shiver ran along my spine, Thirza! Until that moment, I doubt I had truly trusted that a picnic would genuinely take place. I had been terrified that it was merely a figment of my imagination. However, once a minister announces something from the pulpit, you are forced to accept it as real.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Nell, you place far too much importance on things,” Thirza stated, sighing. “I fear that life holds a great number of disappointments for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Oh, Thirza, anticipating events accounts for half of their enjoyment,” cried Nell. “The items themselves might elude you; yet you cannot be deprived of the delight of anticipating them. It is stated by Mrs. Sowerby, ‘Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.’ However, my belief is that anticipating nothing would prove more unpleasant than experiencing disappointment.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: Thirza had put on her amethyst brooch for church that day, just like she always did. To go to church without her amethyst brooch was something Thirza never did. Omitting it would have seemed to her almost blasphemous—just as improper as neglecting to bring her Bible or her collection dime. Thirza prized that amethyst brooch above all her other belongings. It had been presented to her mother by an uncle who was a sailor, and her mother had subsequently left it to Thirza. The piece was a traditional oval shape, housing a woven lock of her mother's hair and framed by an outer ring of exceptionally high-quality amethysts. Because she was unversed in gemology, Thirza failed to appreciate just how exquisite those amethysts truly were; nevertheless, she found them gorgeous and remained delightfully aware of their purple glow resting at her neck, just above her best brown satin gown, despite its being out of her line of sight.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: When Nell had initially laid eyes on that brooch, she was struck with thrilled wonder.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
text: “Oh, Thirza, this pin is absolutely exquisite. Having it pinned on would make it impossible for me to focus on the prayers or the sermon, though I have no idea how you manage. I know for a fact I would fail. To me, amethysts are simply charming. They match the image I used to hold of diamonds. Way back, prior to ever laying eyes on a real diamond, I encountered them in a book and attempted to picture their appearance. My expectation was that they were gorgeous, shining violet gems. My disappointment was so great that tears came when I eventually glimpsed an actual diamond set in a woman’s ring. Naturally, its beauty was undeniable, yet it failed to match my vision of a diamond. Would you allow me to have the pin in my hand for just a moment, Thirza? Could amethysts possibly represent the spirits of virtuous violets?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: UPON the evening of Monday preceding the picnic, Thirza emerged from her room displaying a distressed expression.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell,” she uttered to the tiny individual, who was removing peas from their pods beside the immaculate table while performing “Nelly of the Hazel Dell” with an energy and feeling that reflected well on Isolde’s instruction, “did you notice my amethyst brooch anywhere? I believed I placed it into my pincushion upon returning home from church last night, but it is nowhere to be found.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “I—I observed it earlier today while you were absent at the Aid Society,” Nell remarked, somewhat deliberately. “As I was walking by your door, I noticed it resting on the cushion, which prompted me to step inside to examine it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Was it touched by you?” Thirza asked severely.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Y-e-e-s,” Nell conceded, “I lifted it and attached it to my breast merely to observe the appearance it would make.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “You were not supposed to act in such a manner. Meddling is extremely improper for a young girl. To begin with, you ought not to have entered my room, and furthermore, you ought not to have handled a brooch that was not yours. Where did you leave it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Oh, I placed it on top of the bureau again. It was on me for less than a minute. Honestly, interfering wasn't my intention, Thirza. Entering and putting on the brooch didn't strike me as forbidden; however, I now recognize my mistake, and I promise not to repeat it. I have that single virtue. A bad deed is something I never commit a second time.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “It wasn't returned by you,” Thirza said. “The bureau doesn't have that brooch anywhere on it. Nell, you have taken it out or done something else to it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Indeed I returned it,” Nell stated swiftly—with impudence, in Thirza’s view. “I cannot recall with certainty if I thrust it into the pincushion or placed it inside the porcelain dish. Nevertheless, I am absolutely sure that I returned it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “I will return and check once more,” Thirza said, deciding to be fair. “Should you have returned that brooch, it remains in that place. Should it be absent, I will be certain you failed to do so, nothing more!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Thirza proceeded to her bedroom and conducted an exhaustive hunt, searching not merely across the bureau but throughout all the additional spots where she imagined the brooch could conceivably be. She was unable to discover it, so she went back into the kitchen.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell, the brooch has disappeared. You admitted yourself that you were the final person who touched it. Now, where did you put it? Give me the true story immediately. Did you carry it outside and drop it?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “No, I didn’t,” Nell said with gravity, directly returning the furious look from Thirza. “The brooch was never taken from your room by me, and that is a fact, even were I to be brought to the block on account of it—even though I don’t really know what a block might be. So that is that, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Although Nell’s “so there” had been uttered merely to stress her claim, it was interpreted by Thirza as a sign of rebellion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell, my belief is that you are speaking untruthfully to me,” she stated with sharpness. “My certainty is that you are. Look here, refrain from speaking further unless your intention is to disclose the entire truth. Retire to your chamber and remain within it until your readiness to admit everything arrives.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Shall I carry the peas along?” Nell inquired submissively.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “No, I am going to complete shelling them on my own. Follow my instructions.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: After Nell left, Thirza performed her nightly chores feeling exceptionally unsettled. The fate of her precious brooch deeply troubled her. Had Nell perhaps dropped it somewhere? It seemed terribly deceitful for the young girl to disclaim taking the item, especially since it was blatantly obvious that she had done so. Furthermore, she had maintained such an unguilty expression while doing it!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “I do not know what I would not rather have occurred,” Thirza reflected, while she anxiously removed the peas from their pods. “Naturally, I do not believe she intended to commit a theft or anything of that sort. She has simply removed it to play with or to assist that imagination she has. It is obvious she took it, because nobody has been inside that room since she occupied it, according to her own account, until my visit this evening. And there is nothing more certain than that the brooch is missing. My assumption is that she lost it and fears admitting it out of dread of punishment. Contemplating that she utters lies is a terrible thing. That is a much worse matter than her outburst of anger. Carrying the responsibility of a child in your home whom you are unable to trust is fearful. What she has exhibited is deceit and dishonesty. I assert that I am more upset over that than over the brooch. Had she merely spoken the truth regarding it, I would not care nearly as much.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: At various points over the course of the evening, Thirza returned to her room to look for the brooch, yet she could not locate it. Going to the east gable at bedtime yielded nothing either. Even though Nell continuously claimed to have no knowledge of the brooch, Thirza merely became even more certain of her guilt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: When the next morning arrived, she related the narrative to Obed. Obed found himself mystified and bewildered; although he was unable to abandon his belief in Nell so rapidly, he was forced to concede that the situation pointed toward her guilt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Is there any chance it dropped in back of the bureau?” represented his sole possible idea.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “I’ve shifted the bureau, removed the drawers, and searched through every single crevice,” Thirza answered with certainty. “The brooch has disappeared, taken by that child who then lied regarding it. That is the straightforward, unpleasant fact, Obed Abernethy, and we had better confront it squarely.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “So, how do you plan to handle this?” asked Obed in a dejected manner, privately relieved that Thirza, rather than himself, was forced to manage the circumstances. On this occasion, he possessed no wish to meddle.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Until she confesses, she’ll stay in her room,” Thirza said grimly, recalling how well this strategy had worked in the previous instance. “We’ll see after that. If she’ll just say where she took the brooch, maybe we’ll be able to find it; but regardless, Obed, she’ll have to be severely punished.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Well now, she will need to be punished by you,” said Obed, as he reached toward his hat. “Remember that I am not involved in this. You were the one who warned me away.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Abandonment was all that Thirza felt. Consulting Mrs. Sowerby for counsel was not even an option for her. Carrying an extremely grave expression, she walked up to the east gable, and she departed from it bearing an expression that was graver yet. Confessing was something Nell firmly declined to do. That she had not taken the brooch was what she continued to maintain. The youngster had clearly been weeping, inducing a sharp feeling of compassion in Thirza, though she forcefully held it back. Once night arrived, she found herself, to use her own words, “beat out.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “You will remain inside this room until you admit it, Nell. Make up your mind to that,” she said firmly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “However, Thirza, the picnic takes place tomorrow,” Nell shouted. “Surely you will not prevent me from attending that? You will allow me to leave for just the afternoon, will you not? Following that, I will remain in this place with pleasure for any length of time you desire. Nevertheless, attending the picnic is something I must do.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “You will not attend picnics or any other places prior to confessing, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Oh, Thirza,” Nell gasped.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: However, Thirza had departed and closed the door.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: The morning of Wednesday broke with a brightness and beauty that seemed tailored specifically for the outing. Surrounding Grey Shutters, birds trilled their songs; within the garden, the Madonna lilies released fragrance that swept through every doorway and window on invisible breezes, drifting like blessing spirits across the hallways and chambers. Down in the hollow, the birches swayed their hands merrily, as though waiting for the customary morning hello Nell offered from the eastern gable. However, Nell was absent from her window. Upon bringing her breakfast upstairs, Thirza discovered the girl perched stiffly atop her bed, white-faced and determined, her lips pressed firmly together and her eyes shining.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Thirza, I’m ready to confess.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Ah!” Set down by Thirza was her tray. Yet another time her approach proved effective; nevertheless, her accomplishment brought her deep bitterness. “Let me hear what you have to say then, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “I took the amethyst brooch,” Nell stated, resembling someone reciting a memorized lesson. “Just like you described, I took it. Stealing it was not my intention upon entering. However, Thirza, once I fastened it onto my chest, it appeared so lovely that a powerful temptation conquered me. I pictured the utter thrill of bringing it along to Larkrise while pretending to be the Lady Lucinda Fitzgerald. Possessing an authentic amethyst brooch would make pretending to be the Lady Lucinda far simpler. Although Isolde and I craft necklaces using roseberries, how can roseberries compare with amethysts? Consequently, I stole the brooch. My intention was to return it prior to your arrival back home. To make the journey last longer, I traveled the entire distance by way of the road. While crossing the bridge spanning the Lake of Glassy Waters, I removed the brooch so that I might view it once more. Oh, the way it gleamed in the sun! Then, as I bent over the bridge, it simply slid right out of my fingers—like this—and plunged down—down—down, gleaming with purple flashes, until it submerged eternally under the Lake of Glassy Waters. And Thirza, that is the most thorough confession I am capable of making.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: A fresh wave of furious rage welled up in Thirza's heart. The young girl had appropriated and misplaced her cherished amethyst brooch, yet she remained seated there placidly detailing the particulars of the incident, showing no obvious remorse or regret whatsoever.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell, this is awful,” she remarked, attempting to keep her voice steady. “No girl I have ever known of is as thoroughly bad as you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Yes, I believe I am,” Nell concurred placidly. “And I am aware that I must receive punishment. Performing that punishment will be your responsibility, Thirza. Won’t you kindly execute it immediately, as I wish to attend the picnic without any worries weigh upon me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “A picnic, of all things! Today will bring no picnic for you, Nell Harcourt. This is to be your penalty. Even so, it fails to be anywhere near harsh enough considering your actions!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Refuse to attend the outing!” Nell leaped up and seized the hand of Thirza. “Yet your word was given that I could! Oh, Thirza, attending the outing is essential for me. My admission was made for that reason. Subject me to any penalty except that one. Oh, Thirza, I beg you, I beg you, permit me to attend the outing. Consider the ice cream! As far as you are aware, another opportunity to sample ice cream might never come my way.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Without emotion, Thirza unclasped the hands of Nell that were holding onto her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “There is no need to beg, Nell. That’s final, and you are not attending the picnic. No, do not say a single word.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Nell understood that Thirza could not be persuaded. Joining her hands, she uttered a sharp scream, after which she threw herself face down upon the bed, weeping and twisting about in a complete surrender to grief and frustration.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Goodness gracious!” Thirza puffed as she hurried out of the chamber. “It seems to me that the girl has lost her mind. A sane youth wouldn't act in the manner that she exhibits. If her mind is intact, her wickedness knows no bounds. Goodness me, my fear is that Agatha held the correct view all along. Nevertheless, having committed myself to this course, I shall not turn back.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: It was a gloomy morning. Thirza cleaned with intensity, scouring the shelves of the dairy and the porch floor whenever no other tasks presented themselves. Thirza required that labor, though it was unnecessary for either the porch or the shelves. After that, she stepped outside and cleared the yard with a rake.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: As soon as dinner was prepared, she walked over to the staircase to summon Nell. Over the banisters, a face marked with tears emerged, carrying a tragic expression.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell, come down and eat your dinner.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Thirza, I don’t want any dinner,” Nell said through her sobs. “Eating anything would be impossible for me. My heart has been broken. I anticipate that you will feel remorse of conscience for breaking it someday, Thirza, yet I forgive you. When that moment arrives, remember that I forgive you. However, please do not request that I eat anything, particularly boiled pork and greens. When a person is experiencing affliction, boiled pork and greens are so unromantic.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Feeling exasperated, Thirza went back to the kitchen and shared her story of distress with Obed, who was rendered a wretched individual due to being torn between his devotion to justice and his illicit compassion for Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Indeed, Thirza, taking the brooch was wrong of her, as was lying concerning it,” he conceded, gazing sorrowfully at his portion of mundane pork and vegetables as though he shared Nell’s view that such sustenance was inappropriate for emotional emergencies, “yet she is merely a child—and such a captivating child. Is it not rather harsh, in your opinion, to forbid her attending the outing when she desires it so greatly?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Obed Abernethy, my mind is blown by your behavior. My belief is that I have treated her with far too much leniency. Furthermore, she does not seem to grasp the extent of her wickedness whatsoever—that remains my primary concern. Had she truly experienced remorse, the situation would not prove as severe. Nor do you appear to comprehend it either; you are constantly devising justifications for her in your mind—I am able to perceive that.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Well now, she is a tiny thing,” Obed weakly repeated. “And Thirza, you ought to make allowances. You are aware that she has not received any upbringing.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Well, it’s happening to her right now,” Thirza replied.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Obed was struck mute by the reply, even though he remained unpersuaded. A profound gloom hung over that dinner. Tobias Buote, the hired boy, provided the sole bright spot, yet Thirza viewed his happy demeanor as a direct offense to her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Having completed the washing of her dishes, the setting of her bread sponge, and the feeding of her hens, Thirza recalled seeing a little tear in her finest black lace shawl upon removing it on Monday afternoon after coming home from the Ladies’ Aid.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: She intended to travel and repair it. Within a box inside her trunk rested the shawl. When Thirza extracted it, light from the sun, penetrating the dense vines grouped around the window, shone against an object trapped in the shawl—an object that gleamed and twinkled with facets of violet radiance. With a gasp, Thirza lunged for it. Suspended from a lace thread by its clasp, it was the amethyst brooch!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Dear life and heart,” Thirza uttered expressionlessly, “what is the meaning of this? My brooch, which I believed was resting at the base of Pembroke’s pond, is right here unharmed. What was that girl’s reason for claiming she stole it and misplaced it? I assert that Grey Shutters must be under a spell. It comes back to me now that upon removing my shawl Monday afternoon, I placed it upon the bureau briefly. It seems the brooch became entangled in it in some way. Well!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: With the brooch in her possession, Thirza made her way to the east gable. Having exhausted her tears, Nell sat beside the window in a state of dejection.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell Harcourt,” Thirza uttered in a serious tone, “my brooch was merely attached to my black lace shawl when I discovered it just now. Now, I desire an explanation for the rambling story you recounted to me earlier today.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Why, you told me I’d be held here until a confession was made,” Nell answered tiredly, “and therefore I chose to confess since reaching the picnic was something I had to do. Subsequent to going to bed last night, I devised a confession, making it just as engaging as possible. Furthermore, I repeated it repeatedly to ensure it remained in my memory. However, you refused to allow my attendance at the picnic anyway, meaning every bit of my effort went to waste.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Thirza could not help laughing. Her conscience, however, stung her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Nell, you really are something else! However, I was mistaken—I recognize that this moment. Having never known you to lie, I ought not to have disbelieved what you said. To be sure, admitting to something you were guiltless of was not correct—doing that was extremely wrong. Yet my actions forced you into it. Therefore, provided that you pardon me, Nell, I will pardon you, and we will begin anew on equal footing. Furthermore, prepare yourself now for the picnic.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: Nell launched upward with the speed of a rocket.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Oh, Thirza, is it not past the time?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “No, the time is merely two o'clock. Their assembly will hardly have begun, and tea will not be served for another hour. Clean your face, brush your hair, and dress in your gingham. I am going to pack a basket on your behalf. We have an abundance of baked goods in the dwelling. Furthermore, I will have Tobias harness the sorrel horse to take you down to the location of the picnic.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Oh, Thirza,” Nell cried out, rushing over to the washstand. “A mere five minutes back I felt so wretched that I wished I had not been born, but at this moment I would not trade positions with an angel!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: When night fell, Nell went back to Grey Shutters utterly content and entirely exhausted, experiencing an indescribable condition of beatitude.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “Oh, Thirza, my time was absolutely scrumptious. Today I picked up that brand-new word, scrumptious. Mary Alice Bell was using it when I overheard her. Doesn't it convey a lot? All of it was delightful. A wonderful tea was served to us, after which Mr. Gorham Pullen brought everyone out rowing on the Lake of Glassy Waters, taking six people per trip. Then Odette Pullen almost tumbled into the water. As she reached far out to gather water lilies, Mr. Pullen managed to grab her sash right at the critical moment, preventing her from falling in and likely drowning. My preference would have been for that to happen to me. Being almost drowned would have made for such a romantic adventure. What an exciting story it would make to relate. Plus, there was ice cream for us. That ice cream is beyond my ability to depict with words. Thirza, I guarantee you that it was divine.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: That night, while working on her stocking basket, Thirza recounted the entire tale to Obed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession
text: “I am ready to admit my error,” she finished frankly, “yet I have gained some wisdom. Thinking about the ‘confession’ Nell made brings a laugh to me, even if I ought not to smile since it truly amounted to an untruth. Somehow, though, it feels less terrible than the alternative would have proved, and regardless, the blame for it lies with me. Certain sides of that child are difficult to comprehend. Nevertheless, my faith remains that she will turn out fine in the end. One fact is beyond doubt, however: any home containing her will never suffer from boredom.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “WHAT a magnificent day!” Nell remarked, taking a deep breath. “Is it not wonderful merely to exist on such a day? My heart goes out to the unborn who are absent from it. Naturally, they might experience fine days, but this specific one is forever out of their reach. Furthermore, having a route to school that is so delightful makes it even more magnificent, does it not?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Traveling this way is much pleasant than taking the road, which is very dusty and warm,” Isolde remarked pragmatically, glancing inside her lunch basket while calculating in her head how many bites every girl would get if the trio of succulent, delicious raspberry tarts sitting inside were shared among ten girls.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: The young female students at Brierley school invariably combined their mid-day meals, meaning that if a girl consumed three raspberry tarts completely by herself, or merely split them with her closest friend, she would be perpetually labeled as “awful mean” by the others. However, splitting those tarts between ten girls resulted in a portion that merely teased your appetite.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: The route that Nell and Isolde took to school was lovely. Nell felt that it was impossible even to imagine a better walk to and from school than the one she shared with Isolde. Taking the main road would have lacked romance completely; conversely, traveling via Linger Lane, Reedmere, Primrose Dell, and the Aspen Path was the very definition of romance.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Below the orchard at Grey Shutters, Linger Lane commenced its course, extending deep into the forest until it reached the edge of the Abernethy farm. The cattle were driven along this path to the rear field, and during the winter season, timber was transported back by it. Prior to completing a month at Grey Shutters, Nell had bestowed the name Linger Lane upon it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “It isn't as if lovers actually stroll along it,” she clarified to Thirza, “yet Isolde and I happen to be enjoying an absolutely marvelous novel that features a Linger Lane. Because of that, we wish to possess one as well. Also, the name possesses a great deal of charm, wouldn't you agree? It is so full of romance! You see, we are unable to picture the lovers inside it. My fondness for that lane stems from the fact that you may speak your thoughts openly there and not have people brand you as insane.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Setting off by herself when morning came, Nell traveled along Linger Lane until she reached the brook. Isolde joined her at this spot, and together the two young girls continued traveling up the lane beneath a green canopy of maples—“maples are such friendly trees,” Nell remarked; “they constantly rustle and whisper in your ear”—before arriving at a wooden bridge. Leaving the lane behind, they proceeded across Mr. Pembroke’s back field and traveled past Reedmere. Lying past Reedmere was Primrose Dell—a small, verdant hollow shaded by Mr. Andrew Bell’s large forest. “Naturally, no violets grow there at present,” Nell mentioned to Thirza, “yet Isolde claims millions bloom during springtime. Oh, Thirza, isn't it easy to picture them right before your eyes? It truly makes me gasp. I gave it the name Primrose Dell.
