Isolde remarks that no one surpasses me when it comes to devising imaginative names for locations. Having a talent for something is wonderful, wouldn't you say? However, Isolde chose the name for the Aspen Path. Because she wished to, I permitted her; nevertheless, I know I could have devised a phrase more artistic than just Aspen Path. Anyone is capable of inventing a title of that sort. Even so, the Aspen Path ranks among the most lovely spots anywhere, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Indeed it was. When others chanced upon it, their opinion matched Nell’s. That small, pinched, snaking track sloped downward across a lengthy hill, passing directly through Mr. Bell’s woods, a place where the sunlight filtered through numerous green canopies until it matched the perfection found at the center of a diamond. Tall, graceful birches boasting pale trunks lined every inch of its borders; a dense growth of ferns, starflowers, wild lilies-of-the-valley, and bright red clumps of pigeonberries stretched beside it; moreover, a pleasing aromatic scent continually filled the atmosphere alongside avian melodies and the gentle rustle and chuckle of breeze moving through the upper branches. Occasionally, a calm observer could spot a rabbit darting over the dirt—an occurrence that took place very rarely when Nell and Isolde were present. Reaching the valley bottom, the trail emerged onto the primary thoroughfare, leaving only the pine-covered incline to climb before reaching the school.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: A whitewashed structure featuring low eaves and broad windows housed the Brierley school, containing comfortable, sturdy, old-fashioned desks on the inside that opened and closed, their lids entirely covered in carvings of initials and hieroglyphics from three generations of pupils. Positioned back from the road, the schoolhouse had a dark fir wood to its rear alongside a stream where every child placed their milk bottles during the morning so they would remain cold and fresh through lunchtime.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: With numerous hidden anxieties, Thirza had watched Nell depart for school on the first of September. Nell was a very strange girl. In what way would she interact with the rest of the children? And by what possible means could she succeed in keeping quiet throughout the time class was in session?

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Matters proceeded more favorably than Thirza had anticipated, nevertheless. Nell returned to the house that night in great delight.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I believe this school will suit me,” she declared. “However, I do not hold a high opinion of the teacher. He continuously twirls his mustache and casts romantic glances toward Sukey Pullen. Sukey is an adult, as you are aware. Her age is sixteen, and she is preparing for the Regent’s Academy entrance exam in Port Marlow for the coming year. Tillie Gammon claims that the teacher is hopelessly in love with her. Her skin is lovely, her brown hair is curly, and her hairstyle is arranged so stylishly. Her spot is at the back on the long bench, and he spends the majority of his time seated there as well—claiming it is to clarify her coursework. Nevertheless, Opal Pettigrew claims she caught him scribbling a message on her slate, which made Sukey flush bright red and laugh nervously upon reading it; and Opal Pettigrew claims she doubts that it pertained to the coursework at all.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nell Harcourt, stop speaking of your teacher like that this instant,” Thirza reprimanded. “Attending school to find fault with the master is not why you are there. Surely he has knowledge to impart, and your duty is to absorb it. Furthermore, get it into your head immediately that bringing home gossip regarding him is forbidden. Such behavior will receive no support from me. Were you well-behaved, I trust?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Indeed I was,” said Nell comfortably. “It was not as difficult as you might think, either. I share a seat with Isolde. Positioned right beside the window, our seat lets us look down at the Lake of Glassy Waters. The school contains many nice girls, and we had scrumptious fun playing during dinnertime. Having many little girls to play with is so nice. However, I naturally like Isolde best and always will. I adore Isolde. I am dreadfully far behind everyone else. Everyone else is in the fifth book while I am merely in the fourth. I feel as though it is somewhat of a disgrace. Nevertheless, not a single one of them possesses an imagination like mine, a fact I quickly discovered. Today, we had reading, geography, Canadian history, and dictation. Mr. Pidgeon stated that my spelling was disgraceful, holding up my slate, all covered in marks, so that everyone could see. Thirza, I felt so mortified; I think he could have shown more politeness to a stranger. An apple was given to me by Opal Pettigrew, and Sophia Mott lent me a lovely pink card bearing the words ‘May I see you home?’. I must return it to her tomorrow. Furthermore, Tillie Gammon permitted me to wear her bead ring for the entire afternoon. May I take a few of those pearl beads from the old pincushion in the garret so I can craft a ring for myself? And oh, Thirza, Odette Pullen disclosed to me that Posy MacKinnon told her she overheard Sukey Pullen tell Sara Pettigrew that my nose was very pretty. Thirza, that marks the very first compliment I have ever received in my life, and the strange feeling it imparted to me is beyond your imagination. Thirza, do I truly possess a pretty nose? I know that you will speak the truth to me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Your nose is fine as it is,” Thirza replied abruptly. In truth, she considered Nell’s nose to be exceptionally attractive; however, she was determined not to let her know that.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Three weeks had passed since that time, with everything proceeding without a hitch up to this point. Now, on a cool September morning, Isolde and Nell were walking briskly and cheerfully along the Aspen Path, being a pair of the most joyful young girls in Brierley.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I suppose Hugh Carrow is going to be at school today,” Isolde remarked. “All summer long he’s been over in New Brunswick visiting his cousins, and Saturday night was when he finally returned home. Nell, he’s terribly handsome. And the way he teases the girls is just awful. He simply makes our lives a misery.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Isolde’s tone of voice suggested that she was somewhat fond of having her life plagued out of her instead of the alternative.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Hugh Carrow?” Nell asked. “Isn’t he the one whose name is inscribed on the wall of the porch alongside Julia Bell’s, with a large ‘Take Notice’ above them both?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Yes,” Isolde replied, jerking her head back, “however, it is my belief that Julia Bell is not favored by him to such a high degree. I have listened to him state that he used her freckles to learn the multiplication table.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Oh, do not mention freckles to me,” begged Nell. “When I have such a quantity, it lacks delicacy. However, I truly believe that scribbling notices regarding the boys and girls on the wall is the most ridiculous thing possible. I would simply love to watch anyone have the courage to write my name alongside a boy’s. Not, naturally,” she was quick to insert, “that anyone ever would.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Nell let out a sigh. Having her name recorded was something she preferred to avoid. Even so, realizing that she faced no risk at all of it happening felt somewhat humiliating.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nonsense,” stated Isolde, the individual whose dark eyes and shiny hair had so thoroughly disrupted the emotions of Brierley schoolboys that her name was displayed in six different take-notices on the porch walls. “A joke is all it is intended to be. And you shouldn't feel so certain that a time will never come when your name is scribbled somewhere. Wilfred Mott is completely infatuated with you. It was to his mother—take note, his mother—that he declared you were the cleverest female student in the whole school. Having that said about you surpasses being attractive.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “It is not, though,” Nell remarked, being entirely feminine. “Being pretty is what I would choose over being clever. Also, Wilfred Mott is someone I detest, as I cannot tolerate a boy whose eyes goggle. Isolde Pembroke, I would be permanently ruined if my name were written alongside his by anyone. Even so, remaining at the top of one's class is a pleasant thing.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Following this, Hugh will join your class,” Isolde remarked, “and I can assure you that he is accustomed to leading his class. Despite being almost fourteen, he is merely in the fourth book. Four years back, his father fell ill and was forced to travel to Alberta for his well-being, taking Hugh along. Their stay lasted three years, during which Hughie scarcely attended school at all prior to their return. Nell, maintaining your position at the top will not be nearly as simple now.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I’m happy,” Nell stated rapidly. “Being at the top of a class of young children who are only nine or ten years old wouldn't truly make me feel proud. Yesterday, I moved up to the head by spelling ‘ebullition.’ Flossie Tulk was at the top, and I'm telling you, she sneaked a look at her book. Mr. Pidgeon missed it—his eyes were on Sukey Pullen—however, I caught her. I simply threw her an icy, contemptuous glance, causing her to turn as red as a beetroot, and she ended up spelling it incorrectly anyway.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Every one of those Tulk girls acts dishonestly,” Isolde remarked with irritation while they scaled the main road's fence. “Yesterday, Tibby Tulk literally set her milk bottle where mine belonged in the brook. Can you imagine? Now I refuse to talk to her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: As Mr. Pidgeon listened to Sukey Pullen recite her Latin from the rear of the classroom, Isolde leaned over to Nell and murmured, “Directly across the aisle from you sits Hugh Carrow, Nell. Take a glance at him and tell me whether you find him attractive.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Nell observed in response. She possessed an excellent opportunity for this, as the mentioned Hugh Carrow was fully occupied with quietly attaching the lengthy blonde plait belonging to Opal Pettigrew, who was seated before him, to her chair's back. He was a high-statured youth, possessing wavy chestnut hair, mischievous light-brown eyes, and a mouth contorted into a mocking grin. Before long, Opal Pettigrew rose abruptly to bring an arithmetic problem to the teacher; she collapsed back onto her chair with a faint scream, under the impression that her hair had been yanked out at the roots. All the students gazed in her direction and Mr. Pidgeon stared with such severity that Opal started weeping. Hugh had swiftly hidden the pin and was reading his history lesson with an utterly serious expression; however, once the disturbance quieted down, he caught Nell's eye and winked with boundless humor.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “In my opinion, your Hugh Carrow has good looks,” Nell admitted to Isolde, “yet I find his behavior quite daring. Winking at an unfamiliar girl violates proper etiquette.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: However, real events did not truly start unfolding until afternoon arrived.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Mr. Pidgeon had returned to the corner where he was clarifying an algebraic problem for Sukey Pullen, while the remaining students were behaving largely as they liked by consuming green apples, speaking softly, sketching images on their slates, and steering crickets attached to strings along the aisle. Hugh Carrow was attempting to gain Nell Harcourt’s attention without any success, since Nell was then completely unaware not merely of the presence of Hugh Carrow, but of all the other pupils within Brierley school as well. Supporting her chin with her hands while resting her eyes on the small blue view of the Lake of Glassy Waters visible through the west window, she had drifted into a magnificent realm of fantasy, perceiving and witnessing only her own extraordinary imaginations.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: It was not Hugh Carrow’s habit to exert himself to attract a girl's gaze only to be unsuccessful. That red-haired Harcourt girl, who possessed the small pointed chin along with the large eyes that differed from those of every other girl at Brierley school, ought to look at him.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Hugh extended his arm over the space between their seats, took hold of the tip of Nell’s lengthy crimson plait, stretched it as far as his arm could reach, and uttered in an intense whisper:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Carrots! Carrots!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: At that point, Nell glared at him intensely!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: She went beyond merely gazing. Rising abruptly to her feet, she saw her brilliant imaginations shattered beyond repair. From eyes where a furious gleaming was rapidly drowned by tears of matching rage, she shot a single wrathful look toward Hugh.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “You vile, spiteful youth!” she cried out with deep emotion. “How could you!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: And next—thwack! bringing her slate down upon Hugh’s head, Nell broke it—the slate, not the head—straight in two.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: A commotion was always welcomed at Brierley school. The present one proved particularly delicious. "Oh," everyone uttered with scandalized pleasure. A gasp came from Isolde. Prone to hysteria, Opal Pettigrew started weeping. His mouth agape at the scene, Tommy Mott allowed his collection of crickets to get away from him completely.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Mr. Pidgeon marched down the aisle, placing his hand firmly upon the shoulder of Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nell Harcourt, what is the meaning of this?” he asked in an angry tone. Nell made no reply. Expecting her to admit in front of the entire school that someone had called her “carrots” was asking too much of flesh and blood. Hugh was the one who bravely spoke out.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Mr. Pidgeon, the blame belongs to me because I provoked her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Hugh was completely ignored by Mr. Pidgeon.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “It grieves me to observe a student under my instruction showing this kind of rage and this sort of revengeful attitude,” he remarked with grave gravity, as though just having him as a teacher should eradicate every bad impulse from the minds of young flawed human beings. “Nell, proceed to the dais before the blackboard and remain standing there throughout the remainder of the day.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: A beating would have been vastly favored by Nell over this penalty, which made her tender soul shudder as if struck by a whip. She complied, her countenance pale and rigid. Above her head, Mr. Pidgeon utilized a piece of chalk to write upon the blackboard.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Ann Harcourt possesses an extremely poor temper. Ann Harcourt is required to learn temper control,” and subsequently uttered the sentence aloud so it would be intelligible even to the primer class, who were unable to read handwriting.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Nell remained standing there with that inscription over her head for the remainder of the afternoon. She neither wept nor bowed her head. The rage in her heart remained too intense for such reactions, supporting her through the full anguish of her shame. With a furious stare and cheeks flushed with passion, she faced Isolde’s compassionate look, Wilfred Mott’s angry nods, and Flossie Tulk’s spiteful grins with equal defiance. Regarding Hugh Carrow, she refused to so much as glance in his direction. Never again would she cast her eyes upon him! Never again would she utter a word to him!!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: As soon as classes ended, Nell walked out, holding her red-haired head erect. At the doorway to the porch, Hugh Carrow attempted to block her path.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nell, I’m terribly apologetic about mocking your hair,” he murmured remorsefully. “Truly I am. Please don’t stay angry forever.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Nell brushed past haughtily, failing to glance at him or show any indication that she had heard. “Oh how could you, Nell?” whispered Isolde while they walked along the road, her tone blending slight rebuke with a degree of wonder. Isolde believed that it would have been impossible for her to turn down Hugh’s entreaty.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Hugh Carrow is someone I will never forgive,” Nell declared with conviction. “Furthermore, my name was written minus the final e by Mr. Pidgeon as well. Isolde, the iron has pierced my very soul.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: While Isolde was completely ignorant of Nell’s meaning, she nevertheless grasped that it signified a dreadful thing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “You must not be upset by Hugh teasing you about your hair,” she stated to comfort me. “Really, he teases every single girl. He makes jokes about mine on account of it being so black. He has named me a crow twelve times; and prior to this, I also have not known him to offer an apology for anything.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “It is quite a distinct matter to be named a crow compared to being named carrots,” Nell stated solemnly. “My feelings have been injured most agonizingly by Hugh Carrow, Isolde.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: The situation perhaps could have settled down without further agony had no additional events occurred. However, once incidents commence, they tend to persist.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Students from Brierley frequently passed the midday break collecting gum within the spruce wood belonging to Mr. Bell, located beyond the hill and past his large pasture. This vantage point allowed them to watch the residence of Eben Duckett, the location of the master's lodgings. As soon as Mr. Pidgeon was observed stepping out of it, a race toward the schoolhouse commenced; however, because that journey measured roughly thrice the length of Mr. Duckett’s lane, reaching the destination out of breath and panting approximately three minutes after the time limit was a common occurrence.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: During the next day, Mr. Pidgeon had a sudden impulse to enforce discipline, declaring prior to his departure for dinner at home that he anticipated every student would be occupying their assigned seat upon his comeback. A penalty would be given to anybody arriving after the set time.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: As was their habit, every boy and a portion of the girls headed to Mr. Bell’s spruce grove, thoroughly purposing to remain just until they could “pick a chew.” Nevertheless, spruce groves hold temptation and yellow gum nuts possess charm; they gathered, lingered, and wandered; and, as was customary, what first awakened them to how quickly time had passed was Jimmy Glover yelling “Master’s coming” while perched atop an ancient, patriarchal spruce.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Those girls who were already on the ground set off first, succeeding in getting to the schoolhouse just in time with not a single second to spare. The boys, needing to scramble down from the trees in a hurry, were behind them; while Nell, who had been strolling joyfully at the distant end of the grove instead of gathering gum, buried up to her waist in the bracken, quietly singing to herself, wearing a crown of rice lilies in her hair like a wild spirit of the shaded woods, was the very last. Nevertheless, Nell was able to run as fast as a deer; run she indeed did, producing the mischievous outcome of catching up with the boys at the entrance and being carried into the schoolhouse right in the middle of them precisely when Mr. Pidgeon was hanging up his hat.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: The fleeting impulse for reform that had seized Mr. Pidgeon had passed; he preferred not to go through the trouble of disciplining twelve students; nevertheless, action was required to preserve his reputation, which led him to search for a victim, discovering one in Nell, who had slumped into her chair, breathless, while an overlooked garland of lilies dangled sideways above a single ear, bestowing upon her a remarkably untidy and jaunty air.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nell Harcourt, because you appear to take such pleasure in the presence of the boys, we will satisfy your desire for it later today,” he remarked with sarcasm. “Remove those blossoms from your hair and take a seat next to Hugh Carrow.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: A giggle came from the rest of the boys. Whitenings of compassion washed over Isolde as she pulled the wreath off Nell’s hair and gave her hand a squeeze. Turned seemingly to stone, Nell fixed her gaze upon the master.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nell, did you hear my words?” Mr. Pidgeon asked in a stern manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Indeed, sir,” Nell uttered unhurriedly, “however, I failed to assume that your intentions were genuine.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I assure you I did”—he maintained the mocking tone that every child, particularly Nell, detested. It stung an open wound. “Obey me at once.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Nell appeared momentarily on the verge of refusal. However, acknowledging the inevitability of the situation, she stood up proudly, walked over the aisle, took a seat next to Hugh Carrow, and hid her face within her arms upon the desk. Opal Pettigrew, catching a brief sight of her face while it descended, informed the other children on their way back from school that she had “acksually never seen anything like it—it was so white, with awful little red spots in it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: For Nell, this felt like the utter conclusion of everything. Being selected for disciplinary action out of twelve peers who shared identical guilt was terrible in itself; being forced to occupy a seat beside a boy was even worse, yet the fact that the male student was Hugh Carrow added an utterly intolerable level of offense to her existing misfortune. Nell was convinced that enduring this was beyond her capacity, and making an effort would serve no purpose. Shame, wrath, and degradation churned throughout her entire spirit.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Initially, the remaining students stared, murmured, laughed softly, and poked one another. However, because Nell refrained from raising her eyes and Hugh solved math problems as though his entire spirit was concentrated solely on them, the pupils shortly went back to their individual work, leaving Nell ignored. When the history lesson was summoned by Mr. Pidgeon, Nell ought to have attended, yet she remained seated, while Mr. Pidgeon, who was composing a poem titled “To Honora” prior to calling the group, remained preoccupied with a stubborn rhyme and failed to notice her absence. At one point, while no one was watching, Hugh extracted a small pink confection heart bearing a gilded message, “You are sweet,” from his desk and slid it beneath the bend of Nell’s arm. At this, Nell stood up, held the pink candy delicately with her fingertips, let it fall to the ground, crushed it into dust under her shoe, and sat back down as before without condescending to look at Hugh.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Upon the conclusion of class, Nell proceeded to her workspace, where she made a point of withdrawing all her belongings, including her books and notepad, pen and inkwell, testament and math text, stacking them orderly atop her fractured slate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nell, why are you bringing all those items back with you?” inquired Isolde, the moment they reached the road, having lacked the courage to pose the query earlier.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I am not coming back to school any more,” Nell declared. Isolde caught her breath and gazed at Nell, trying to discern if she was serious.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Will Thirza permit you to remain at home?” was her question.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “She will be forced to,” declared Nell. “I am never returning to school to be taught by that man.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Oh, Nell!” Isolde appeared on the verge of tears. “I really believe you are unkind. What am I to do? Mr. Pidgeon is going to force me to be seated next to that dreadful Tibby Tulk—I am certain he will since no one is sitting beside her. Please return, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I’d perform nearly any act on earth on your behalf, Isolde,” Nell uttered mournfully. “I’d suffer being ripped apart piece by piece if that might benefit you. However, this is beyond what I can do, so I beg you not to request it. You deeply torment my innermost spirit.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Only consider the amount of enjoyment you are bound to forgo,” grieved Isolde. “Our plans involve constructing the most wonderful fresh dwelling beside the stream; additionally, ball games will commence during the coming week, a sport you have yet to try, Nell. The thrill is immense. Furthermore, a fresh melody is on our schedule to master—Odette Pullen is currently refining her execution of it; moreover, Alice Pullen intends to transport a fresh Pansy volume in the upcoming week, which every one of us will recite in turn, taking a chapter each, beside the stream. Besides, your deep affection for reciting aloud is well known to you, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Not a single thing altered Nell's decision. She had settled her thoughts. Going to school to Mr. Pidgeon again was something she would not do; upon returning home, she informed Thirza of this.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Nonsense,” Thirza said.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “That is not nonsense whatsoever,” Nell stated, her serious, accusing gaze fixed upon Thirza. “Can you not comprehend, Thirza? A offense has been committed against me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Fiddlesticks to being insulted! Tomorrow, you will attend school just like always.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Oh, no.” Nell gave a soft shake of her head. “I’m not returning, Thirza. I’ll study my lessons at home and I’ll be as well-behaved as I can manage and keep quiet continuously if it’s at all feasible. But I will not return to school, I promise you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Thirza observed what appeared to be resolute obstinacy staring from the diminutive face of Nell. It was clear to her that defeating this trait would prove difficult, yet she prudently decided to refrain from speaking any further at that moment.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “This evening, I will go down to consult Agatha regarding the matter,” was her inner thought. “Attempting to reason with Nell at this moment is pointless. Given how overwrought she is, I suspect she possesses a dreadful streak of obstinacy when the mood strikes her. Based on what I can gather from her account, Mr. Pidgeon’s conduct has been somewhat overbearing. Expressing such a view to her directly, however, would be a mistake. I will simply discuss it with Agatha instead. Having put ten children through school, she should possess some insight into the situation. Moreover, she will undoubtedly have learned the entire tale by now.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Mrs. Sowerby was discovered by Thirza knitting quilts with her customary industry and cheer.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I imagine you are aware of the reason for my visit,” she stated, looking somewhat embarrassed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Mrs. Agatha gave a nod.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Regarding Nell’s trouble at school, I suppose,” she remarked. “Tillie Gammon stopped by while coming home from school and mentioned it to me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “I am at a loss regarding her,” Thirza remarked. “She asserts that returning to school is out of the question. A child has never appeared so agitated to me. Ever since her schooling began, I have anticipated difficulties. The situation was progressing far too smoothly for it to endure, as I was well aware. Her nervous temperament is so pronounced. Agatha, what recommendation would you offer?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Well, Thirza, because you’ve requested my counsel,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked pleasantly—she thoroughly enjoyed being consulted for guidance—“I would simply indulge her a bit to begin with, I really would. I reckon that Mr. Pidgeon made a mistake. Naturally, one shouldn't admit that to the youngsters, as you are aware. And naturally he was correct in chastising her yesterday when she lost her temper. However, today was another matter. Everyone else who arrived late ought to have faced chastisement alongside Nell, that is my opinion. Furthermore, I disapprove of forcing the girls to sit alongside the boys as a penalty. It lacks modesty. Tillie Gammon felt truly outraged. She supported Nell entirely and mentioned that every student did as well. Nell appears to be quite well-liked by them, for some reason. I failed to imagine she would fit in among them so successfully.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “So you truly believe it would be best for me to allow her to remain at home,” Thirza remarked, thoroughly astonished.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Yes. That is I wouldn’t bring up school to her again until she brought it up herself. Rely on it, Thirza, she’ll calm down in about a week and be willing enough to return on her own, that’s what, whereas, if you forced her to return immediately, good Lord knows what whim or fit of temper she’d have next and cause more problems than ever. The smaller the scene created the better, as I see it. She won’t miss a great deal by staying away from school, for that matter. Mr. Pidgeon is not effective whatsoever as an instructor. The discipline he maintains is disgraceful, that’s what, and he ignores the little children while spending all his effort on those older pupils he’s preparing for Regent’s. He would not have secured the school for another year if his uncle was not a trustee—the real trustee, since he simply controls the other two completely, that’s what. I swear, I don’t know what education in this Island is turning into.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Mrs. Agatha moved her head from side to side, as if to imply that matters would be handled far more effectively were she merely in charge of the Province's educational system.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Following the counsel of Mrs. Agatha, Thirza ensured that returning to school was never again mentioned to Nell. Her studies took place at home, where she completed her tasks and engaged in play with Isolde during the crisp, purple dusk of autumn; however, whenever she came across Hugh Carrow along the pathway or saw him during Sunday-school, she walked past him with a freezing disdain that remained completely unthawed despite his clear wishes to make amends. Not even the attempts of Isolde to act as a mediator yielded any results. Nell had clearly resolved that she would despise Hugh Carrow for the rest of her days.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Yet, to the same degree that she despised Hugh, she adored Isolde, devoting to her the full affection of her fervent small heart, which was just as strong in its affections as in its hatreds. During one dusk, as Thirza returned from the orchard carrying a basket filled with apples, she discovered Nell weeping inconsolably, seated by herself near the eastern window.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “What on earth is wrong now, Nell?” she inquired.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: “Isolde is the reason,” wept Nell with abandon. “My love for Isolde is so immense, Thirza. Living without her will never be possible for me. Yet I am fully aware that upon reaching adulthood, Isolde is going to marry someone, depart, and abandon me. Oh, whatever will I do? That husband of hers is someone I despise—I simply despise him with a passion. My mind has been picturing the entire scenario—the ceremony and all the rest—with Isolde attired in pure white clothes, wearing a veil, and appearing every bit as gorgeous and majestic as a monarch; while I serve as her bridesmaid, also wearing a gorgeous gown featuring puffy sleeves, yet concealing a fracturing heart behind my grinning visage. And after that, saying farewell to Isolde—” At this point Nell completely lost control, weeping even more bitterly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
text: Thirza swung around rapidly so that her twitching face would not be seen; however, her efforts failed; she broke down into the closest chair, erupting into a laugh so genuine and unfamiliar that Obed, who was walking across the yard outdoors, stopped, utterly astonished. Before this moment, when had Thirza’s laughter ever sounded like that to him?

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “No.” Taking a deep breath, Nell said. “I assumed you held me in affection, naturally, but my hopes never reached your loving me. Why, Isolde, my belief was that no person was capable of loving me. Ever since the time I can recall, I have been loved by no one. Oh, how amazing this is! A beam of illumination has appeared, one that will perpetually illuminate the shadow of a road separated from thee, Isolde. Oh, utter it merely one more time.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “You can be certain that my love for you, Nell, is devoted and will last forever,” Isolde declared firmly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “And I shall forever hold thee dear, Isolde,” stated Nell, offering her hand in a serious manner. “Throughout the future, the thought of thee will gleam such as a star above my solitary existence, just as it is stated in that final tale we perused in company. Isolde, wilt thou grant me a strand of thy raven hair upon our farewell to cherish for all time?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “Is there anything you can use to slice it?” asked Isolde, who dried the tears that Nell’s touching tone had prompted to stream once more, as she shifted her focus back to realistic matters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “Yes. Fortunately, I have my patchwork scissors in the pocket of my apron,” Nell said. One of Isolde’s curls was solemnly clipped by her. “Farewell, my beloved friend. From now on, although we live next to one another, we must be like strangers. My heart, however, will always remain faithful to thee.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Nell remained standing and observed Isolde until she was no longer visible, sorrowfully waving her hand toward her each time Isolde turned around to glance back. Afterward, she went back inside the house, temporarily comforted to no small degree by this imaginative farewell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “Everything is ended,” she told Thirza. “Another friend will never be mine. My situation is actually more terrible than it was previously, since Lettie Marchant and Melisande are no longer with me. Even were they present, a change would have occurred. Little imaginary girls simply fail to fulfill you once you have known a genuine companion. Down beside the spring, Isolde and I shared a deeply moving goodbye. For the rest of my days, my memory will hold it sacred. Employing the most sorrowful phrasing I could imagine, I addressed her as ‘thou’ and ‘thee.’ Words like ‘thou’ and ‘thee’ appear far more poetic than ‘you.’ A lock of her hair was given to me by Isolde, which I plan to stitch inside a small pouch to hang about my neck for as long as I live. Be sure that it goes into the grave with me, because my life likely will not endure much longer. Maybe seeing me laid out frozen and deceased in her presence will cause Mrs. Pembroke to experience guilt over her actions, allowing Isolde to attend my burial.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “I don’t think you are in any great danger of passing away from sorrow so long as your tongue keeps moving, Nell,” Thirza remarked without sympathy.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: When the next Monday arrived, Nell caught Thirza off guard by descending from her bedroom, carrying her book basket supported by her arm and hip, her mouth drawn tight into a resolute expression.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “I will return to school,” she declared. “Since my companion has been so mercilessly ripped away from me, nothing else remains in my life. I am able to gaze upon her at school and reflect on bygone days.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “You would do well to ponder your schoolwork and arithmetic,” Thirza remarked, hiding her happiness regarding how things were turning out. “Should you return to classes, my expectation is that we will not hear any further about smashing slates on folks’ heads or similar misbehavior. Conduct yourself properly and obey every instruction given by your educator.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “I will attempt to be an exemplary student,” Nell assented mournfully. “I anticipate that it will not contain much enjoyment. Mr. Pidgeon stated that Posy Pullen was an exemplary student, and she possesses not a single trace of imagination or vitality. She is merely tedious and plodding, and she never appears to enjoy herself. However, I am feeling so downhearted that maybe I will find it simple at present. My route will be around by the road. Traveling via the Aspen Path entirely by myself is something I could not endure. Doing so would cause me to cry bitter tears.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Everyone at school greeted Nell back with enthusiasm. During games, they had deeply missed her creativity, while her vocals were missed in the music, and her theatrical talent had been missed when books were read out loud at the dinner hour. While testament reading was taking place, Opal Pettigrew secretly passed three blue plums to her; Ella May MacKinnon presented her with a massive yellow pansy that had been excised from a floral catalogue's cover—a type of desk ornament highly valued at Brierley school. A proposal to instruct her in a truly exquisite new design of knit lace, which was very suitable for apron trimming, was made by Sophia Mott. A perfume bottle to hold slate water was given to her by Lettie Gammon, and on a sheet of light pink paper featuring scalloped edges, Julia Bell painstakingly transcribed this verse:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “TO NELL

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “As evening pulls its veil across And secures it with a star Keep in mind you possess a friend Even if she should roam afar.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “To have one's worth recognized feels truly wonderful,” Nell murmured delightedly to Thirza later that evening.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Female students were not the sole pupils who “appreciated” her. Upon returning to her desk following the dinner hour—Mr. Pidgeon had directed her to share a seat with the exemplary Posy Pullen—she discovered a large, mouth-watering “strawberry apple” lying there. Nell snatched it up, fully prepared to bite into it, until it occurred to her that the sole location in Brierley producing strawberry apples was the ancient Carrow orchard situated across the Lake of Glassy Waters. Nell let the apple fall as though it were a piece of burning coal and conspicuously cleaned her hands using her handkerchief. The apple remained undisturbed upon her desk through to the following day, at which time young Timothy Pullen, whose duties included sweeping the schoolhouse and lighting the fire, claimed it as part of his earned benefits. Wilfred Mott’s slate pencil, magnificently decorated in banded red and yellow paper, priced at two cents whereas normal pencils were priced at merely one, which he passed along to her following the dinner hour, received a far more approving response. Nell was kindly inclined to take it and compensated the giver with a smile that instantly elevated that enamored boy into the seventh heaven of joy, leading him to commit such terrible mistakes during his dictation that Mr. Pidgeon forced him to stay behind after school to write it again.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: However since,

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: When Brutus’s bust was missing from Cæsar’s procession, it served only to bring Rome’s finest son even more to her mind,

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Thus, because Isolde Pembroke, who occupied a seat beside Tibby Tulk, noticeably failed to offer any tribute or acknowledgment, Nell’s modest victory was rendered bitter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “I think Isolde may have offered me a single smile,” she lamented to Thirza when evening came. Yet as the following morning arrived, Nell received a tiny package alongside a letter that had been folded and twisted in the most extraordinary and terrifying manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “My dear Nell,” read the first, “it is Mother’s instruction that I must neither play with you nor speak to you, even at school. You must not be angry with me, as it is not my doing, for my love for you remains as strong as ever. Without you to hear all my secrets, I miss you terribly, and Tibby Tulk is not to my liking at all. I crafted a new bookmarker for you using red tissue paper. These are extremely popular currently, with a mere three girls in school possessing the skill to construct them. As your eyes fall upon it, keep in mind

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Your genuine companion, Isolde Pembroke.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Having perused the message, Nell bestowed a kiss upon the bookmark and sent a swift answer back across the school grounds.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: My own darling Isolde:— Naturally, I am not angry with you for needing to comply with your mother's wishes. Our souls are able to communicate. I will preserve your beautiful gift eternally. Posy Pullen is an exceedingly pleasant small girl—even though she lacks imagination—however, having served as Isolde’s busum friend, I am unable to become Posy’s. Kindly pardon any errors since my spelling remains somewhat imperfect, even if greatly improoved.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Ever yours to the end of life, Nell or Lucinda Harcourt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: P.S. Tonight, I will rest with your letter beneath my pillow.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: A. or C.S.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: Thirza harbored gloomy anticipations of fresh difficulties now that Nell was attending school once more. However, no trouble materialized. It may be that Posy Pullen’s “model” attitude influenced Nell; in any case, her relationship with Mr. Pidgeon remained quite smooth from that time on. Throwing her whole heart and soul into her academic work, she was resolved that Hugh Carrow would not surpass her in a single subject. The competition that arose between the two soon became obvious; while Hugh’s participation was completely friendly, it is greatly to be doubted that Nell felt the same way, as she indisputably possessed an undesirable tendency to harbor animosity. The intensity of her dislikes matched the intensity of her affections. She refused to demean herself by confessing an intention to compete against Hugh in her studies, as doing so would amount to recognizing his existence, which Nell resolutely refused to do; nevertheless, the contest persisted with academic achievements shifting back and forth between them. At one moment, Hugh occupied the top spot in spelling; at the next, Nell, tossing her long red braids, successfully spelled him down. On a particular morning, Hugh completed every sum without error and earned a place on the honor roll on the blackboard; on the following morning, Nell, having engaged in a frantic struggle with decimals throughout the previous night, took top honors. On one terrible occasion, they achieved identical scores and had their names posted side by side. The humiliation for Nell was nearly equal to that of a published marriage notice, and her embarrassment was just as obvious as Hugh’s delight. Every month, when the written tests were administered, the resulting tension was agonizing. During the initial month, Hugh finished three points in front. During the second, Nell surpassed him by five points. Yet her victory lost its sweetness because Hugh openly offered her his enthusiastic congratulations in front of all the students. Victory would have brought her far greater joy if he had experienced the bitterness of his failure.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: A pupil whose resolve to learn was as unwavering as Nell's could scarcely avoid advancing under any instructor, even if Mr. Pidgeon was perhaps not a particularly effective one. Nell and Hugh had each been advanced to the fifth class when the term concluded, and they were permitted to commence their studies in the fundamentals of “the branches”—a term that referred to Latin, geometry, French, and algebra. It was in geometry that Nell suffered her ultimate defeat.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “It’s completely terrible material, Thirza,” she moaned. “I’m certain I will not ever manage to understand it. There isn't any room for imagination in it whatsoever. Mr. Pidgeon tells me I am the biggest blockhead he has ever seen with it. And Hughie—that is to say certain of the rest are so clever with it. It is deeply humiliating, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
text: “Isolde manages even better than I manage. However, I have no objection to Isolde outdoing me. Even though our meetings are as strangers now, my love for her remains one that cannot be extinguished. Thinking of her causes me great sadness on occasion. Nevertheless, Thirza, a person is unable to remain sad for very long when the world is this interesting, isn't that so?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: EVERY great matter is intertwined with every small matter. On the surface, it may not appear that the choice made by a particular Canadian Premier regarding the addition of St. Brendan’s Island to a political tour could possess much or any connection to the fate of little Nell Harcourt at Grey Shutters. Nevertheless, it did.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: The Premier arrived during one January so that he could speak to his devoted followers and whatever opponents selected to attend the enormous public gathering hosted in Port Marlow. Because the majority of Brierley residents shared the political party of the Premier, almost every man and a large fraction of the women traveled to the town thirty miles distant during the evening of the gathering. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby departed as well. Being a passionate partisan, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby was incapable of believing the political rally might succeed if she were absent, even though her political views were opposing. Consequently, she traveled to town, bringing along her spouse—Thomas would prove helpful by caring for the horse—as well as Thirza Abernethy. Having a secret fascination with politics on her own part, Thirza believed this could be her sole opportunity to view an actual living Premier, so she immediately seized the occasion, leaving Nell and Obed to watch over the home prior to her arrival back the next day.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Therefore, during the time that Thirza and Mrs. Agatha were having a wonderful time at the mass meeting, Nell and Obed were alone in the cozy kitchen at Grey Shutters. In the old-style Waterloo stove, a brilliant fire glowed, and frost crystals of a bluish-white color sparkled on the windowpanes. On the sofa, Obed was dozing over a Farmers’ Advocate, whereas Nell sat at the table and applied herself to her lessons with stubborn resolve, even though she cast several longing looks toward the clock shelf, which held a fresh book that Odette Pullen had provided her that very day. Odette had promised her that it was guaranteed to deliver countless thrills, or something along those lines, and Nell’s hands ached to grasp it. However, doing so would result in Hugh Carrow’s victory the following day. Nell rotated away from the clock shelf and attempted to pretend it did not exist.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Did you ever learn geometry when you attended school, Obed?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well now, no, I didn’t,” Obed remarked, abruptly awakening from his slumber.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “I wish you had done so,” sighed Nell, “since you would then have the capacity to sympathize with me. Proper sympathy is impossible if the subject has never been studied by you. My entire life is being darkened by it. Obed, I am such a dunce at it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well now, I dunno,” Obed said in a soothing manner. “I reckon you do well enough at everything. It was last week in the Delford store owned by Blair that Mr. Pidgeon mentioned to me that you were the school's brightest student and were advancing rapidly. ‘Rapid progress’ were the exact words he used. Some people disparage Teddy Pidgeon and claim he isn't much of an instructor, but I reckon he's fine.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Whoever spoke well of Nell would have been considered “all right” by Obed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “If only he wouldn't alter the letters, I’m sure geometry would be easier for me,” Nell complained. “After I memorize the proposition, he draws it on the blackboard using letters that differ from the ones in the book, which confuses me completely. Do you think it’s fair for a teacher to take a mean advantage like that? Agriculture is what we are studying now, and I’ve finally discovered the reason the roads are red. That brings me great comfort. I wonder if Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby are having a good time. According to Mrs. Sowerby, Canada is going to the dogs because of how things are managed at Ottawa, serving as a terrible warning to voters. She claims a blessed change would happen quickly if women had the right to vote. How do you vote, Obed?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Conservative,” Obed answered without delay. Supporting the Conservative party formed a component of Obed’s faith.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Then I’m Conservative as well,” Nell stated with conviction. “I’m happy about it since Hughie—since a few of the male students at school are Grits. I suppose Mr. Pidgeon is a Grit as well because the father of Sukey Pullen is one, and Opal Pettigrew claims that a courting man must always share the same religion as the girl’s mother and the same political views as her father. Is that accurate, Obed?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well now, I don’t know,” Obed remarked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Was there ever a time you went courting, Obed?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well now, no, I reckon I never did,” uttered Obed, who assuredly had never contemplated such a matter throughout his entire life.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Nell thought carefully, resting her chin on her hands.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Wouldn’t you agree that it must be quite fascinating, Obed? According to Opal Pettigrew, once she reaches adulthood she intends to keep a whole bunch of suitors dangling and drive every one of them wild over her; nevertheless, my own feeling is that it would prove excessively thrilling. My preference would be for merely a single one who remains sane. Even so, Opal Pettigrew is well versed in those topics on account of having a large number of older sisters, and Mrs. Sowerby remarks that the Pettigrew daughters have been snapped up rapidly like hot cakes. Almost every night, Mr. Pidgeon pays a visit to Sukey Pullen. His explanation is that he goes to assist her with her schoolwork, yet Ottilie Mott is likewise preparing for the Regent’s examination, and it seems to me her need for assistance is far greater than Sukey’s since she is considerably more foolish, yet he fails to visit her in the evenings to assist her whatsoever. This world contains a vast number of matters that I struggle to comprehend clearly, Obed.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Indeed, I am not sure that I grasp every one of them on my own,” Obed admitted.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well, I guess my lessons need to be completed. I will not permit myself to unseal that new volume Odette gave me to borrow before I am finished. However, it is an awful lure, Obed. I can view it right there just as clearly even if I rotate away from it. Odette mentioned that she wept until she was ill because of it. A book that causes me to weep is something I adore. Nevertheless, my thought is to transport that volume to the sitting room, secure it inside the jam closet, and hand the key over to you. Furthermore, you are forbidden from handing it back to me, Obed, prior to my lessons being completed, even in the event that I beg you on my knees. Declaring one should resist temptation is fine, but resisting it becomes far simpler when obtaining the key is impossible. Additionally, should I hurry to the cellar to retrieve a few russets, Obed? Would some russets appeal to you?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well now, I don’t know but what I would,” stated Obed, who refrained from eating russets himself yet was aware of Nell’s fondness for the fruit.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Right as Nell stepped out of the cellar in triumph carrying her plate of russets, the noise of rushing feet on the frozen board walk outdoors was heard, and a second later the kitchen door flew open to admit Isolde Pembroke, who burst in pale and out of breath with a shawl thrown hurriedly over her head. Nell immediately dropped her plate and candle due to her shock, and the plate, candle, and apples tumbled all at once down the cellar ladder, where they were discovered at the foot covered in cooled grease the following day by Thirza, who picked them all up and expressed gratitude that the home had not caught fire.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “What on earth has happened, Isolde?” Nell shouted. “Did your mother finally change her mind?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Oh, Nell, do come quick,” Isolde begged anxiously. “Posy Fay is terribly ill—she has croup. Young Mary Joe says—and Father and Mother have gone to town and no one is available to fetch the doctor. Posy Fay is terribly bad and Young Mary Joe is at a loss as to what to do—and oh, Nell, I am so frightened!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Silently, Obed took his coat and cap, glided by Isolde, and vanished into the yard's dark night.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “He has set off to hook up the sorrel mare so he can head to Delford to fetch the physician,” stated Nell, who was hastily putting on her jacket and hood. “It is as clear to me as if he had spoken it aloud. Obed and I share such a deep bond that I am able to discern his mind with no words whatsoever.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “He won't catch the doctor at Delford, I'm sure,” Isolde wept. “Dr. Blair went to town, as I am aware, and Dr. Tranter likely went as well, I suppose. Nobody with croup has ever been seen by young Mary Joe, and away is where Mrs. Sowerby is. Oh, Nell!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Do not weep, Izzy,” Nell remarked in a cheerful manner. “I am fully aware of how to treat croup. It has escaped your mind that Mrs. Rudge gave birth to twins on three occasions. Caring for three sets of twins inevitably provides a person with extensive practice. Every one of them contracted croup at frequent intervals. Remain here briefly while I fetch the bottle of ipecac—it is possible you lack it in your home. Let us go at this moment.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Clasping hands, the pair of young girls rushed forward, traveling along Linger Lane and then over the crusted field past it, since the excessive depth of the snow prevented them from taking the briefer forest path. While Nell felt genuine sympathy for Posy Fay, she remained fully attuned to the romantic nature of the circumstances and the joy of partaking in that melodrama again alongside a like-minded companion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: It was a clear, frosty night, filled entirely with the silver of snowy slopes and the ebony of shadows; above the quiet fields, large stars shone bright; scattered throughout, the dark, pointed firs rose up, their branches dusted with snow as the wind whistled amongst them. Nell felt that traveling smoothly across such mystery and beauty alongside the bosom friend who had been alienated from her for so long was genuinely wonderful.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: At three years old, Posy Fay was truly extremely ill. Resting on the sofa in the kitchen, she was restless and running a fever, and the entire house echoed with her raspy breaths. Mrs. Pembroke had hired young Mary Joe, a healthy, wide-faced French girl from the creek, to look after the children while she was away, but Mary Joe was confused and powerless, entirely unable to figure out what needed to be done, or to execute it even if she did know.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Nell set about her task with deftness and speed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Posy Fay definitely has croup, and her condition is rather severe, though I have witnessed more extreme cases. Our initial requirement is a large quantity of hot water. Isolde, I swear the kettle barely contains a cup! Now that I have topped it off, Mary Joe, you can add wood to the stove. Without meaning to cause offense, it strikes me that an imaginative person would have anticipated this earlier. Next, I will remove Posy Fay’s clothes and tuck her into bed while you attempt to locate some soft flannel rags, Isolde. To begin her treatment, I intend to administer a dose of ipecac.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Posy Fay did not react well to the ipecac, yet Nell’s experience in raising three sets of twins proved useful. That ipecac was swallowed, not just one time, but repeatedly throughout the lengthy, worrisome night as the pair of young girls attentively tended to the afflicted Posy Fay, while Young Mary Joe, sincerely eager to assist in any way possible, maintained a blazing fire and warmed a larger quantity of water than a hospital filled with croupy infants would have required.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Obed brought a physician at three o'clock, having found it necessary to travel as far as Tullyvale to secure him. However, the urgent necessity for help had elapsed. Feeling significantly improved, Posy Fay was resting deeply.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Despair almost caused me to surrender,” Nell clarified. “Her condition steadily deteriorated until her illness surpassed that of the Rudge twins, even the final set. My belief was truly that choking to death would be her end. Every single drop of ipecac from that bottle was administered by me, and as the final dose was swallowed, I uttered to myself—avoiding Isolde and Young Mary Joe so as not to increase their existing anxiety, yet needing to speak it internally merely to ease my emotions—‘Upon this final remaining hope I rely, though I dread it is useless.’ Nevertheless, roughly three minutes later, she expelled the phlegm through coughing and immediately commenced recovering. Doctor, you have to envision my sense of relief, since expressing it verbally is impossible for me. As you are aware, certain matters defy verbal expression.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Yes, I know,” the doctor affirmed with a nod. He gazed toward Nell as though contemplating aspects of her that defied verbal description. Subsequently, though, he voiced these thoughts to Mr. and Mrs. Pembroke.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “The small red-haired girl living at Abernethy’s possesses as much intelligence as anyone could. I am telling you that the baby would have died before my arrival if she had not saved its life. A child as young as she is exhibits a degree of ability and composure that is truly remarkable. When she described the situation to me, her eyes were unlike anything I had ever witnessed.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: It was a marvelous, white-frosted winter morning when Nell headed back to her house, her eyes heavy due to a lack of sleep, yet she conversed tirelessly with Obed while they traversed the expansive white field and passed beneath the sparkling, magical arch formed by the maples of Linger Lane.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Oh, Obed, isn’t this morning marvellous? It seems as though the world is something created by God purely for His own enjoyment, wouldn’t you say? Those trees appear so delicate that a single breath from me could blow them away—pouf! It makes me so happy to reside in a world that features white frosts, doesn’t it you? Also, I am very pleased that Mrs. Rudge ended up having three sets of twins. Had she not, I might have been at a loss regarding how to help Posy Fay. I truly regret ever being angry with Mrs. Rudge on account of her having twins. Even so, oh, Obed, I feel terribly tired. School is out of the question for me. I am certain I could not hold my eyes open and would act so foolishly. Yet I dislike remaining at home, because of Hughie—someone else will take the top spot in class, and climbing back up is so difficult—even if, naturally, the greater the difficulty, the more gratification one receives upon reaching the top again, don't you think?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well now, I suppose you’ll get by fine,” Obed said, observing Nell’s pale small face as well as the dark circles beneath her eyes. “You simply go straight to bed and get some rest. I’m going to handle every chore.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Nell consequently retired to bed, sleeping with such duration and depth that the pale, blushing winter afternoon was far advanced by the time she roused herself and went down to the kitchen, in which sat Thirza, having returned in the interim, engaged in her knitting.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Oh, was the Premier seen by you?” Nell immediately blurted out. “Thirza, how did he look?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Well, his appearance prevented him from ever becoming Premier,” Thirza stated. “That man possessed quite a nose! However, he possesses speechmaking ability. Belonging to the Conservatives made me proud. Agatha Sowerby, who is a Liberal naturally, found him worthless. Nell, your dinner rests inside the oven, and from the pantry you may retrieve some blue plum preserve for yourself. You must be hungry, I suppose. Obed described last night's events to me. Truly, knowing how to act was lucky, I must admit. Having never witnessed a croup case, I would have lacked any idea what to do. There now, refrain from speaking until after you consume your dinner. Your appearance tells me you are simply overflowing with speeches, yet they can wait.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: Thirza possessed news for Nell, yet she withheld it at that moment because she recognized that sharing it then would cause Nell’s resulting enthusiasm to transport her completely away from practical concerns like her appetite or the meal. Thirza waited until Nell had consumed the last of her dish of blue plums before stating:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: “Mrs. Pembroke came by this afternoon, Nell. Although she wished to speak with you, I chose not to disturb your sleep. According to her, you preserved Posy Fay’s life, and she deeply regrets her behavior regarding that currant wine incident. She mentioned that she currently realizes you had no intention of making Isolde intoxicated, and she trusts you will pardon her and resume your close friendship with Isolde. You have permission to visit her tonight if you wish, since Isolde is unable to step outside her home because of a severe cold she acquired yesterday evening. Now, Nell Harcourt, please do not lose your temper for goodness’ sake.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
text: The caution appeared far from unwarranted, given how elevated and weightless Nell’s demeanor and posture became as she leaped up, her countenance illuminated by the fire of her soul.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
