Nevertheless, I can simply sense her joy in being a Christian, and that she would remain one even were it possible for her to reach heaven without doing so.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “I guess we ought to invite Mr. and Mrs. Wace over for tea one of these days,” Thirza remarked thoughtfully. “They have visited practically every place except this one. Let me think. Upcoming Wednesday should be a suitable date to entertain them. However, do not mention a thing to Obed regarding it, because if he were aware of their arrival he would invent a reason to be absent then. He had grown so accustomed to Mr. Bentley that he was comfortable with him, yet he will struggle to adjust to a different pastor, and a different pastor’s spouse will terrify him completely.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “I will keep it as quiet as the grave,” promised Nell. “However, Thirza, is it all right if I bake a cake for the event? I would be thrilled to contribute something for Mrs. Wace, and you are aware that I have become quite skilled at baking a cake now.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “It is possible for you to bake a layer cake,” Thirza pledged.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Extensive arrangements were made at Grey Shutters throughout Monday and Tuesday. Serving tea to the minister and his spouse was a grave and significant event, and Thirza was resolved to outshine all the housekeepers in Brierley. Nell was filled with wild delight and excitement. Sitting on the large red rocks beside the Nymph’s Well during Tuesday evening's dusk, she discussed everything with Isolde while they created rainbows upon the water using small twigs coated in fir balsam.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Isolde, every single thing is prepared, with the exception of my cake that I am supposed to bake in the morning, alongside the baking-powder biscuits that Thirza is going to prepare right before the time for tea. Isolde, I promise you that these two days have been extremely busy for Thirza and me. Hosting a minister’s family for tea involves a great deal of responsibility. An event like this has never happened to me until now. Our pantry is something you really ought to look at. It is a remarkable vision. Jellied chicken and cold tongue are going to be served by us. We will serve a pair of jelly varieties, one red and one yellow, as well as whipped cream, lemon pie, cherry pie, three varieties of cookies, fruit cake, Thirza’s well-known yellow plum preserves which she reserves specifically for ministers, pound cake, layer cake, plus the previously mentioned biscuits; furthermore, both new and old bread will be provided, should the minister suffer from dyspepsia and be unable to consume new bread. Mrs. Sowerby claims that ministers suffer from dyspepsia, but my opinion is that Mr. Wace has not served as a minister for a sufficient duration to suffer ill effects from it. Thinking about my layer cake makes me freeze up completely. Oh, Isolde, suppose it turns out badly! Last night brought a dream where a horrifying goblin featuring a large layer cake as a head pursued me everywhere.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “It’s going to be good, no doubt,” affirmed Isolde, who was a exceptionally comforting kind of companion. “I’m certain that portion of the one you prepared which we ate for lunch at Larkrise a fortnight back was absolutely splendid.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Yes; but cakes possess such an awful tendency to end up ruined precisely at the moment you most desire them to prove successful,” sighed Nell, launching a twig that was exceptionally heavily coated in balsam. “Nonetheless, I imagine my only option is to rely on Providence while ensuring I remember the flour. Oh, see, Isolde, what a beautiful rainbow! Do you think the dryad might emerge once we depart and use it as a scarf?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “You are aware that dryads do not exist,” Isolde stated. Because her mother had discovered the Whispering Wood and shown clear anger about it, Isolde had ceased all subsequent imaginative mimicry and considered it unwise to foster a mindset that believed even in inoffensive dryads.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “However, picturing it there is extremely simple,” Nell stated. “Prior to retiring each evening, I gaze through my window, asking myself whether the dryad actually sits in this spot, utilizing the spring as a mirror to comb her hair. On occasion, I search the morning dew for her tracks. Oh, Isolde, do not lose your belief in the dryad!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Wednesday morning arrived. Nell arose at dawn since her great excitement prevented her from sleeping. Because she had dabbled in the spring during the previous evening, she had contracted a bad head cold; however, only total pneumonia could have dampened her enthusiasm for cooking that morning. Following breakfast, she set about preparing her cake. Upon finally closing the oven door on it, she took a deep breath.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Thirza, I’m certain nothing was left out on this occasion. Do you believe it will swell up, though? What if the baking powder might be bad? The new can provided what I used. According to Mrs. Sowerby, a person can never rely on securing quality baking powder these days since all products are so impure. It is Mrs. Sowerby's opinion that the Government should address the issue, yet she claims a Tory Government will never act on it in our lifetime. Thirza, suppose that cake fails to rise?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “We’ll have plenty without it” expressed Thirza’s emotionless attitude regarding the matter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: The cake actually rose, nevertheless, emerging from the oven with the featherlight lightness of golden foam. Radiant with joy, Nell pressed its layers together using ruby jelly and, within her mind, envisioned Mrs. Wace consuming a portion and perhaps requesting a second helping!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Thirza, you will certainly utilize the finest set of tea, will you not?” she inquired. “Am I able to adorn the table using wild roses alongside ferns?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “That is complete rubbish to my mind,” Thirza scoffed. “As I see it, the food itself is important, whereas fancy trimmings are not.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Mrs. Pembroke’s table was decorated,” remarked Nell, who was not completely free of serpent-like shrewdness, “and she received a graceful compliment from the minister. It was a banquet for both the eye and the palate, according to him.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Very well, act according to your wishes,” stated Thirza, who was fully resolved to avoid being outdone by Mrs. Pembroke or anyone else. “Just ensure that you preserve sufficient space for the plates and the victuals.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Nell exerted every effort to deck the setting using a style and method intended to outdo Mrs. Pembroke's completely. Possessing a wealth of ferns and roses alongside a naturally refined artistic sensibility, she rendered the tea table so visually stunning that the minister and his wife, upon being seated before it, uttered joint exclamations regarding its exquisite charm.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Nell is responsible for this,” Thirza remarked with stern impartiality; and Nell considered the pleased expression on Mrs. Wace’s face to be an amount of joy nearly exceeding what this life could offer.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Obed had been included, though solely goodness and Nell understood how he had been enticed into joining the group. His extreme shyness and agitation had caused Thirza to abandon all hope for him, yet Nell managed him so capably that he was currently seated at the board wearing his finest attire and a white collar, conversing with the minister in a manner that was far from dull. Not a single word was uttered by him to Mrs. Wace, though that was likely too much to anticipate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Everything proceeded as joyfully as a wedding until the passing of Nell’s layer cake. Having been served a confusing number of dishes earlier, Mrs. Wace turned it down. However, Thirza, noticing how disappointed Nell looked, spoke with a smile:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Oh, Mrs. Wace, you really have to have a slice of this. Nell baked it specifically for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “If so, I have to try some,” Mrs. Wace laughed, taking a fat triangle for herself, which the minister and Thirza did as well.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: A bite was taken of hers by Mrs. Wace, and an extremely strange look passed over her features; she uttered not a single word, though, but persisted in consuming it. Seeing that look, Thirza hurried to sample the cake.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Nell Harcourt!” she cried out, “whatever did you add to that cake?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Only the ingredients specified in the recipe, Thirza,” Nell exclaimed, her face showing deep distress. “Oh, is something wrong?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Very well! That is just dreadful. Mr. Wace, do not attempt to consume it. Nell, sample it for yourself. Which flavor did you add?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Vanilla,” Nell remarked, her cheeks flushed bright red with embarrassment once she had sampled the cake. “Just vanilla. Oh, Thirza, the baking powder has to be to blame. I was already doubtful about that bak—”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Baking powder my foot! Fetch the vanilla bottle that you worked with and hand it to me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Nell hurried off to the pantry and came back carrying a little bottle, somewhat full of a brown fluid, which bore a yellowed label reading, “Best Vanilla.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Thirza accepted it, removed the cork, and took a whiff of it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Heaven help us, Nell, you used Anodyne Liniment to season that cake. After smashing the liniment container a week ago, I transferred the remaining portion into a used, vacant vanilla jar. My own failure to caution you means I am somewhat to blame, I guess—yet in the name of mercy, was it impossible for you to have caught its scent?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Under this twofold shame, Nell broke down crying.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “I couldn’t—my cold was so severe!” and uttering these words, she precipitously escaped to the gable chamber, where she threw herself onto the bed and cried like someone who declines all solace.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Before long a faint footfall rang upon the steps and someone walked into the chamber.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Oh, Thirza,” wept Nell, not raising her eyes, “I am ruined eternally. I can never overcome this shame. People will find out—word always spreads in Brierley. Isolde is going to inquire about my cake, forcing me to confess what happened. Everybody will forever single me out as the person who put anodyne liniment in a cake to flavor it. Hughie—the male students at school will continue to mock it indefinitely. Oh, Thirza, provided you possess any fraction of Christian compassion, do not force me to clean the dishes downstairs following this event. I am willing to scrub them once the minister and his wife leave, but meeting Mrs. Wace's gaze ever again is impossible for me. She might believe I attempted to poison her. Mrs. Sowerby claims to be acquainted with an orphan girl who attempted to poison the person who took care of her. However, the liniment contains no poison. It is intended for internal consumption—even if not inside cakes. Will you please inform Mrs. Wace of that, Thirza?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Why don't you leap to your feet and inform her of that directly,” suggested a cheerful voice.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Nell leaped out of bed, only to see Mrs. Wace beside her, watching her with amused eyes.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “My dear little girl, you mustn’t weep this way,” she remarked, truly unsettled by the tragic expression on Nell’s face. “Why, it’s merely a comical error that any person could commit.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Oh, no, only I could commit a blunder like that,” Nell uttered in a dejected manner. “And my intention was to bake that cake so wonderfully for your sake, Mrs. Wace.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Indeed, I am aware, my dear. I give you my word that your generosity and consideration mean just as much to me as though everything had gone well. You must stop weeping now, and instead accompany me downstairs so you can display your flower garden to me. According to Miss Abernethy, you possess a small patch that belongs entirely to you. I wish to view it, because flowers hold a great deal of interest for me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: Nell allowed herself to be taken downstairs and consoled, thinking how truly fortunate it was that Mrs. Wace shared her disposition. No further mention was made of the liniment cake, and as the visitors departed, Nell realized that she had derived greater pleasure from the night than might have been anticipated, given that awful event. Still, a heavy sigh escaped her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Is it not lovely to consider, Thirza, that a fresh day arrives tomorrow, completely free of errors so far?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “I am certain you will commit many therein,” Thirza remarked. “I have never met anyone who equals your knack for error, Nell.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Indeed, and I am fully aware of it,” Nell conceded sorrowfully. “However, Thirza, have you ever observed a single hopeful aspect regarding me? I do not repeat a blunder.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “I fail to see how that offers much advantage when you are constantly creating additional ones.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Oh, is it not clear to you, Thirza? A person can only commit so many errors, and once I have made every single one, I will finally be done with them. I find great comfort in that idea.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
text: “Indeed, you ought to head off and feed those pigs the cake,” Thirza remarked. “No person could possibly consume it, not even Tobias Boute.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: “AND what makes your eyes bulge like that. Now?” Thirza inquired, as Nell returned from a quick trip to the post office. “Have you found another like-minded soul?” Excitement draped over Nell like a dress, gleamed in her eyes, and illuminated all her features. Through the warm sunlight and drifting shadows of the August dusk, she had come skipping up the lane, resembling a gust-driven fairy.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: “No, Thirza, but oh, what do you think? Tomorrow afternoon, I have been invited to the manse for tea! At the post office, Mrs. Wace dropped off the letter for me. Thirza, just look at it. ‘Miss Nell Harcourt, Grey Shutters.’ Never before was I referred to as ‘Miss.’ It gave me such a thrill! Among my choicest treasures, I shall forever cherish it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: “Mrs. Wace mentioned that her intention was to invite every child in her Sunday-school class for tea one by one,” Thirza remarked, viewing the extraordinary occurrence with great composure. “There is no need for you to become so agitated about it. My dear, you must try to accept events with tranquility.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: Had Nell reacted with composure, it would have required an alteration of her very character. Being entirely “spirit and fire and dew,” both the joys and the sorrows of living struck her with a threefold force. Recognizing this, Thirza experienced a subtle anxiety, aware that life's fluctuations would likely fall heavily upon such a spontaneous spirit, yet failing to fully comprehend that an equivalent aptitude for joy could overcompensate. Consequently, Thirza believed it her responsibility to train Nell into a serene evenness of temperament that was as unachievable and foreign to her as to a sunbeam dancing in a shallow brook. As she regretfully conceded to herself, she was not achieving much progress. Whenever a cherished expectation or scheme failed, Nell was cast into “deeps of affliction.” Whenever it was realized, she was elevated to dizzying heights of joy. Thirza was nearly losing hope of ever transforming this global stray into her ideal modest child possessed of reserved behavior and stiff decorum. Nor would she have accepted that she actually preferred Nell far more precisely as she was.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: Overcome with silent grief, Nell retired for the night since Obed had mentioned the wind coming from the northeast, making him worry that rain would fall the following day. Hearing the poplar trees rustle around the dwelling distressed her, as it resembled the tapping of rain, while the distant, deep bellow of the gulf—a sound she usually enjoyed for its unusual, resonant, and persistent beat—now felt like a forewarning of tempests and ruin to a young girl who desperately desired pleasant weather. It seemed to Nell that dawn would be delayed forever.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: However, every single thing eventually concludes, even those nights preceding the date you are asked for tea at the manse. Regardless of what Obed had predicted, the morning turned out beautiful, causing Nell’s mood to reach its ultimate peak. Washing the dishes from breakfast, she cried out, “Oh, Thirza, a feeling inside me today makes me simply adore all the people I lay eyes on! My feelings are so wonderful, you cannot imagine! If only it might endure, wouldn't that be lovely? Were I merely asked to tea each day, I think I could become an exemplary child. Yet, Thirza, oh, a serious nature belongs to this event as well. Nervousness fills me so. Suppose my manners fail to be correct? As you are aware, taking tea at a manse has never happened to me previously, and despite my reading of the guidelines provided inside the Family Herald’s Etiquette Department from the moment I arrived here, my knowledge of all etiquette rules remains uncertain. Doing something foolish or failing to perform a required act frightens me greatly. If a person desired something immensely, would accepting another portion align with polite behavior?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: “Your problem, Nell, is that your own self occupies too much of your thoughts. Your focus ought to be simply on Mrs. Wace and whatever she would find pleasant and delightful,” declared Thirza, who, for a single moment in her existence, struck upon a most sensible and concise bit of counsel. Nell grasped the truth of this right away.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: “Thirza, you are correct. I will attempt to refrain from giving any thought to myself.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: It was clear that Nell had managed her call without committing any grave faux pas, as she returned in the evening dusk beneath a vast, lofty sky adorned with streaks of rose and yellow clouds, her spirits completely elevated; she sat upon the large red-sandstone step by the kitchen doorway, resting her weary, curly head upon Thirza’s gingham apron, and joyfully recounted the entire experience to Thirza.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: Down over the extensive harvest fields, a chill breeze swept from the edges of fir-covered western hills and blew loudly through the poplars. Above the orchard, a single bright star was suspended, and across Linger Lane, fireflies darted back and forth amid the ferns and swaying branches. As she spoke, Nell observed them, feeling in some way that the breeze, stars, and fireflies had all become intertwined into an indescribably lovely and magical thing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII. Nell Is Invited Out to Tea
text: “Oh, Thirza, my time was exceedingly fascinating. I believe my life has not been in vain, a feeling I will retain forever even if another invitation to tea at a manse is never extended to me. Upon my arrival, Mrs. Wace greeted me at the entrance. The most charming pale-pink organdy dress clothed her, complete with many frills and sleeves reaching her elbows, making her look precisely like a seraph. Truly, Thirza, I think being a minister's wife when I mature would suit me. Because a minister would not focus on such earthly matters, my red hair might not bother him. Naturally, however, a person would need to be inherently good for that, which I will never achieve, so considering it is likely pointless. Certain individuals possess natural goodness, as you know, while others do not. I belong among the others. Mrs. Sowerby claims that original sin fills me. Regardless of how diligently I attempt to be good, I can never succeed to the extent of those possessing natural goodness. It resembles geometry quite a bit, I imagine. Nevertheless, don't you believe that trying so intensely should be worth something? Belonging to those who are naturally good, Mrs. Wace is someone I love passionately. As you know, certain people, such as Obed and Mrs. Wace, can be loved instantly without any effort. Conversely, loving others, such as Mrs. Sowerby, requires immense effort. Since they possess great knowledge and work so actively in the church, you realize you should love them, yet unless you continuously remind yourself, you forget. Originating from the Pale Sands Sunday-school, another little girl attended tea at the manse. Laurette Bradley was her name, and she proved to be a very pleasant little girl. Although not precisely a soulmate, you understand, she was nevertheless very pleasant. Our tea was splendid, and I believe I observed all the decorum rules fairly well. Following tea, Mrs. Wace performed music and sang, and she persuaded Lauretta and me to join in singing as well. Mrs. Wace remarks that my voice is good and states that I must perform in the Sunday-school choir from now on. The pure idea thrilled me beyond what you can imagine. Singing in the Sunday-school choir, just as Isolde does, has been a deep desire of mine, though I worried it was a privilege beyond my reach. Due to a major concert occurring at the Pale Sands Hotel this evening where her sister will recite, Lauretta had to depart early. According to Lauretta, the Americans residing at the hotel organize a concert every two weeks to benefit the Port Marlow hospital, and they request many individuals from Pale Sands to recite. Lauretta mentioned that she anticipates being invited herself eventually. I merely stared at her with reverence. Following her departure, Mrs. Wace and I shared an intimate conversation. I revealed all to her—concerning Mrs. Thomas, the twins, Lettie Marchant, Melisande, my arrival at Grey Shutters, and my struggles with geometry. Can you imagine it, Thirza? Mrs. Wace confessed to me that she too was a fool when it came to geometry. That heartened me immensely. Just prior to my departure, Mrs. Sowerby arrived at the manse, and what do you suppose, Thirza? A new teacher has been hired by the trustees, and she is a woman. Miss Agnes Thorne is her name. Is that not an enchanting name? According to Mrs. Sowerby, a female teacher has never been employed in Brierley previously, and she regards it as a perilous change. Yet I feel having a woman as a teacher will be wonderful, and I truly do not know how I will endure the fortnight remaining until school opens. Seeing her makes me so eager.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: NELL had to survive for over fourteen days, as things turned out. Nearly four weeks having gone by since the incident with the liniment cake, the time was ripe for her to become involved in a new kind of plight, minor errors—like distractedly pouring a basin of skimmed milk into a container of yarn balls in the pantry rather than into the swine’s trough, and stepping right off the side of the log bridge into the stream while lost in creative daydreaming—not truly being deserving of notice.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: One week following the afternoon tea held at the manse, a party was thrown by Isolde Pembroke.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Little and choice,” Nell promised Thirza. “Only the female students from our form.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: A very good time was had by them, and not a single untoward thing took place until tea had ended, at which point they ended up in the Pembroke garden, having grown slightly weary from all their games and ready for whichever tempting type of mischief could show itself. Before long, this manifested as “daring.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Taking risks happened to be the trendy pastime for the young children of Brierley at that time. Although it originated with the boys, the trend quickly caught on with the girls, and a whole book could be filled with all the foolish acts performed in Brierley that summer simply because those who did them were “dared” to accomplish them.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Initially, Carrie Mott challenged Opal Pettigrew to scale the enormous old willow tree facing the front door up to a specific spot; Opal Pettigrew promptly accomplished this to the embarrassment of the previously mentioned Carrie Mott, despite feeling a deadly terror of the plump green caterpillars swarming the tree and fearing her mother's reaction if her new muslin dress were ripped. Subsequently, Flossie Tulk challenged Odette Pullen to continuously hop on her left leg around the garden, never pausing or placing her right foot down; Odette Pullen bravely attempted this feat, but her strength failed at the third corner, forcing her to admit defeat.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Because Flossie’s victory was somewhat more obvious than propriety allowed, Nell Harcourt challenged her to step along the crest of the wooden fence that bordered the garden on its eastern side. Indeed, to “walk” wooden fences demands greater dexterity and balance of mind and foot than a person who has never attempted it might imagine. However, Flossie Tulk, though lacking in certain traits that foster popularity, possessed at minimum an innate and inherent talent, properly practiced, for stepping along wooden fences. Flossie navigated the Pembroke fence with a light indifference that appeared to suggest that such a small feat was not deserving of a “dare.” Unwilling praise met her achievement, as the majority of the remaining girls could respect it, having endured much adversity themselves during their attempts to step along fences. Flossie stepped down from her elevated spot, glowing with success, and shot an adversarial look toward Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Nell flipped her red braids.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “I do not consider treading on a small, low, wooden fence to be a particularly impressive feat,” she remarked. “In Marysville, I was acquainted with a girl capable of balancing along the ridgepole of a roof.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “I don’t believe it,” Flossie stated flatly. “I don’t believe anyone could walk a ridgepole. At any rate, you couldn’t.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Couldn’t I?” Nell exclaimed impulsively.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “In that case, I challenge you to manage it,” Flossie stated with defiance. “I challenge you to scale that spot and balance across the ridgepole belonging to the kitchen roof of Mr. Pembroke.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Nell grew pale, yet the sole course of action was obvious. She moved in the direction of the dwelling, against whose kitchen roof a ladder rested. Every one of the fifth-class girls uttered, “Oh!” in a mixture of excitement and dismay.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Do not attempt it, Nell,” begged Isolde. “Falling off will kill you. Pay no attention to Flossie Tulk. Daring someone to perform such a perilous act is unfair.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “I have to do it. My honor is on the line,” Nell stated gravely. “I will traverse that ridgepole, Isolde, or die trying. Should I be killed, my pearl bead ring goes to you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Nell went up the ladder while everyone held their breath, reached the ridgepole, stood upright and steady on that unsafe perch, and began making her way across it, lightheadedly aware that she was at an uneasy height above the ground and that stepping along ridgepoles was not an activity where your imagination offered much assistance. Even so, she succeeded in making a few strides prior to the arrival of the disaster. At that moment she tottered, slipped from her equilibrium, tripped, lurched, and plummeted, skidding down the heat-dried roof and hurtling off it through the wild mass of Virginia creeper underneath—all preceding the moment when the horrified audience underneath could let out a single, frightened scream.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Had Nell tumbled off the roof on the side she had climbed, Isolde would likely have inherited the pearl bead ring right at that moment. Luckily, her fall occurred on the opposite side, where the roof stretched down over the porch so close to the ground that falling from it was far less grave. Even so, when Isolde and the rest of the girls hurried wildly around the building—with the exception of Opal Pettigrew, who stayed as though attached to the earth and collapsed into hysterics—they discovered Nell lying entirely pale and lifeless amid the shattered remains of the Virginia creeper.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Nell, have you been slain?” Isolde screamed as she collapsed onto her knees next to her companion. “Oh, Nell, my sweet Nell, utter merely a single word to me so I know whether you have been slain.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: It was an enormous relief to every girl, but particularly to Flossie Tulk—who, despite her absence of imagination, had suffered terrible mental images of a destiny marked as the person responsible for Nell Harcourt’s premature and dismal demise—when Nell sat up in a daze and responded hesitantly:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor

text: “What is the problem? In what place are you injured?” Mrs. Pembroke asked urgently.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor

However, Thirza, what action would you have taken if someone had dared you to walk across a ridgepole?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “I’d have remained on solid, stable earth and permitted them to continue their bold attempts. What foolishness!” Thirza declared.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: A sigh escaped Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Thirza, you possess immense mental fortitude, whereas I lack it entirely. The prospect of facing Flossie Tulk’s contempt simply seemed unbearable to me. She would have boasted at my expense forever. Besides, Thirza, my suffering has been so severe that you really do not need to be angry with me. Fainting is truly unpleasant, to say the least. Furthermore, setting my ankle caused me terrible agony at the hands of the doctor. Walking will be impossible for me for six or seven weeks, meaning I shall miss the arrival of the new lady teacher. By the time my school attendance resumes, her novelty will have worn off. On top of that, Hughie—and every other classmate—will surpass me academically. Truly, my misfortune is great. Nevertheless, I will attempt to endure every hardship courageously, provided you refrain from being angry with me, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Now, now, I am not angry,” Thirza remarked. “You are certainly an unfortunate youngster, without a question; yet just as you mentioned, you are the one who will endure the pain from it. Now then, attempt to consume a bit of supper.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Is it not lucky that I possess this kind of imagination?” asked Nell. “It is going to assist me marvelously, I anticipate. What is done by folks who lack an imagination whenever they fracture their bones, Thirza, in your opinion?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: Nell frequently found ample cause to be grateful for her imagination throughout the seven dreary weeks that ensued. Nevertheless, she did not rely entirely upon it. She received numerous callers, and not a single day went by when at least one schoolgirl did not visit to present her with flowers and books, as well as to inform her about everything taking place within Brierley's youth community.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “Everyone has shown so much goodness and kindness, Thirza,” Nell uttered with a happy sigh on the date she was finally able to hobble from one side of the room to the other. “Being stuck in bed is not very enjoyable; nevertheless, there is a positive aspect, Thirza. It reveals to you the true number of friends you possess. Why, I was even visited by Superintendent Bell, who is actually an extremely nice gentleman. Naturally, he is not a kindred spirit; all the same, I am fond of him and feel terribly regretful that I used to find fault with his prayers. I am convinced now that his intentions behind them are genuine, except he has formed the practice of reciting them as though he lacks earnestness. He could overcome that tendency if he would apply a bit of effort. I dropped him a clear, strong suggestion. I explained to him how much I attempted to render my own personal prayers engaging. He recounted to me the entire story of the occasion when he fractured his ankle as a youth. It appears so odd to picture Superintendent Bell as ever having been a child. My imaginative powers have boundaries, after all, because that is something I am unable to visualize. Whenever I attempt to picture him as a child, I picture him wearing gray whiskers and glasses, precisely as he appears during Sunday-school, except tiny. On the other hand, visualizing Mrs. Wace as a young girl is so simple. I have received fourteen visits from Mrs. Wace. Is that not an achievement to take pride in, Thirza? Especially when the spouse of a minister faces so many demands upon her day! Furthermore, she is such a joyful individual to have pay a call on you. She does not ever inform you that you brought it upon yourself and that she trusts you will become a improved girl because of the experience. Mrs. Sowerby invariably remarked that to me whenever she paid me a call; moreover, she stated it in a manner that caused me to sense she might express a wish for me to become a improved girl, yet lacked actual faith that I would. Even Flossie Tulk paid me a call. I treated her with as much politeness as possible, since I believe she experienced regret for daring me to tread upon a ridgepole. Had I perished, she would have been forced to bear a heavy load of guilt for the rest of her days. Isolde has proved to be a devoted companion. She has come across every single day to bring comfort to my solitary bed. However, oh, I will be immensely happy when I am able to attend school, for I have learned such thrilling details regarding the new instructor. All the girls consider her utterly delightful. Isolde states that her light curly hair is the most exquisite, and her eyes are so captivating. Her attire is gorgeous, and the puffiness of her sleeves exceeds that of any other person in Brierley. On every second Friday afternoon, she conducts recitations during which each pupil must recite a passage or participate in a dialogue. Oh, anticipating it is simply wonderful. Flossie Tulk claims to despise it, but that is merely due to Flossie possessing so little creative mind. Isolde together with Opal Pettigrew and Odette Pullen are rehearsing a dialogue, titled ‘A Morning Visit,’ meant for the upcoming Friday. And on the Friday afternoons when recitations are not held, Miss Thorne escorts everyone out to the forest for a ‘field’ day, where they examine ferns, blossoms, and wild birds. Additionally, they perform physical culture routines each morning and afternoon. Mrs. Sowerby claims that she has never encountered such behavior and that the whole thing results from employing a female educator. Nevertheless, I reckon it must be wonderful, and I trust I will discover that Miss Thorne constitutes a kindred spirit.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
text: “One matter is clear enough, Nell,” Thirza remarked, “and it’s that your tumble from the Pembroke roof hasn't damaged your tongue in the slightest.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: OCTOBER had arrived once more by the time Nell was prepared to return to school—a magnificent October, entirely crimson and gold, featuring mild mornings in which the valleys were packed with subtle mists as though the autumn spirit had filled them up for the sun to drink dry—amethyst, pearl, silver, rose, and smoke-blue. Heavy dews caused the fields to shine like silver cloth, and large piles of rustling leaves rested in the hollows of many-stemmed woods, inviting one to run briskly through them. A yellow canopy hung over the Aspen Path, where the ferns were withered and brown along its entire length. A sharpness existed in the air itself, invigorating the spirits of young girls walking, contrary to snails, rapidly and eagerly toward school; and returning to the small brown desk next to Isolde brought great joy, while Opal Pettigrew nodded from across the aisle, Carrie Mott dispatched notes, and Julia Bell handed down a “chew” of gum from the rear seat. Nell inhaled a deep, happy breath while she sharpened her pencil and placed her picture cards inside her desk. Life was undoubtedly quite fascinating.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: The newly arrived instructor proved to be yet another loyal and supportive ally for her. Miss Thorne, an intelligent and compassionate young lady, possessed the delightful talent for capturing and keeping her students' love while drawing forth their finest intellectual and moral qualities. Beneath this beneficial guidance, Nell blossomed like a blossom, returning to her household to give enthusiastic descriptions of her academic endeavors and ambitions to an appreciative Obed and a discerning Thirza.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: “Thirza, my entire heart belongs to Miss Thorne. Her manners are so refined, and her spoken tone is exceedingly gentle. Whenever my name leaves her lips, I sense without a doubt that an E is included in the spelling. Recitations took place this afternoon. How I long for you to have been present while I delivered ‘Mary, Queen of Scots.’ My entire soul was poured into that performance. On the journey back, Opal Pettigrew mentioned that when I uttered the line, ‘Now for my father’s arm,’ and she noted, ‘my woman’s heart farewell,’ it chilled her blood completely.”

text: “Well now, one of these days, you could repeat it to me when we are out in the barn,” Obed proposed.

text: Yet every physical culture contortion, recitation Friday, and field afternoon seemed insignificant compared to an initiative that Miss Thorne proposed during November. With the students without exception agreeing warmly to this proposal, work on a program commenced immediately. Furthermore, out of every thrilled future participant, not one felt as thrilled as Nell Harcourt, who devoted herself completely to the project, despite being hindered by the opposition of Thirza. To Thirza, the entire affair was sheer absurdity.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: “Your minds are simply being crammed with foolishness, consuming hours that should be spent on your studies,” she complained. “Children organizing performances and hurrying off to rehearsals does not have my sanction. It renders them boastful, impudent, and eager for useless roaming.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: “However, consider the noble purpose,” begged Nell. “A flag will foster a patriotic feeling, Thirza.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: “Well, if you are able to mix patriotism and fun together, isn’t it fine? Naturally, organizing a concert is really wonderful. Six choruses are on our program, and Isolde will perform a solo song. I have parts in two dialogues—‘The Society for the Suppression of Gossip’ along with ‘The Fairy Queen.’ A dialogue will also be performed by the boys. On top of that, Thirza, I am scheduled for two recitations. Thinking about it makes me literally tremble, though it is a pleasant, exciting sort of tremble. To conclude the event, there will be a tableau—‘Grace, Hope and Charity.’ The performers in it will be Isolde, Opal, and myself, dressed in white drapery with our hair loose. Dressed as Hope, I must clasp my hands—like this—and look upward. My recitation practice will take place in the garret. If you listen to me groaning, do not feel frightened. A heartrending groan is required in one piece, and producing a proper artistic groan is actually difficult, Thirza. Flossie Tulk has become moody since she missed getting her desired role in the dialogue. Her wish was to play the fairy queen. Such a choice would be absurd, as a fairy queen with Flossie’s weight is unheard of. A fairy queen needs to be slim. The queen's part went to Odette Pullen, while I will act as a maid of honor to her. According to Flossie, a fairy with red hair is every bit as absurd as a heavy one, yet I refuse to let Flossie’s remarks bother me. My hair will feature a crown of white roses, and because I lack my own pair, Opal Pettigrew plans to loan me her slippers. After all, slippers are essential for fairies. Can you picture a fairy dressed in boots? Particularly ones featuring copper toes? The hall will be adorned by us using creeping spruce as well as fir mottoes filled with pink tissue-paper roses. Following the seating of the audience, everyone will process inside two by two to an organ march performed by Emma White. Oh, Thirza, though I realize your enthusiasm does not match mine, aren't you hoping that your little Nell brings honor to herself?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: “My sole wish is for you to act properly. When this whole commotion ends and you can finally quiet down, I will be truly relieved. chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: Nell let out a sigh and went to the back yard, where the boughs of the leafless poplars framed a young new moon shining out of a western sky of apple-green, and where Obed was chopping wood. Sitting down on a block, Nell discussed the concert with him, certain that she had found a listener who was both appreciative and sympathetic, on this occasion if no other.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Thorne and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
text: “Well now, I reckon it’s going to be a pretty good concert. And I expect you’ll do your part fine,” he said, looking down with a smile at her eager, lively little face. Nell returned his smile. Thirza handled that task entirely on her own; had it fallen to him, he would have been troubled by constant clashes between his desires and that obligation. Because of this setup, he had complete liberty to “spoil Nell”—to use Thirza’s expression—to his heart's content. Yet the situation worked out well enough; an occasional bit of “appreciation” can be just as beneficial as an abundance of dutiful “bringing up.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves
text: OBED was experiencing a disagreeable ten minutes. During the twilight of a chilly, gray December evening, he had entered the kitchen and sat down near the woodbox corner to remove his heavy boots, unaware that Nell and a group of her schoolmates were practicing “The Fairy Queen” inside the sitting room. Shortly afterward, they came trooping through the hall and into the kitchen, laughing and chatting merrily. Shrinking bashfully back into the shadows behind the woodbox while holding a boot in one hand and a bootjack in the other, Obed was not seen by them, and he shyly observed them for the aforementioned ten minutes while they put on caps and jackets and spoke about the dialogue and the concert. Nell stood in their midst, as bright eyed and animated as the rest; however, Obed all at once realized that there was something about her that differed from her companions. And what troubled Obed was that this distinction struck him as a thing that ought not to be present. Nell possessed a brighter face, alongside larger, starrier eyes, and finer features than the others; even shy, unobservant Obed had come to notice these aspects; yet the distinction that unsettled him was not found in any of these details. In what, then, did it lie?

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves
text: Obed remained troubled by this inquiry well after the young women had departed, hand in hand, along the lengthy, deeply frozen path and Nell had retreated to her reading. He was unable to bring it up to Thirza, who, he sensed, would certainly turn up her nose in disdain and observe that the sole distinction she perceived between Nell and the rest of the girls was that the others occasionally held their peace whereas Nell never ceased talking. Such an answer, Obed realized, would offer little assistance.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves
text: That night, he turned to his pipe to assist him in figuring it out, which greatly disgusted Thirza. Obed reached an answer to his dilemma following two hours of smoking and intense thought. The other girls did not dress the way Nell did!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves
text: As Obed pondered the issue further, his certainty grew that Nell had failed to dress like her peers at any point following her arrival at Grey Shutters. Thirza ensured her wardrobe consisted of simple, somber garments, which were entirely crafted from a single, unchanging design. Obed barely possessed an awareness that clothes followed shifting trends, yet he possessed complete certainty that the sleeves on Nell’s dresses bore no resemblance to those worn by her peers. His memory returned to the group of young girls who had gathered near her that night, each bright in a bodice of crimson, navy, rose, or ivory, causing him to question the reasons behind Thirza’s insistence on keeping her in such simple and subdued attire at all times.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves

Obed resolved to present her with one; undoubtedly nobody could oppose that as an unjustified interference on his part. Christmas lay merely two weeks away. An attractive, freshly made dress would serve as the ideal gift. Obed, exhaling a pleased sigh, stowed his pipe and retired to sleep, as Thirza flung open every door and ventilated the dwelling.
