Sitting on the steps, Elias Purdy was the very first individual we encountered, and he was mumbling to himself. When Odette inquired what in the world he was up to, he replied that he was reciting the multiplication table repeatedly to calm his anxiety and begged for goodness’ sake not to break his concentration, since pausing even briefly made him terrified and erased all the knowledge he had ever acquired, whereas the multiplication table anchored every piece of information securely where it belonged!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “When our rooms were assigned to us Miss Thorne was forced to depart from us. Odette and I took seats beside one another and Odette possessed such composure that it made me envious of her. Good, steady, sensible Odette had no requirement for the multiplication table! I questioned whether my appearance matched my feelings and whether my heart could be heard thumping by them all the way across the room. After that a man entered and started handing out the English examination sheets. My hands turned cold right then and my head literally spun as I lifted it. Merely one terrible moment—Isolde, my feelings were precisely the same as four years back when my request to stay at Grey Shutters was put to Thirza—and after that all became clear within my mind and my heart commenced beating once more—I neglected to mention that its beating had ceased entirely!—because I was aware that I could manage something with that paper at least.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “We returned home for dinner at noon, after which we went back for history in the afternoon. That history exam was quite difficult, and my dates became terribly confused. Even so, I believe my performance today was fairly good. However, oh, Isolde, the geometry exam takes place tomorrow, and contemplating it requires all the resolve I have to refrain from opening my Euclid. If I believed it would be of any assistance, I would recite the multiplication table continuously until tomorrow morning.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “This evening I went down for a visit with the other girls. As I was going, I encountered Elias Purdy walking about in a distracted manner. He told me he knew he had failed his history exam and was destined to disappoint his parents, so he intended to leave on the morning train; moreover, he remarked that working as a carpenter would be simpler than becoming a minister. I comforted him and convinced him to remain until the conclusion, pointing out that leaving early would be unkind to Miss Thorne. There are times when I have desired to be a boy, yet whenever I observe Elias Purdy, I feel grateful to be a girl and relieved that I am not his sister.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Opal was hysterical as I arrived at their boarding-house, having only recently realized the terrible error she committed on her English exam. After she calmed down, we traveled uptown to eat ice cream. We longed for you to be there alongside us.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Oh, Isolde, I wish the test in geometry was already finished! Still, as Mrs. Sowerby is accustomed to saying, the sun is going to keep coming up and going down regardless of my failing geometry. Though that is accurate, it does not bring much solace. My preference, I believe, would be for it to stop if I were to fail!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Yours devotedly,

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Nell”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: When the geometry test alongside the remaining exams concluded at the expected hour, Nell returned to her house that Friday night, feeling fairly exhausted yet carrying a subdued sense of victory. Isolde happened to be visiting Grey Shutters at the moment of her arrival, and their greeting was as dramatic as though an eternity had passed since they last saw each other.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “You dear old thing, seeing you return is absolutely wonderful. Your departure for town feels like an eternity ago, and oh, Nell, how did things go for you?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “I believe I did fairly well, except for geometry. Whether I passed that subject is uncertain to me, and I possess a strange, uneasy feeling that I failed. Ah, returning here brings such joy! Grey Shutters remains the most cherished, exquisite place on earth.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “In what manner did the rest perform?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “ Although the girls claim to be certain of their failure, my impression is that they performed quite admirably. According to Flossie, the geometry problem was simple enough for a ten-year-old child! Elias Purdy continues to believe he flopped in history, while Wilfred claims to have flunked algebra. Nevertheless, we remain completely in the dark and will continue to be until the pass list is published. Two weeks will pass before that happens. Imagine existing for a full fortnight in such anxiety! If only I could fall asleep and not awaken until the waiting is finished.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: Because Isolde recognized that inquiring about the outcome for Hugh Carrow would serve no purpose, she simply remarked:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Oh, you’ll get through without a problem. Do not fret.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “I’d rather not pass at all than not come out pretty well up on the list,” Nell declared impetuously, expressing the idea—which Isolde fully understood—that any victory would feel flawed and resentful unless she placed higher than Hugh Carrow.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: To achieve this goal, Nell had pushed herself to the utmost throughout the tests. Hugh had done the same. On twelve occasions they had encountered one another while walking, offering no indication of knowing each other, and on each occasion Nell had raised her chin slightly more, desired with greater intensity that she had befriended Hugh upon his request, and resolved with firmer intent to beat him in the test. She was aware that the entire lower school at Brierley debated who would take top place; she was aware as well that Ned Duckett and Jimmy Glover possessed a wager regarding the outcome and that Flossie Tulk had declared Hugh was certain to come first beyond any doubt; and she believed that missing the top spot would cause her unacceptable shame.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: Yet a different and finer reason urged her to succeed. On account of Obed and Thirza—Obed above all—she desired to “pass high.” Obed had stated to her his belief that she “would beat the whole Island.” Even in the most fantastical dreams, Nell believed, hoping for that was absurd. Nevertheless, she did earnestly wish to rank in the top ten at minimum, enabling her to watch Obed’s warm brown eyes shine with satisfaction at her accomplishment. For all her strenuous efforts and quiet labor over dry equations and conjugations, that, she thought, would truly be a delightful recompense.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: When the two weeks concluded, Nell began "haunting" the post office as well, alongside the agitated Odette, Opal, and Flossie, unsealing the Port Marlow newspapers with trembling fingers and chilled, nauseating sensations that rivaled any felt throughout the Entrance week. Wilfred and Hugh were equally willing to engage in this behavior, yet Elias Purdy remained firmly absent.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “I lack the courage to head over and examine a result sheet deliberately,” he confessed to Nell. “My plan is simply to hold off until a person arrives and abruptly informs me if I passed or failed.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: As three weeks passed with no pass list in sight, Nell started to think she truly was unable to bear the tension for much longer. She lost her appetite, and her enthusiasm for Brierley events waned. Mrs. Sowerby inquired about what other outcome one might anticipate when a Tory superintendent of education led affairs, while Obed, observing Nell’s pale face, her lack of interest, and the slow pace at which she returned from the post office each afternoon, commenced earnest consideration of whether he ought to cast a Grit vote in the upcoming election.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: However, the information arrived on a certain evening. Forgetful for the moment of world anxieties and examination troubles, Nell sat by her unclosed window and absorbed the charm of the summer twilight, which breathed sweet scents from the flowerbeds beneath and sounded whispering and rustling with the movement of poplar trees. The eastern heavens over the fir trees were tinted a delicate rose by the reflected light of the setting sun, and Nell was musing absently whether the spirit of color possessed such an appearance, when she noticed Isolde racing downward through the firs, across the log bridge, and up the incline, clutching a waving newspaper in her hand.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: Nell leapt up, immediately recognizing the contents of that document. The results of the examination were published! A feeling of dizziness overcame her head, and her heart pounded to the point of pain. She found herself incapable of taking a single step. To her, it felt like an hour passed prior to Isolde racing down the corridor and charging into the chamber without bothering to knock, driven by her immense state of agitation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Nell, you passed,” she exclaimed, “passed at the absolute top—you as well as Hugh—the two of you tied—however your name comes first. Oh, my heart is brimming with pride!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: Isolde cast the document upon the table and threw herself onto the bed belonging to Nell, completely winded and unable to say another word. Nell set fire to the lamp's wick, knocking over the match container and expending six matches prior to her trembling fingers completing the action. Following that, she grabbed the document. Indeed, she had succeeded—her name appeared at the absolute head of a roster containing two hundred! Existing for that single instant was genuinely worthwhile.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Nell, your performance was simply wonderful,” Isolde gasped out, regaining enough breath to sit upright and address her, since Nell, with glowing eyes and an enchanted expression, had remained completely silent. “Dad brought the newspaper from Alder River barely ten minutes back—it arrived via the afternoon train, as you are aware, and the post won't deliver it here until tomorrow—so the moment I spotted the list of successful candidates, I tore over here like a madwoman. All of you have succeeded, every single one, even Elias Purdy, though he has a condition in history. Odette and Opal scored fairly well—they are positioned in the middle—and Wilfred did too. Flossie barely made it with a mere three-point margin, yet you can bet she will act just as haughty as if she had come out on top. Won't Miss Thorne be thrilled? Oh, Nell, how does it feel to behold your own name right at the top of a pass list like that? Were I in your place, I am certain I would lose my mind from happiness. I feel almost wild with excitement myself, yet you remain as serene and chilled as a spring night.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “My mind is simply overwhelmed,” Nell stated. “There are a hundred things I wish to express, yet the phrasing eludes me. Such a thing was beyond my imagination—actually, no, I imagined it a single time! A single time I permitted myself to ponder, ‘What if the top position ends up being mine?’ with much trepidation, as you can imagine, because assuming I might top the Island felt exceedingly arrogant and conceited. Give me just a moment, Isolde. I need to dash out to the field immediately so I can inform Obed. After that, we will proceed up the road to share the fortunate report with everyone else.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: They rushed down to the hayfield beneath the barn, where Obed was making haycocks, and, fortunately, Mrs. Sowerby was conversing with Thirza by the lane fence.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Oh, Obed,” Nell cried out, “I got through, and my mark is at the top—or nearly at the top! Vanity isn't my motive, but gratitude is.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “Well now, I always said it,” Obed remarked, looking at the pass list with delight. “I knew you could beat them all easy.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “I must say, Nell, you have performed quite well,” Thirza remarked, attempting to conceal her deep pride in Nell from Mrs. Agatha’s discerning gaze. Nevertheless, that kind-hearted woman declared with warmth:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: “I simply reckon she has succeeded, and I would certainly not hold back from stating as much. You bring honor to your companions, Nell, indeed you do, and every one of us is proud of you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
text: Later that evening Nell, who concluded the enchanting night by having a grave short conversation with Mrs. Wace in the manse, was kneeling sweetly near her open window amid a grand radiance of moonlight and uttered a prayer of thanks and longing that originated directly from her heart. Within it was appreciation for days gone by along with a respectful plea for what lay ahead; and as she lay sleeping upon her white pillow her dreams proved to be just as lovely and brilliant and wonderful as a young girl could wish for.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Nell, you should definitely wear your white organdy,” Isolde firmly suggested.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: The east gable chamber held them both; beyond its walls lingered merely twilight—an exquisite twilight of yellowish-green beneath a cloudless, clear-blue expanse. Above the Whispering Wood hung a large round moon, which gradually intensified from a pale sheen to polished silver; the night air overflowed with delightful summer noises—the twitter of drowsy birds, capricious gusts of wind, and distant voices accompanied by laughter. However, within Nell’s chamber, the blind had been pulled down and the lamp turned on, because a significant dressing process was underway.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: The east gable bore little resemblance to how it had appeared four years earlier on that evening, when its starkness had chilled Nell to the very core of her soul with its unwelcoming coldness. Modifications had gradually taken place, with Thirza reluctantly tolerating them, to the point where it had become as charming and delicate a haven as any young woman might wish for.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Although the pink-rose velvet carpet and pink silk drapes of Nell’s youth had failed to appear, her aspirations had evolved alongside her maturity, making it unlikely that she mourned their absence. A lovely matting concealed the floor, while light-green art muslin formed the curtains that muted the tall window and moved in the stray gusts of wind. Rather than gold and silver brocade tapestry, a charming apple-blossom wallpaper covered the walls, which featured a handful of fine prints presented to Nell by Mrs. Wace. The position of prominence was held by Miss Thorne’s portrait, beneath which Nell made a tender ritual of placing blooming blossoms on the shelf. On this evening, a stalk of white lilies subtly scented the chamber like a remembered aroma. No “mahogany furniture” was present, yet the room contained a white-painted bookshelf stocked with volumes, a padded wicker rocking chair, a dressing table adorned with white muslin ruffles, an unusual mirror with a gilded frame topped by a curved apex painted with plump pink Cupids and purple grapes—which had previously belonged in the guest bedroom—and a low-built white bed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Nell was getting dressed because she was going to a concert at the Pale Sands Hotel. To assist the Port Marlow hospital, the guests had organized the event and had searched for every accessible amateur performer in the neighboring regions to contribute. A duet was requested from Bertha Sampson and Pearl Clay, who belonged to the Pale Sands Baptist choir; a violin solo was scheduled to be performed by Milton Clark of Stonebridge; a Scotch ballad was going to be sung by Winnie Adella Blair of Delford; and recitations were to be delivered by Laura Tranter of Tullyvale alongside Nell Harcourt of Brierley.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Just as Nell used to remark, the event marked “an epoch in her life,” and the sheer thrill of it left her delightfully electrified. Obed experienced supreme bliss from the sense of pride in the distinction given to his Nell, while Thirza felt almost as much delight, even if she would have perished before acknowledging it, claiming that she deemed it quite inappropriate for a group of youngsters to go roaming off to the hotel lacking an adult to supervise them.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: A double-seated buggy driven by Odette Pullen and her brother Barney was going to carry Nell and Isolde; moreover, various other Brierley girls and boys were attending as well. Out from town, a group of visitors was anticipated, and following the concert, the performers were to be served a supper.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Is the organdy truly going to be the finest choice?” Nell asked in an anxious manner. “My blue-flowered muslin seems prettier to me—and this one is definitely not as stylish.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “However, it fits you far better,” Isolde remarked. “It is very soft, frilled, and body-hugging. That muslin is rigid, giving you an overly formal appearance. Yet it appears as though the organdy developed naturally upon you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Nell let out a sigh and gave in. Isolde was starting to become known for her remarkable taste in attire, making her counsel on these matters highly desirable. On this specific evening, she looked quite attractive in a gown of that charming wild-rose pink, a shade from which Nell was permanently excluded; however, because she had no role in the concert, how she looked mattered less. Her entire effort was focused on Nell, whom she swore had to be attired, groomed, and decorated to suit the Regent’s liking for the sake of Brierley.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “ Tug that frill out slightly further—like that; come here and allow me to fasten your sash; now we shall attend to your slippers. My plan is to weave your hair into a pair of heavy plaits, securing them midway up using large white ribbons—stop, do not draw even one curl onto your brow—leave only the gentle parting. No other hairstyle you wear flatters you to the same degree, Nell, and Mrs. Wace remarks that your appearance resembles a Madonna whenever it is parted in this manner. I am going to pin this tiny white house rose right behind your ear. My bush bore merely a single blossom, which I preserved on your behalf.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Would it be all right if I wore my pearl beads?” Nell inquired. “A string of them was brought to me from town by Obed last week, and I am certain he would enjoy seeing me wear them.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Isolde pressed her lips together, tilted her dark head thoughtfully to evaluate the options, and ultimately chose the beads, which were subsequently fastened about the slender, alabaster neck of Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “You have such a stylish quality, Nell,” Isolde remarked, admiring her without envy. “The way you carry your head gives you quite an air. My guess is it comes from your figure. Me, I am merely a dumpling. It has been a constant fear of mine, and now my suspicion is confirmed. Oh well, I guess I must simply accept it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “However, you possess such dimples,” spoken by Nell, who smiled fondly into the lovely, lively face that was close to her. “Charming dimples, similar to small depressions in cream. I have abandoned any expectation of dimples. My dream of having dimples will not be realized; yet a great number of my dreams have been fulfilled, so I should not protest. Am I completely prepared now?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Everything is prepared,” Isolde stated when Thirza stepped into the threshold, appearing as a lean form whose hair was more silvered than before and whose sharp contours remained, though her expression was considerably gentler. “Walk straight inside and see our reciter, Thirza. Is she not beautiful?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Thirza produced a noise that fell somewhere between a grunt and a sniff.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Her appearance is tidy and respectable. That hairstyle of hers appeals to me. However, she will probably spoil that gown while traveling over there through the dust and dampness, plus it seems almost overly light for such chilly evenings. Organdy is absolutely the most impractical material imaginable, a point I expressed to Obed when he purchased it. Yet talking to Obed these days serves no purpose. There was a period when he listened to my counsel, but currently he merely purchases items for Nell without care, and the Delford shop employees realize they can sell him whatever they wish. If they simply inform him that an item is attractive and stylish, Obed surrenders his cash instantly for it. Make certain your skirt stays away from the wheel, Nell, and wear your heavy coat.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Afterward, Thirza marched down the stairs, reflecting with pride on how charming Nell appeared, featuring that

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “One ray of moonshine extending from the forehead unto the crown”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: and feeling regret that she was unable to attend the concert in person to listen to her daughter's recitation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “I wonder whether my dress will suffer from the dampness,” Nell remarked with concern.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Not in the least,” Isolde remarked, raising the window shade. “The night is flawless, and dew will not form. Observe the moonlight.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “I’m so happy that my window faces east toward the rising sun,” said Nell, walking across to Isolde. “It’s truly wonderful watching the morning emerge above those distant hills and shine through those pointed fir tops. Every morning it is brand new, and I feel as though my actual soul is washed in that stream of initial sunlight. Oh, Isolde, I cherish this small room so deeply. I cannot imagine how I will manage without it when I depart for town next month.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Please avoid mentioning that you are leaving this evening,” pleaded Isolde. “Thinking about it makes me feel extremely unhappy, and my desire is to enjoy myself tonight. What piece will you be reciting, Nell? Also, do you feel anxious?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “By no means. Having performed so many times before an audience, it doesn't bother me in the least anymore. My choice is to perform ‘The Maiden’s Vow.’ Its tone is very moving. A humorous piece will be performed by Laura Tranter, yet bringing tears to the audience appeals to me more than bringing laughter.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “If you are encored, what will you recite?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “They will not even think about asking me for an encore,” sneered Nell, although she harbored her own private wishes that they might, and she was currently imagining recounting the entire affair to Obed when they sat down for breakfast the following day. “That must be Barney and Odette arriving—I can hear the carriage wheels. Let’s go.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Barney Pullen demanded that Nell sit beside him on the front seat, causing her to climb up against her wishes. Sitting in the back with the girls would have been far more to her liking, as she could have chattered and laughed as much as she pleased. Barney possessed very little capacity for either chatter or laughter. Being a large, overweight, emotionless twenty-year-old lad, he had a round face devoid of expression and an agonizing inability to hold a conversation. Nevertheless, his admiration for Nell was vast, and the thought of traveling to Pale Sands accompanied by the slender, straight-backed figure at his side filled him with immense pride.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Nell, through the effort of chatting behind her back to the girls and now and then tossing a courteous word to Barney—who smirked and laughed softly, never managing to devise an answer until the moment had passed—managed to take pleasure in the ride regardless of everything. The night was made for taking pleasure. The avenue swarmed with buggies, every single one heading toward the hotel, and laugher, pure as silver, reverberated again and again down its length. By the time they arrived at the hotel, light poured brilliantly from every floor. The women from the concert committee greeted them, and one of these ladies escorted Nell away to the performers' dressing room, a space packed with the members of a Port Marlow Symphony Club, in whose presence Nell abruptly experienced shyness, fear, and a sense of being rustic. Her gown, which had appeared so delicate and lovely inside the east gable, appeared basic and ordinary now—excessively basic and ordinary, it struck her, amid the numerous silks and laces shimmering and swishing all around her. How did her pearl beads measure up to the diamonds belonging to the large, striking woman beside her? Moreover, how pathetic her single tiny white rose had to appear next to the abundant hothouse blossoms worn by everyone else! Nell set her hat and jacket aside, cowering unhappily in a corner. She longed to be returned to the white room located at Grey Shutters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Her situation grew even more unpleasant when she shortly afterward reached the stage of the hotel’s large concert hall. Her eyes were blinded by the bright electric lamps, while she felt confused by the heavy fragrance and the drone of voices. She desired to be seated among the spectators alongside Isolde and Odette, who appeared to be enjoying themselves immensely far in the rear. Her position was compressed between a large woman wearing pink silk and a lofty, contemptuous young woman in a gown of white lace. Now and then, the large woman would pivot her head directly toward Nell to examine her through her eyeglasses, making Nell, who felt deeply bothered by this intense observation, feel as though a loud scream would burst from her; meanwhile, the young woman in white lace continuously remarked to the person beside her, loud enough to be heard, concerning the “country bumpkins” and “rustic belles” among the spectators, while lazily looking forward to “such fun” provided by the performances of area participants listed on the schedule. Nell felt certain that her hatred for that girl in the white-lace dress would last as long as she lived.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: It was bad luck for Nell that a hotel guest happened to be a professional elocutionist who had agreed to give a performance. This woman was supple, possessing dark eyes, and she wore an incredible dress made of a sparkling gray material that resembled woven moonbeams, along with jewels adorning her throat and her dark locks. Her voice possessed an extraordinary flexibility alongside an amazing expressive capacity, causing the spectators to react with extreme enthusiasm to her piece. For the moment, Nell paid no attention to herself or her difficulties, listening with entranced, glowing eyes; however, once the performance concluded, she abruptly covered her face using her hands. Standing up to recite after such an act was impossible for her—completely out of the question. Was it possible she had previously believed she possessed the ability to recite? Oh, how she wished to be back at Grey Shutters!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: In this unfavorable instant, they called her name. Nell—who failed to see the somewhat guilty small jump of astonishment made by the girl in white lace, and who would not have grasped the delicate praise it suggested even if she had noticed—somehow rose, walking in a daze toward the front. Her face had grown so drained of color that, seated in the audience below, Isolde and Odette gripped one another's hands out of anxious empathy.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: A crushing wave of stage fright overwhelmed Nell. Although she had frequently given public recitations, an assembly like this had never confronted her before, and her energies were totally paralyzed by the vision of it. Every element—the lines of women wearing evening gowns, the discerning expressions, the entire environment of affluence and refinement surrounding her—proved exceedingly unfamiliar, dazzling, and disorienting. This contrasted sharply with the unadorned seating at the Debating Club, which was occupied by the familiar, kind expressions of acquaintances and townspeople. She believed these individuals would judge her without mercy. They probably expected entertainment from her “rustic” endeavors, just as the white-lace girl did. She experienced a feeling of shame and misery that was entirely beyond hope or help. A terrifying lightheadedness overtook her, her heart fluttered, and her knees shook; no speech could leave her mouth, and she would have escaped the stage the very next instant, notwithstanding the disgrace that she believed would permanently become her lot if she ran away.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: However, abruptly, while her wide, terrified eyes stared across the listeners, she spotted Hugh Carrow far at the rear of the hall, leaning frontward with a grin upon his countenance—a grin that appeared to Nell simultaneously victorious and mocking. Actually, it was not that at all. Hugh was simply grinning in admiration of the entire event overall, and specifically of the impression created by Nell’s slim white figure and ethereal face set before a backdrop of palms. Flossie Tulk, whom he had brought in his carriage, was seated next to him, and her expression truly was simultaneously victorious and mocking. Yet Nell failed to spot Flossie, and had she done so, she would not have minded. She sucked in a deep breath and threw her head backward with pride, bravery and resolve rushing through her like a jolt of electricity. She refused to falter in front of Hugh Carrow—he must not ever have the chance to mock her, not ever, not ever! Her terror and anxiety disappeared; and she commenced her performance, her distinct, lovely tone carrying to the most distant area of the hall with no shake or interruption. Composure had been entirely regained by her, and amid the bounce-back from that terrible instance of helplessness, she performed in a manner she had never achieved previously. As she concluded, there occurred explosions of genuine praise. Nell, moving backward toward her chair, turning red from modesty and joy, had her hand firmly gripped and moved by the heavy woman dressed in pink silk.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “My dear, you performed wonderfully,” she gasped out. “I have been weeping like an infant, truly I have. Listen, they are calling for an encore—they will definitely make you return!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Oh, I am unable to go,” Nell said in a state of confusion. “However—I have to, or else Obed is going to be disappointed. He stated that I would receive an encore from them.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “In that case, ensure you do not let Obed down,” uttered the lady in pink, emitting a laugh.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Wearing a smile and a blush, her eyes clear, Nell stepped back out and delivered an endearing, amusing short piece that charmed those listening even more. Her entire remaining evening proved to be a modest success.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: At the conclusion of the concert, the plump, rosy woman—the spouse of a wealthy American—escorted her around and presented her to all the guests, all of whom treated her with great kindness. The career reciter, Mrs. Evans, approached and conversed with her, remarking that her voice was delightful and that she “interpreted” her pieces marvellously. A faint, indifferent word of praise was even offered to her by the girl in white lace. In the grand, splendidly adorned dining hall, they ate supper; because they accompanied Nell, Isolde and Odette received an invitation to join in this meal as well, but Barney could not be located anywhere, having fled out of sheer dread of receiving a similar offer. Nevertheless, he was waiting for them alongside the team once everything had concluded, and the trio of girls stepped cheerfully outside into the peaceful, pale glow of the moonlight. Drawing a deep breath, Nell gazed up at the limpid sky past the shadowy branches of the fir trees.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: Ah, escaping once more into the night's untainted quiet felt truly wonderful! Everything possessed such vastness, stillness, and marvel, filled with the echoing hum of the ocean while the shadowy precipices past it resembled stern behemoths protecting spellbound shores.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Wasn’t that an absolutely marvelous occasion?” Odette murmured, while they rode off. “If only I were a wealthy American who could pass the summer months residing in a hotel, donning gems and decollete gowns, and eating chicken salad along with ice cream each and every day. That must be vastly superior to working as a teacher. Your performance was truly wonderful, Nell, even though it initially seemed to me as if you would not start at all. It surpassed Mrs. Evans’s, in my opinion.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Oh, no, do not utter such remarks, Odette,” Nell said rapidly, “for it seems foolish. It could not possibly surpass Mrs. Evans’s, you see, since she works as a professional, whereas I am merely a schoolgirl possessing a slight talent for recitation. I am entirely content provided the audience simply enjoyed mine reasonably well.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Nell, I have a compliment to pass on to you,” Isolde remarked. “Considering the tone he used, I am fairly sure it has to be a compliment. In any case, a portion of it was. Directly behind Odette and myself sat an American—a man who looked so romantic, possessing coal-black hair together with eyes of the same shade. According to Flossie Tulk, he is an eminent artist, and the cousin of her mother in Boston has married a man who formerly attended school alongside him. Anyhow, we overheard him remarking—isn't that right, Odette?—‘Which girl is that on the platform with the magnificent Titian hair? Her face is one I would love to paint.’ So there you are, Nell. However, what is the meaning of Titian hair?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “If it is translated, it stands for simple red, I suppose,” Nell giggled. “Titian was an extremely renowned painter who enjoyed portraying women with red hair.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Were you looking at every one of the diamonds worn by those ladies?” Odette asked with a sigh. “They shone so brightly. Wouldn’t you girls adore being wealthy?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “We are rich,” Nell stated firmly. “Why, sixteen years stand to our credit, and we enjoy the happiness of queens, and imaginations belong to all of us, to one degree or another. Direct your gaze to that sea, girls—entirely composed of silver, shadow, and visions of unseen things. Having millions of dollars and strands of diamonds would not enable us to appreciate its beauty any further. You would refuse to transform into any of those women if the choice were yours. Would it be your desire to become that white-lace girl, bearing a bitter expression throughout your existence, as though your very birth occurred with your nose turned up at everything? Or the pink lady, pleasant and good-natured though she may be, yet so heavy and low of stature that a figure is truly lacking? Or even Mrs. Evans, possessing that deeply, deeply sorrowful expression within her eyes? A terrible unhappiness must have befallen her at some point to produce such an expression. You know you would not, Odette Pullen!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “I am not sure—precisely,” Odette stated without conviction. “My belief is that a person would find much solace in diamonds.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
text: “Well, I have no desire to be anybody other than myself, even should I remain unsoothed by diamonds for the rest of my days,” Nell announced. “Being Nell of Grey Shutters suits me fine, along with my pearl bead strand. I am certain that Obed bestowed just as much affection upon me through them as was ever attached to Madame the Pink Lady’s gems.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: At Grey Shutters, the subsequent three weeks were filled with activity, as Nell prepared for her departure to Regent’s, requiring a great deal of needlework alongside numerous matters to discuss and organize. Because Obed ensured it, Nell possessed a generous and attractive wardrobe, with Thirza surprisingly raising not a single complaint about any of his purchases or ideas. Furthermore, carrying a bundle of fine, light green fabric in her arms, she walked up to the east gable one night.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Nell, I have a piece of fabric for a lovely light gown for you. It’s likely not an absolute necessity; you possess a great deal of attractive waists; yet it occurred to me that perhaps you would desire something truly elegant to put on should anyone invite you out somewhere during a night in town, for a gathering or an occasion of that nature. It has reached my ears that Odette, Opal, and Flossie possess ‘evening dresses,’ using their terminology, and I have no intention of letting you fall behind them. Mrs. Wace assisted me in selecting it in town during the previous week, and our plan is to have Emily Pettigrew craft it for you. Emily possesses taste, and nobody can match her fits.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Oh, Thirza, this is simply wonderful,” Nell expressed. “I appreciate it very much. You really shouldn't treat me with such goodness—it renders my departure more difficult with each passing day.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: The green gown was fashioned with all the tucks, frills, and shirrings that Emily’s preference allowed. One night, Nell donned it to show Obed and Thirza, and she performed “The Maiden’s Vow” for their entertainment in the kitchen. Observing the luminous, lively visage and elegant movements, Thirza found her mind drifting to the night Nell had come to Grey Shutters, with recollection bringing forth a clear image of the peculiar, terrified young girl in her absurd yellowish-brown wincey frock, intense sorrow gazing from her eyes full of tears. A element within that remembrance caused tears to spring to Thirza’s eyes as well.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Upon my word, the story I told has brought tears to your eyes, Thirza,” Nell remarked cheerfully, bending down to the chair where Thirza sat to plant a fleeting kiss upon the woman's cheek. “Indeed, I consider that a clear victory.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “No, your poem didn’t make me cry,” Thirza declared, as she would have felt humiliated to let mere poetic verse cause her to show such vulnerability. “It’s just that I was unable to stop picturing how you used to be as a small child, Nell. And I found myself hoping you might remain a child forever, despite every one of your strange habits. At this point you are an adult and leaving us; furthermore, wearing that attire makes you appear remarkably tall, elegant, and—and—completely changed—as though Brierley isn't your home anymore—and pondering every bit of it simply made me feel lonely.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Thirza!” Nell positioned herself on Thirza’s gingham-covered lap, held Thirza’s wrinkled face with both hands, and gazed with seriousness and affection into Thirza’s eyes. “I am not altered at all—not in truth. I have merely been trimmed back and grown new limbs. The genuine me—deep inside—remains unaltered. No matter where my journey leads or how extensive my exterior transformations are, it will not alter a single thing; fundamentally, I will perpetually remain your little Nell, loving you, Obed, and beloved Grey Shutters increasingly with each passing day.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: Nell pressed her youthful, smooth cheek to the withered one belonging to Thirza, extending her hand simultaneously to tap Obed’s shoulder. Thirza longed greatly at that moment to hold the ability Nell had to express her emotions verbally; yet her disposition and custom had decreed a different reality, leaving her capable only of wrapping her arms tightly around her girl and clutching her lovingly to her chest, hoping she would never have to release her.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: With a suspicious wetness showing in his eyes, Obed stood up and stepped outside. He paced in a state of agitation beneath the stars of the blue summer night, crossing the yard to reach the gate situated under the poplars.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Well now, I suppose she hasn’t been spoiled very much,” he murmured, with pride. “I suppose my stepping in now and then didn’t do much damage when all is said and done. She’s clever and beautiful, and affectionate, too, which surpasses everything else. She’s been a godsend to us, and a more fortunate error than the one Mrs. Tranter made never existed—if luck had anything to do with it. I don’t think it was anything of the sort. It was Divine Intervention, since I calculate the Almighty perceived that we required her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: The arrival of the day when Nell had to depart for town lastly occurred. On a splendid September morning, she and Obed journeyed there by carriage, following a tear-filled goodbye with Isolde and a tearless, sensible one—from Thirza's perspective, at any rate—with Thirza. However, once Nell had departed, Isolde wiped her eyes and attended an outing on the shore at Pale Sands alongside a few of her relatives from Delford, where she managed to have a fairly pleasant time; whereas Thirza threw herself violently into unneeded chores and persisted in them the entire day with the most resentful sort of grief—a pain that seethes and consumes and is unable to cleanse itself through easy weeping. Yet during that evening, as Thirza retired to rest, intensely and sorrowfully aware that the small gabled bedchamber at the hallway's termination held no vibrant youthful presence and was untouched by any gentle breath, she pressed her face into her pillow, crying for her child with a fury of weeping that terrified her once she became peaceful enough to ponder the great wickedness of grieving so intensely over a flawed human being.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: Nell, alongside the remaining scholars from Brierley, arrived in town barely soon enough to rush to the Academy. A flurry of excitement characterized that initial day, which went by agreeably as they met every new student, learned to recognize the professors by sight, and were grouped and arranged into classes. Having been recommended to do so by Miss Thorne, Nell planned to pursue the Second Year work; Hugh Carrow chose to follow the same path. Should they succeed, this choice involved acquiring a First Class teacher’s license within a single year rather than two; nevertheless, it likewise demanded a great deal more labor of a more difficult nature. Because they were unbothered by ambitious impulses, Odette, Opal, Flossie, Wilfred, and Elias Purdy were satisfied to begin the Second Class work. Nell felt a sudden sting of isolation upon realizing she shared a room with fifty different students, every one of them a stranger except for the tall, brown-haired boy on the other side of the space; furthermore, as she morosely considered, her particular acquaintance with him offered little comfort. Even so, she was indisputably pleased regarding their placement in the identical class; their accustomed competition might still continue, and Nell would scarcely have understood how to proceed without its presence.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “It would be uncomfortable for me to be without it,” was her thought. “Hugh appears remarkably resolute. Right now, in this place, I imagine he is deciding to capture the medal. His chin is so magnificent! It never caught my attention until now. If only Odette and Opal had also entered for First Class. Even so, once I become familiar with everyone, I probably will not feel quite so out of place. I am curious about which girls in this room will become my friends. Contemplating it is truly fascinating. Naturally, I gave my word to Isolde that I would never hold any Regent’s girl as close to my heart as I hold her, regardless of how much I affection I develop for her; nevertheless, I possess plenty of secondary affection to share. That girl who has brown eyes and a crimson waist appeals to me. Vibrant and rosy-red is how she appears; then there is the pale, light-haired one who is staring through the window. Her hair is exquisite, and she has the appearance of someone who understands a bit about dreams. Getting to know both of them would be wonderful for me—knowing them thoroughly—enough to wrap my arm around their waists as we walk, and to use pet names for them. However, at this precise moment, we are strangers to one another, and they likely have no special desire to get to know me. Oh, how lonely it is!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: A deeper solitude settled over Nell as dusk fell and she remained by herself in her hall bedroom that evening. Because every other girl had local kin to show her compassion, Nell was not going to live with them. Although Miss Lavinia Pembroke desired to host her, the great distance between Beechwood and the Academy made this impossible; consequently, Miss Pembroke searched for a rooming house, guaranteeing to Obed and Thirza that Nell would find it ideal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “The woman managing it is a lady of diminished fortune,” Miss Pembroke clarified. “A British officer was her husband, and she exercises great caution regarding the kind of boarders she accepts. Under her roof, Nell will never encounter any undesirable people. Good food is served, and the residence stands close to the Academy, situated within a peaceful area.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: Though all of this could be entirely correct, as it ultimately turned out to be, it brought no real comfort to Nell when she was overcome by the initial pangs of homesickness. She gazed despondently around the small, cramped bedchamber, taking in its unadorned, drab-papered walls, its tiny iron bedframe, and its vacant bookshelf; meanwhile, a terrible lump formed in her throat at the memory of her white bedroom at Grey Shutters, where she could comfortably feel the presence of the expansive, quiet green outdoors, the sweet peas blooming in the garden, the moonlight shining over the orchard, the stream running down the slope, the spruce branches swaying in the evening breeze further off, the immense starry heavens, and the glow from Isolde’s window beaming through the opening among the trees. Nothing like that existed in this place; Nell was aware that just beyond her window lay a paved street, a web of telephone wires blocking the sky, the footsteps of unfamiliar passersby, and countless lights illuminating the faces of strangers. Realizing that tears were imminent, she tried to resist them.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “I will not weep. It is foolish—and feeble—a third tear has dropped past my nose. Further ones are arriving! I need to recall something amusing to prevent them. Yet nothing is amusing unless it relates to Brierley, and that merely aggravates matters—four—five—I am returning home on the coming Friday, though that feels a century off. Oh, Obed has almost reached home by this time—and Thirza stands at the gate, gazing along the lane to spot him—six—seven—eight—oh, counting them is pointless! They will be pouring out like a deluge shortly. I am unable to feel happier—I have no desire to feel happier. Being wretched is preferable!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: A torrent of weeping undoubtedly would have arrived if Flossie Tulk had not shown up right then. Because she was happy to behold an acquainted visage, Nell no longer remembered that she and Flossie had never shared much affection. Even a Tulk was a sight she received gladly as a piece of Brierley existence.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “I’m really happy you made the trip up,” Nell remarked with genuine warmth.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “You’ve been weeping,” Flossie observed, showing an irritating sympathy. “I imagine you’re missing home—certain folks possess so little restraint regarding that. I certainly don't plan to be homesick, let me assure you. City life is far too wonderful after that dull old Brierley. I marvel at how I managed to survive there for such a long time. You ought not to weep, Nell; it fails to flatter you, because your nose and eyes turn crimson, making you appear completely flushed. I had an absolutely delightful experience at the Academy today. Our French instructor is a total sweetheart. The sight of his moustache would make your heart flutter. Do you possess any food nearby, Nell? I am genuinely ravenous. Ah, I suspected it was probable Thirza would pack you full of cake. That is the reason I came by. If not for that, I would have proceeded to the park so I could listen to the band perform alongside Frank Stockley. He resides at the same lodging as I do, and he is a fun-loving fellow. He spotted you during class today, and inquired of me who the auburn-haired girl was. I informed him that you were an orphan whom the Abernethys had taken in, and no one understood a great deal regarding what your background was prior to that.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: Nell was questioning whether being alone and weeping might actually be preferable to Flossie Tulk’s company when Odette and Opal arrived, both boastfully wearing an inch of Regent’s color ribbon—scarlet and purple—pinned upon their coats. Because Flossie was not “speaking” to Odette at that moment, she was forced to settle into a state of relative harmlessness.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Well,” Odette uttered with a sigh, “it seems to me like I’ve existed through numerous moons since this morning. My presence is required at home to review my Virgil—twenty lines were assigned to us by that miserable old professor to begin tomorrow. Tonight, however, settling down to study was simply impossible for me. Nell, it appears to me that I spot evidence of weeping. Own up if you have been crying. My self-respect will be restored by it, since I was crying abundantly until Opal arrived. Being a goose does not bother me quite as much when another person is also goosey. Cake? A teeny slice will be given to me by you, won't it? Thank you. The genuine Brierley flavor is present in it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: Noticing the Regent’s calendar resting on the table, Opal inquired whether Nell intended to compete for the gold medal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: Her face reddened as Nell acknowledged that the thought had crossed her mind.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “Oh, I almost forgot,” Flossie remarked, “Regent’s will receive a scholarship from Avery in the end. Information arrived today. I learned it from Frank Stockley—you are aware that his uncle serves on the board of governors. Tomorrow, the Academy will announce it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: A scholarship for Avery! Nell was conscious of her heart thumping faster, and as though through enchantment, the boundaries of her hope moved and expanded. Prior to Flossie sharing the information, the absolute summit of Nell's desires had been a provincial license for teaching, First Class, when the year concluded, and maybe the medal! Yet presently, within a single instant, Nell envisioned herself gaining the Avery scholarship, pursuing an Arts degree at Wexcombe College, and finishing her studies wearing a gown and mortar board, even before the reverberation of Flossie’s statement had faded. Because the Avery scholarship was awarded in English, and Nell believed that in this subject she stood upon familiar ground.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: A rich maker of goods from New Brunswick passed away, bequeathing a portion of his wealth to fund numerous scholarships that were to be divided among different academies and high schools in the Maritime Provinces, based on their individual ranks. Considerable uncertainty had existed regarding whether Regent’s would receive one, yet the issue was finally resolved, and when the year concluded, two hundred and fifty dollars annually for four years at Wexcombe College would be awarded to the graduate achieving the top score in English and English Literature. It was no surprise that Nell’s cheeks were burning as she retired to bed that evening!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl
text: “I will secure that scholarship if I can achieve it through hard work,” she determined. “Wouldn’t Obed feel pride if I managed to become a B.A.? Oh, having ambitions brings such delight. I am extremely pleased that I possess so many. And the finest part is that they never appear to cease. The moment you reach one goal, you spot another sparkling even higher above. It renders existence so captivating.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Her weekend trips to her house were a big assistance in fading away NELL’S longing for home. Every Friday evening, provided the mild weather continued, those who attended Brierley took the new branch line to travel to Delford. A cheerful group of them would all journey to Brierley on foot after Isolde, along with various other Brierley youths, usually arrived to greet them. Nell felt that the finest and sweetest times of the entire week were those Friday night rambles through the cool, bright air across the autumn hills, while the lights of home in Brierley shimmered in the distance.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Almost all the time, Hugh Carrow accompanied Opal Pettigrew on her walks and tote her bag for her. Opal was a most attractive young woman, who at present considered herself just as mature as she actually was; her skirts were worn as long as her mother permitted, and her hair was styled up while she was in town, even though she was required to let it down upon returning home. Her eyes were big and vivid blue, her skin radiant, and her shape full and eye-catching. She indulged in much laughter, maintained a sunny and pleasant disposition, and openly delighted in the enjoyable aspects of living.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “However, I don’t believe she is the kind of girl Hugh would enjoy,” Odette murmured in a whisper to Nell. Nell shared that opinion, yet not even the Avery scholarship would have induced her to express it. Furthermore, she was unable to avoid thinking that possessing a friend like Hugh would be delightful, allowing one to joke, talk idly, and trade thoughts regarding books, studies, and future goals. Hugh possessed goals, as she was aware, and Opal Pettigrew appeared not to be the type of individual with whom a person could gainfully converse about them.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Nell entertained no foolish sentimentality regarding her thoughts on Hugh. To her mind, on the rare occasions she considered them, boys were simply potential good companions. Had a friendship existed between herself and Hugh, the number of his other companions or the identity of his walking partners would not have mattered to her. Friendship was her natural talent; while she possessed numerous female friends, she felt an indistinct awareness that male comradeship could likewise prove beneficial in completing one's ideas of fellowship and providing wider viewpoints for evaluation and comparison. Naturally, Nell would have been unable to express her sentiments on the topic in precisely those explicit terms. Nevertheless, she believed that had Hugh ever accompanied her on the journey home from the train, across the frosty meadows and down the fern-lined lanes, they could have engaged in numerous cheerful and captivating discussions concerning the emerging realm expanding before them, alongside their personal aspirations and desires within it. Hugh was a smart youth who possessed individual perspectives on matters, coupled with a resolve to extract the finest elements from existence while contributing his utmost to it. Opal Pettigrew informed Odette Pullen that she failed to comprehend half of the statements made by Hugh Carrow; he conversed in the exact manner as Nell Harcourt during one of her reflective moods, and as far as she was concerned, she found no enjoyment in troubling herself with literature and similar topics when it was not required. Frank Stockley exhibited much superior energy and spirit, yet he lacked even half of Hugh’s attractive appearance, leaving her truly incapable of determining which one she preferred!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Within the Academy, Nell slowly gathered around herself a small group of companions, who were contemplative, creative, and driven scholars just like she was. She quickly grew close to Mabel Colby, the “rose-red” girl, and Honora Hollis, the “dream girl,” discovering that this last fair, ethereal-appearing young woman was thoroughly packed with mischief, jokes, and humor, whereas the striking, dark-eyed Mabel possessed a heart brimming with yearning dreams and imaginations, which were as light and multicolored as those belonging to Nell herself.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: When the Christmas holidays ended, the students at Brierley stopped returning home on Fridays and devoted themselves to rigorous study. By then, every scholar from Regent’s had moved into their respective positions within the ranks, and the different classes had taken on clear, fixed traits of personality. Some details were now commonly agreed upon. People acknowledged that those competing for the medal were effectively reduced to three—Hugh Carrow, Nell Harcourt, and Penrose Wilson; the recipient of the Avery scholarship remained less certain, as any member of a particular group of six might win it. A chubby, amusing, small boy from the up-country, who possessed a bumpy forehead and a mended coat, was viewed as virtually certain to capture the bronze medal for mathematics.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: At the Academy that year, Opal Pettigrew was the most beautiful girl; among the Second Year classes, the beauty prize was won by Mabel Colby, though a minor yet discerning group preferred Nell Harcourt. Everyone qualified to judge agreed that Ethel Marr possessed the most fashionable hairstyles, while Odette Pullen—unassuming, hardworking, dutiful Odette—won top marks in domestic science. Flossie Tulk even achieved her own distinction for being the most caustic-tongued young woman attending Regent’s. Thus, one could justly claim that the former students of Miss Thorne maintained their prominence within the larger sphere of the academical curriculum.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Nell applied herself diligently and without pause. The competition between her and Hugh remained just as fierce as it was during their time at Brierley school, even if the rest of the class remained unaware of it, yet the resentment behind it had inexplicably vanished. Winning merely to triumph over Hugh was no longer Nell's goal; instead, she sought the honorable satisfaction of a hard-earned triumph against a respectable opponent. Succeeding would certainly be gratifying, but failing to do so no longer felt to her like an endurable existence was impossible.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Even with their studies, the pupils discovered chances to enjoy themselves. Nell passed a large portion of her free time at Beechwood, where she usually had her Sunday meals and accompanied Miss Pembroke to services. The old lady confessed that she was getting on in years, yet her dark eyes remained sharp, and her speech lost none of its original force. However, she refrained from directing her harsh words at Nell, who remained a special favorite of the discerning elder.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “That Nell-girl gets better continually,” she remarked. “Other girls weary me—they possess a sameness so annoying and endless. Nell possesses a rainbow’s many hues, with each hue being the most beautiful while present. I am uncertain if her ability to amuse matches her childhood days, yet she compels my affection, and my preference goes to those who compel my affection. Doing so spares me immense effort in forcing myself to feel affection for them.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Then, nearly prior to anyone recognizing it, the arrival of spring occurred; over in Brierley, the Mayflowers were showing pink hues on the withered barrens where remnants of snow remained; and the woods and valleys bore the “mist of green.” However, inside Port Marlow, anxious Regent’s students concentrated their thoughts and conversations solely on examinations.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “It hardly seems believable that the term is almost at an end,” Nell said. “Why, during last fall it felt like such a long time ahead—an entire winter filled with studies and classes. And now here we stand, with the exams drawing near next week. Girls, at times I get the feeling that those exams are the only thing that matters, yet whenever I observe the large buds expanding on those chestnut trees and the hazy blue atmosphere at the street ends, they lose half of their significance.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Odette, along with Opal and Flossie, who had paid a visit, held a different opinion on the matter. In their eyes, the approaching tests were perpetually of immense significance—much more critical than Maytime hazes or chestnut buds. While it was fine for Nell, who was certain to pass at minimum, to occasionally minimize their importance, one could not look at them dispassionately when one’s entire destiny hinged upon them, which the girls genuinely believed theirs did.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “In the past fortnight, I have dropped seven pounds,” Odette sighed. “Telling me not to fret is pointiess. I am going to fret. Fretting gives a little relief—as though you are taking action while you fret. Failing to obtain my certificate would be terrible, having attended Regent’s the whole winter and spent such a large sum of money.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “It makes no difference to me,” Flossie Tulk declared. “Should I fail to pass during this year, I shall return for the following one. Paying for me to attend is well within my father's means. Nell, according to Frank Stockley, Professor Tremaine mentioned that Hugh Carrow was certain to receive the medal, whereas Emily Clay would probably be awarded the Avery scholarship.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “Tomorrow that might cause me to feel badly, Flossie,” Nell laughed, “yet right now I genuinely believe that provided I am aware that the violets are blooming all purple down in the hollow under Grey Shutters and that small ferns are pushing their heads up in Lovers’ Lane, it does not matter very much whether I win the Avery or fail to. I have given my best effort and I am starting to grasp the meaning of the ‘joy of the strife.’ Second only to trying and succeeding, the finest thing is trying and losing. Girls, stop speaking about exams! Observe that arch of light green sky above those houses and imagine for yourself how it has to look above the purply-dark beech-woods behind Brierley.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: “Odette, what will you be wearing for commencement?” Opal inquired sensibly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s
text: Odette and Flossie both replied simultaneously, and the conversation strayed into a secondary current regarding fashions. But Nell, resting her elbows on the window sill, placing her soft cheek against her interlocked hands, and having her eyes brimming with visions, gazed out without paying attention past city roof and spire toward that magnificent dome of sunset sky and fashioned her dreams of a potential future out of the golden fabric of youth’s inherent optimism. Every bit of the Beyond belonged to her, its possibilities hiding rosily within the approaching years—with every year being a rose of promise meant to be crafted into an everlasting chaplet.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: UPON the day that the last scores for every test were scheduled for display on the Regent’s notice board, Nell alongside Odette traversed the road in each other's company. Grinning and joyful, Odette felt relieved that testing had concluded, feeling pleasantly certain of having secured a passing mark minimum; additional worries did not disturb Odette in the least; possessing no grand aspirations, she remained undisturbed by the agitation that accompanies them. Indeed, a cost attaches to every object we obtain or accept throughout life; while aspirations remain truly valuable to possess, their acquisition comes at a high cost, demanding their required payments of effort, abstaining from pleasure, worry, and disheartenment. Colorless and silent, Nell realized that within another ten minutes' time, the identity of the medal recipient as well as the Avery winner would be revealed to her. Past those coming ten minutes, there appeared to be no duration, right at that moment, deserving of the name Time.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Naturally, you will secure one among them regardless,” remarked Odette, who failed to comprehend how the faculty could possess such bias as to mandate a different outcome.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “I don’t hold out any hope for the Avery,” Nell remarked. “The general opinion is that Emily Clay is going to be the winner. There’s no way I’m walking right up to that bulletin board to check it in front of the whole crowd. My moral courage isn’t up to it. My plan is to head directly to the girls’ dressing room. Odette, you have to look at the announcements and bring the news to me afterwards. For the sake of our longstanding friendship, I beg you to make it as fast as you can. Should I have lost, simply state it plain, rather than attempting to soften the blow; and under no circumstances offer me sympathy. Give me your word on this, Odette.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Odette made a solemn pledge; nevertheless, as things turned out, no such vow was needed. Upon ascending the front steps at Regent’s, the hall met their eyes filled with schoolboys hoisting Hugh Carrow onto their shoulders while shouting with all their might, “Hurrah for Carrow, Medalist!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Nell experienced a single nauseating wave of failure and letdown briefly. Thus, she had lost while Hugh had triumphed! Ah, Obed would feel regret—he possessed such certainty regarding her victory.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: And then!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: A person shouted:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Hip, hip, hooray for Miss Harcourt, who has taken the Avery!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Oh, Nell,” Odette panted, while enthusiastic applause accompanied them on their flight toward the dressing room for girls. “Oh, Nell I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: And after that, the girls surrounded them, making Nell the middle of a merry, well-wishing crowd. Her hands were gripped firmly, and her shoulders were slapped. She was yanked, jostled, and embraced, yet amidst the commotion, she succeeded in murmuring to Odette:

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Oh, Obed and Thirza are going to be so happy! I have to send a letter with the news to my family immediately.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: The following significant event was commencement. In the large assembly hall of the Academy, the ceremonies took place. Speeches were delivered, compositions recited, vocal pieces performed, and the public presentation of diplomas, honors, and medals occurred.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Obed and Thirza stood present, their sight and hearing consumed by a single scholar upon the stage—a towering young woman dressed in soft green, whose face bore a gentle blush and whose eyes shone like stars, who delivered the finest paper and whom others indicated and spoke of in hushed tones as the Avery victor.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Guess you're pleased we retained her, Thirza?” murmured Obed, breaking his silence for the first time since coming into the room, after Nell had concluded her composition.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “I’ve felt relieved on previous occasions as well,” Thirza fired back. “You certainly enjoy dwelling on things, Obed Abernethy.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Positioned in the seat behind the pair, Miss Pembroke bent towards them and jabbed Thirza’s back using her parasol.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Does that Nell-girl not make you proud? She makes me proud,” she stated.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Nell returned to Brierley alongside Obed and Thirza during that evening. Having been away from home since April, she felt an urgency that prevented her from waiting even one more day. The blossoms on the apple trees had bloomed, making the world appear young and fresh. Isolde was present at Grey Shutters so that she could meet her. Within her private white room, in which a flowering house rose had been placed on the window sill by Thirza, Nell surveyed her surroundings and inhaled a deep, joyful breath.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Oh, Isolde, returning here feels so wonderful. Watching those pointed firs silhouetted against the pink sky is truly wonderful—along with that white orchard and the old Frost Maiden. Doesn't the mint smell delightful? As for that tea rose—well, it combines a song, a hope, and a prayer into a single thing. And seeing you once more is so good, Isolde!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “It was my impression that Mabel Colby was more to your liking than I was,” Isolde uttered with a tone of reproach. “I was informed by Flossie Tulk that this was so. According to Flossie, you were completely taken with her.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Laughter escaping her, Nell threw the wilted "June lilies" from her bouquet at Isolde.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Other than a single person, Mabel Colby is the most precious girl in existence, and that one person is you, Isolde,” she stated. “My love for you is greater than it has ever been—and I have a great deal to share with you. However, at this moment, simply sitting in this spot and gazing at you seems like sufficient happiness. It occurs to me that I am weary—weary of my scholarly pursuits and aspirations. Tomorrow, I intend to devote a minimum of two hours to reclining on the grass in the orchard, allowing my mind to remain entirely blank.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “You have performed wonderfully, Nell. I imagine you will not continue teaching now that the Avery has been awarded to you?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “No. I am headed to Wexcombe come September. Does it not sound marvelous? After three splendid, sunlit months off, I will possess a fresh store of drive by then. Odette and Opal intend to teach. Is it not fantastic to consider that every one of us passed, even extending to Elias Purdy and Flossie Tulk?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Odette has already been offered their school by the Stonebridge trustees,” Isolde said. “Furthermore, Hugh Carrow will be teaching. It is necessary for him. After all, his father is unable to pay for him to attend college next year, which means he intends to cover his own expenses. Should Miss Ames choose to depart, I anticipate he will secure the school here.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: A strange, subtle feeling of startled disappointment came over Nell. This was news to her; her assumption had been that Hugh's destination was likewise Wexcombe. How would she manage in the absence of their motivating competition? Wouldn't studying—even inside a coeducational institution offering the possibility of an actual degree—feel somewhat dull if her friendly foe was missing?

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: While eating breakfast the following morning, it occurred to Nell all at once that Obed appeared unwell. Without a doubt, his hair had turned far grayer than it was twelve months prior.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Thirza,” she asked with hesitation once he had left, “is Obed quite well?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “No, he isn’t,” Thirza answered anxiously. “His heart has given him a lot of trouble this spring and he refuses to take things easy. He’s caused me a great deal of worry, though he has improved a bit lately and our hired man is reliable, so my hope is that he will take a break and regain his strength. Having you back might help him do that. You have always lifted his spirits.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Reaching over the table, Nell cupped Thirza’s face with her hands.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Thirza, your own appearance is not as healthy as I would prefer, either. Fatigue shows on your face. It worries me that your labor has been excessive. Now that my return has occurred, resting is imperative for you. My intention is merely to spend this single day away from work, visiting every beloved familiar location and searching for the dreams of my past, after which you shall have the opportunity to relax while the labor becomes my responsibility.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Thirza gave her daughter a loving smile.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “It isn’t the labor—it’s my head. Frequently now, I suffer from an ache—behind my eyes. Glasses have been tried on me by Doctor Tranter, yet they fail to help me. At the end of June, a prominent oculist is visiting the Island, and the doctor insists that I consult him. I suppose it will be necessary. Reading or sewing cannot be done comfortably by me anymore. Well, Nell, it must be said that you performed truly well at Regent’s. Taking a First Class License within a single year alongside winning the Avery scholarship—well, well, pride goes before a fall according to Mrs. Sowerby, who disbelieves in women’s higher education entirely; she claims that it renders them unfit for the true sphere of a woman. Not one word of that is believed by me. Mentioning Agatha brings it to my mind—have any updates concerning the Abbey Bank reached you recently, Nell?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “I was told it was unstable,” Nell replied. “For what reason?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Agatha stated that very thing. Having come up here on a day during the previous week, she mentioned that people were discussing it. Obed became genuinely anxious. Everything we have put away—to the last cent—is held in that bank. Originally, my desire was for Obed to deposit it into the Savings Bank, yet old Mr. Abbey had been a close friend of father’s, and father had constantly done his banking through him. Obed declared that whatever bank had him as its leader was sufficiently reliable for anyone.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “In my opinion, he has merely been its leader in name for a long time,” Nell said. “Being an exceptionally aged man, the institution is actually run by his nephews.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: “Indeed, once Agatha mentioned that to us, my desire was for Obed to withdraw our funds immediately, a course of action he promised to consider. However, yesterday Mr. Russell assured him that the bank’s condition was secure.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
text: Nell experienced her favorable day amid the company of nature.
